The current `data/normalized_yaml/algae/bb.yaml` (`CultureMech:000053`) retains `MoO` at `ingredients/2`, with `0.71 G_PER_L` at the medium root. The original CCAP recipe instead gives **MoO3, 0.71 g per litre of trace-element stock 7**, followed by **1 mL of stock 7 per litre of medium**.

Primary evidence: [CCAP Bold's Basal Medium PDF](https://www.ccap.ac.uk/wp-content/uploads/MR_BB.pdf), page 1, stock 7 table and final medium table. The captured PDF SHA256 is `2e9f5cfb8ab4df8e0db0ca08a274d2652abada40d075ed68a74478608ca7367a`. Current GitHub main file bytes, checked 2026-11-08 UTC, match the frozen source SHA256 `746699aed1ad8d8078dd48d8d5fd4186ca99fc91cc9d2761ee01fe5ff598dc69`.

This is a residual source transcription and stock hierarchy defect. Closed #276/#282 repaired other subscript losses; this file's history records a correction of `Co(NO ) .6H O`, while `MoO` remains. Closed #118 describes the broader stock concentration problem. Open #408 covers related unit ingestion. None of the reviewed issue bodies or #276 comments identifies this exact residual MoO occurrence.

Proposed follow-up:

- Reconstruct the BB stock and addition hierarchy from the primary recipe, including the other trace components now placed at the root.
- Restore this source token to MoO3 with primary-source provenance; establish its MIM identity through the normal guarded review.
- Keep 0.71 g/L as the stock composition. Where a final-medium concentration is represented, derive it transparently from the documented 1 mL/L addition (0.00071 g/L), without confusing the two stages.
- Preserve the original token in history and prevent a global `MoO` alias from hiding the parser defect. Validate against duplicate ingredients and missing stock constituents.

Found in authorized all-unmatched worker09 review, frozen case `CM_NAME:75d52d9f7d5b45ad6946c61474cb1f4c0e640d76c41680ab8fc544b6ca555b43`, occurrence `CM_OCC:fb0182bd4a6f07cc7f5618a1892150ebcc0c8c7867435ad8ab1c537b408636cf`. This issue does not claim other shards or authorize an MIM export release. No maintained source was changed by the review.

`CultureMech:000143` (`data/normalized_yaml/algae/waris_h.yaml`) still has two ingredient rows named `Dissolve`, with 1.04 and 2.74 G_PER_L. This is a residual source-recovery problem after #273, whose advice to recover the substance and quantity rather than merely delete an instruction remains applicable.

The [CCAP Waris-H primary recipe](https://www.ccap.ac.uk/wp-content/uploads/MR_Waris_H.pdf), pages 1–2, identifies those values as KOH 1.04 g and FeSO4·7H2O 2.74 g in the 100 mL Fe-EDTA stock. It also lists Na2EDTA·2H2O 4.08 g. The final medium takes 0.1 mL of that stock per litre. The current record already has separate KOH and FeSO4·7H2O ingredient rows with the same unscaled values, so blindly replacing each `Dissolve` row would duplicate the substances. Removing only the two words would also leave the stock/medium scaling error.

Verified on remote main `199cd9191881e8e929cd95ea0ed13aabe388e58c`, file SHA256 `6b84f51622f463c72b01063a0da7ffa457db8a996ee118263eddbf8fb1ddee46`. MIM must not mint a chemical or resolving synonym named Dissolve.

Recover this recipe against the primary source as a whole: represent Fe-EDTA stock separately with its ingredients and addition volume, reconcile the existing duplicated/mis-scaled material rows, and retain raw instruction text and quantities as provenance. Check the remaining stock stages before claiming the whole medium is corrected. Add a regression for this exact short instruction token and the two-stage quantities. **What:** `src/culturemech/render_media_pages.py:258` (at `199cd9191881`, equal to `origin/main` on 2026-11-06) links TaxonMech as `https://culturebotai.github.io/TaxonMech/#q=<label>`. The site root is a meta-refresh redirect to `pages/index.html`, the landing page, not the browse page; whether the `#q=` fragment survives the redirect and is applied was not checked in a browser, but the browse page reads its query from `?q=`, not from the fragment.

Checked with HTTP HEAD requests on 2026-11-06: `https://culturebotai.github.io/TaxonMech/browse.html` returns 404, `https://culturebotai.github.io/TaxonMech/taxa/NCBITaxon_562.html` returns 404, while `https://culturebotai.github.io/TaxonMech/pages/browse.html` and `https://culturebotai.github.io/TaxonMech/pages/taxon.html?id=NCBITaxon:562` return 200. TaxonMech publishes only `index.html` (a redirect to `pages/index.html`) and `pages/`; its browse index lists `pages/taxon.html?id=NCBITaxon:<n>` as the page of every one of its 626,048 records.

**Fix:** when the record carries the NCBITaxon id, link the record page `https://culturebotai.github.io/TaxonMech/pages/taxon.html?id=NCBITaxon:<n>`; a search by label belongs at `https://culturebotai.github.io/TaxonMech/pages/browse.html?q=<label>`. CultureBotAI/culturebotai-claw#655 proposes declaring each site's routes in the fleet manifest so a renderer cannot drift from them again, and an offline test that every emitted sibling URL starts with a declared route. Found by the assessment in CultureBotAI/culturebotai-claw#881.

**Addendum (2026-11-06):** an independent review of the assessment found two more facts. `app/browser.html:771` also emits `https://culturebotai.github.io/TaxonMech/browse.html?q=`, without the `pages/` prefix, so the browser's handoff is dead for the same reason as the other Mechs'. And TaxonMech's `pages/index.html`, where the root redirect lands, loads only `theme-toggle.js` and reads no URL fragment; its search form submits to `browse.html` with `?q=`, so the `#q=` from `render_media_pages.py:258` performs no search.
title: The TaxonMech handoff on record pages returns 404 on the published site

**Correction (2026-11-06, same day):** not a defect. The single occurrence is curator prose in `data/merge_yaml/merged/sulfolobus_medium_for_dsm_9790.yaml` (lines 299-302) that explains the synonymy itself: "the former strain id NCBITaxon:263820 ('Picrophilus torridus DSM 9790') is now an alternative id of NCBITaxon:1122961". The assessment's text scan counted every CURIE in a file, prose included; the slot-declared check that replaces it (`kg-microbe-links taxa`, claw PR in progress) finds no retired id in any CultureMech taxon slot. Closing as not planned; the original text follows for the record.

---

**What:** records cite NCBI taxon ids that NCBI has since merged into other ids. Against the NCBI taxdump snapshot TaxonMech pins (2026-09-13), each id below is retired; the id it merged into is a TaxonMech record. 

Measured at CultureMech `199cd9191881` (equal to `origin/main` on 2026-11-06). Sample records are the first three found; the count is every record citing the id.


| cited id | name | status | records citing | sample records |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| NCBITaxon:263820 | Picrophilus oshimae DSM 9789 | merged into NCBITaxon:1122961 | 1 | `data/merge_yaml/merged/sulfolobus_medium_for_dsm_9790.yaml` |

**Why it matters:** a retired id resolves nowhere in TaxonMech, whose scope holds current ids, and any consumer that joins on `NCBITaxon` misses the record. TaxonMech carries the merge table (`data/raw/ncbi_merged_ids.tsv`, 101,006 rows); nothing in this repository reads it. claw is adding a `kg-microbe-links taxa` check that reports these per Mech.

**Fix:** replace each cited id with its current id, keeping the original where the record's provenance needs it (notes or curation history). For an id absent from the taxdump, recover the intended taxon from the record's source.

Measured by the cross-Mech taxon-link assessment in CultureBotAI/culturebotai-claw#881 (report: `docs/reviews/2026-11-06-cross-mech-taxon-links.md`; the per-Mech table comes from its `scripts/adhoc/report_taxon_data_fixes_by_mech.py`). Re-check after the fix with `scripts/adhoc/measure_all_taxon_curies_in_taxonmech.py` followed by `scripts/adhoc/classify_taxa_outside_taxonmech_scope.py` from that PR.

body:
## What

CultureMech is adopting claw's shared quote gate (CultureBotAI/culturebotai-claw#729). The adoption PR commits the PubMed abstract each quote cites under `evidence_cache/` and runs `qc-evidence` in CI. Measured on 2026-11-04 against `main` at `a74dd48972`, 51 of 91 quote-bearing evidence items occur verbatim in their cited abstract. These 40 do not:

| Finding | Items | What it usually means |
|---|---:|---|
| `SNIPPET_NOT_IN_SOURCE`: not in the cited abstract | 33 | Usually quoted from the full text, or paraphrased. |
| `MISSING_CACHE`: no PubMed abstract | 7 | The PMID has no abstract, or the DOI has no single PubMed record that lists it. |

They sit in 9 records under `data/merge_yaml/merged/`, most in `caldicellulosiruptor_medium_for_dsm_10319.yaml` (11), `chopped_meat_medium_atcc_1490_with_formate_and_fumarate_atcc_9733.yaml` (9), `bacto_marine_broth_difco_2216_for_dsm_11879.yaml` (7), `ignicoccus_medium_for_dsm_18386.yaml` (4).

The adoption PR records all 40 in `curation/evidence_known_findings.tsv`, each naming this issue. They are reported, counted apart and never shown as validated, but they do not block. Every new or edited quote is checked from adoption onward.

## How to repair one

- Replace the quote with the sentence from the cited abstract that supports the claim, copied verbatim.
- Or cite a source whose abstract carries the support, and add its cache with `kg-microbe-evidence-fetch`.
- If the support exists only in the full text, remove the `snippet` and keep the citation and explanation. It then reports as `NO_QUOTE`: not validated, but not misrepresented.

Never change the scientific claim to satisfy the gate, and never trim a quote to a fragment that matches but no longer supports the claim. A match proves the quote occurs in the source, not that the source supports the claim.

After repairs, drop the repaired entries. A repaired entry left in the ledger is stale and fails the gate. From a claw checkout:

```bash
uv run kg-microbe-evidence --mech culturemech --root <worktree> --record-known-findings --apply
```
title: Repair 40 evidence quotes the shared quote gate cannot validate

Found during decision support for MediaIngredientMech #1004 (carnitine hydrochloride identity).

**What happens:** the NLDM "Carnitine Hydrochloride" ingredient is grounded to `CHEBI:91318`, **(R)-oleoylcarnitine hydrochloride**, a long-chain acylcarnitine. But its own notes say `CAS: 461-05-2; MW: 197.66; From NLDM_metabolites`. That CAS and MW are DL-carnitine hydrochloride (PubChem CID 5970, C7H16ClNO3, 197.66; NCIT:C216679 "DL-Carnitine Hydrochloride"). The mapping came from `ols_exact (confidence: 0.92)`.

**Where:** 22 files reference `CHEBI:91318`, including `data/merge_yaml/merged/NLDM_defined.yaml` (around line 785), `NLDM_defined_pH5.yaml`, `NLDM_defined_pH8.yaml`, `NLDM_defined_no_P.yaml`, and `src/culturemech/data/chebi/structure_index.csv`. Checked with `gh search code`, so generated or ignored copies may not be included.

**Suggested fix:** reground the NLDM carnitine hydrochloride ingredient using its CAS 461-05-2 to the carnitine hydrochloride identity MediaIngredientMech settles in #1004. Until then, use carnitine (CHEBI:17126) as the parent, not an acylcarnitine. Then add a guard against OLS label matches that contradict the recorded CAS or MW.
title: NLDM Carnitine Hydrochloride is grounded to CHEBI:91318 ((R)-oleoylcarnitine hydrochloride) despite CAS 461-05-2

  - Declares 31 prefixes (`linkml`, `culturemech`, `biolink`, `rdfs`, `CHEBI`, `NCBITaxon`, `DSMZ`, `TOGO`, `ATCC`, `NCIT`, `UTEX`, `CCAP`, `SAG`, `OBI`, `ENVO`, `UO`, `UBERON`, `FOODON`, `mediadive.compound`, `PMID`, `DOI`, `KEGG`, `EC`, `geo`, `sra`, `GTDB`, `RefSeq`, `GenBank`, `BioSample`, `sigma`, `thermofisher`). **No `UniProt` or `UniProtKB` prefix or `UniProtTerm` class exists.**
  - `CofactorDescriptor` (lines 1234–1296) defines `enzyme_examples` (`range: string`, `multivalued: true`), `biosynthesis_genes` (`range: string`, `multivalued: true`), and `ec_associations` (`range: string`, `multivalued: true` with EC pattern).
  - `CofactorRequirement` (lines 2000–2028) defines `genes` (`range: string`, `multivalued: true`).
  - `TransporterAnnotation` (lines 2029–2072) defines `name` (`range: string`), `genes` (`range: string`, `multivalued: true`), `ec_number` (`range: string`), and `evidence` (`EvidenceItem`).
  - `StrainModification` (lines 1565–1602) defines `target` (`range: string`, description `"Gene, operon, or pathway modified"`).
- **Corpus & reference data audit (`15,915` normalized records + `data/reference/cofactors.yaml`)**:
  - Across all `15,915` normalized YAML records in `data/normalized_yaml/`, `cofactors_provided`, `cofactor_requirements`, `transporters`, `enzyme_examples`, `biosynthesis_genes`, and `ec_associations` have **`0` populated instances**; `strain_modifications` is populated in `2` records (`archaea/pyrococcus_medium.yaml` with `target: cellulose utilization`, `bacterial/magnetospirillum_gryphiswaldense_medium.yaml` with `target: mamAB operon`) using free-text strings.
  - `data/reference/cofactors.yaml` (56 entries across 8 categories generated by `src/culturemech/import/import_cofactors.py`) uses `enzyme_examples` only for generic free-text enzyme family labels (e.g., `"pyruvate dehydrogenase"`, `"methanol dehydrogenase (XoxF-MDH)"`), with `0` UniProt accessions, `0` organism (`NCBITaxon`) bindings, `0` claim-level `EvidenceItem` records, and unvalidated ChEBI mappings (including duplicate `CHEBI:60052` across `heme_c` (`heme C`) and `heme_d1` (`heme d1`)).
  - `docs/ENRICHMENT_GUIDE.md` references `normalized_yaml/bacterial/Nitrate_Mineral_Salts_Medium_(NMS)_ENRICHED_EXAMPLE.yaml`, which does not exist in the repository.
- **Validation & Exporter Gaps**:
  - `conf/oak_config.yaml` and `conf/id_label_targets.yaml` have no `UniProtKB` adapter or prefix rule; adding `UniProtKB:` IDs into `(id, label)` validated targets without adapter configuration would fail `scripts/validate_id_label.py` with `UNKNOWN_PREFIX`.
  - `src/culturemech/export/kgx_export.py` (lines 468–833) does not emit protein nodes (`biolink:Protein`) or medium/cofactor/transporter-to-protein edges.

## Missing Prerequisites to Unblock Stage 3 (`protein_examples`)

1. **LinkML Schema Support (`src/culturemech/schema/culturemech.yaml`)**:
   - Add prefix `UniProtKB: https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/` to `prefixes:`.
   - Define `UniProtTerm` (`id` required with pattern `^UniProtKB:([OPQ][0-9][A-Z0-9]{3}[0-9]|[A-NR-Z][0-9]([A-Z][A-Z0-9]{2}[0-9]){1,2})(-\d+)?$`, `label` required for canonical protein name) and `ProteinExample` (or typed `protein_examples` slot on `CofactorDescriptor`, `TransporterAnnotation`, and/or `OrganismDescriptor`) that binds:
     - `uniprot_term` (`UniProtTerm`),
     - explicit `organism_term` (`NCBITaxonTerm` so every UniProt accession is tied to the exact strain/taxon in the medium),
     - optional `gene_symbol`, `ec_number`, and `role_in_medium` (e.g., cofactor-dependent enzyme, uptake transporter),
     - mandatory claim-scoped `evidence` (`EvidenceItem` with `reference` `PMID:`/`DOI:`/`gomodel:`, `supports`, and verbatim `snippet`).
2. **Validation & ID-Label Correspondence (`conf/id_label_targets.yaml`, `conf/oak_config.yaml`, `scripts/validate_strict.py`)**:
   - Configure `UniProtTerm` validation rules (syntax + accession/taxon/label verification or explicit `id_label_targets.yaml` handling) and `scripts/validate_strict.py` checks ensuring every `ProteinExample` carries a verified `UniProtKB:` ID, matching `NCBITaxon:` organism, and non-empty `EvidenceItem`.
   - Remediate or isolate `data/reference/cofactors.yaml` ChEBI label drift (`CHEBI:60052` collision) before importing cofactor protein examples into `data/normalized_yaml/`.
3. **Maintained Writer & KGX Exporter (`scripts/`, `src/culturemech/export/kgx_export.py`)**:
   - Implement a schema-validating writer that updates `data/normalized_yaml/` and appends `curation_history`, plus `kgx_export.py` emission of `biolink:Protein` nodes and typed edges without mutating generated outputs (`data/merge_yaml/merged/`, `app/`, `pages/`, `output/`) directly.
4. **Repository-Local Skill & Profile Unblocking (`.claude/skills/`, `workflow/mech-workflow.yaml`)**:
   - Create a `.claude/skills/` skill for curating evidence-backed UniProt protein examples on media cofactors/transporters, add `tests/` coverage, and update `workflow/mech-workflow.yaml` Stage 3 `skill_paths` and `applicability` for the next cycle reload.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `UniProtKB` prefix, `UniProtTerm`, and `ProteinExample` classes validate cleanly under `scripts/audit_schema.py` and `scripts/validate_strict.py`.
- Maintained writer, KGX exporter, validator config, unit tests, and `.claude/skills/` skill are in place before Stage 3 (`protein_examples`) is marked `applicable` in `workflow/mech-workflow.yaml`.
title: infra(stage-3): define UniProtKB prefix, typed ProteinExample schema, OAK validation, writer, and skill prerequisites

## Summary

Cycle 2 Stage 2 (`causal_graphs`) in `workflow/mech-workflow.yaml` (and pinned in `/Users/marcin/Documents/VIMSS/ontology/KG-Hub/KG-Microbe/culturebotai-claw/workspace/session-orchestration/20261019/culturemech/effective-workflow.json`) is currently marked `applicability: blocked` with `skill_paths: []` and reason:

> CultureMech models growth-media compositions and preparation protocols rather than causal mechanism graphs; no native causal-graph schema slot or curation skill is defined.

A repository-wide prerequisite audit (`audit-schema-gaps` + `culturemech-evolve-workflow`, including hidden and git-ignored paths) at commit `231e0ba71b41d45362168d539efebe7991823464` verified what CultureMech can currently represent versus what is required for evidence-backed causal mechanism graphs.

## Current Native Capabilities (Composition & Role Facets Only)

- **Native schema (`src/culturemech/schema/culturemech.yaml`, `src/culturemech/schema/mim_roles.yaml`)**:
  - `IngredientDescriptor` (lines 865–1193) supports composition amounts (`concentration`), ChEBI/MediaIngredientMech term references (`chebi_term`, `mediaingredientmech_term`), three role facet enums (`nutritional_roles` (`NutritionalRoleEnum`), `physicochemical_roles` (`PhysicochemicalRoleEnum`), `cellular_metabolic_roles` (`CellularMetabolicRoleEnum`)), and `cofactors_provided` (`CofactorDescriptor`).
  - `OrganismDescriptor` (lines 1344–1564) supports `growth_metrics` (`GrowthMetrics`, with `nutrient_overrides` (`NutrientOverride`: `role`, `source`, `is_sole_source`, `notes`)), `perturbations` (`Perturbation` with `modification_type`, `description`, `growth_outcome`, `effect_description`, `evidence`), and `strain_modifications` (`StrainModification` with `modification_type`, `target`, `description`, `ontology_id`, `evidence`).
  - Corpus population across all `15,915` normalized YAML records in `data/normalized_yaml/`: `nutritional_roles` (`217`), `physicochemical_roles` (`249`), `cellular_metabolic_roles` (`5`), `perturbations` (`3`), `strain_modifications` (`2`), `nutrient_overrides` (`2`), `cofactors_provided` (`0`).
- **Maintained writers & exporters**:
  - `scripts/render_media_role_graph.py` (`.claude/skills/render-media-role-graph/SKILL.md`) renders bipartite Mermaid composition/role diagrams (`MediaRecipe` -> `IngredientDescriptor` -> role facet enum values + `OrganismDescriptor` `community_role` / `nutrient_overrides`), not directed causal mechanism chains.
  - `src/culturemech/export/kgx_export.py` (lines 468–833) defines 12 `*_to_edge` functions emitting 7 predicates (`METPO:2000517` organism-to-medium, `biolink:has_part` medium-to-solution/ingredient/role, `biolink:has_attribute` medium-to-type/state/pH, `biolink:related_to` cofactor hierarchies, `biolink:same_as`, `biolink:subclass_of`, and `biolink:has_dataset`), with `0` causal predicate edges (`biolink:causes`, `biolink:affects`, `biolink:regulates`, etc.).
  - `scripts/repair_top_causal_graph_score15.py` only curates media composition, stock solutions, role enums, pH, preparation steps, and sterilization; its filename is a historical misnomer that appears in `curation_history.curator` of 4 bacterial records (`my20_agar.yaml`, `my75s.yaml`, `mycoplasma_medium_atcc_243_with_sucrose.yaml`, `na_0_5_yeast_extract.yaml`).
  - `src/culturemech/schema/mech_shared.yaml` mentions `causal_graphs#edge_x` only in the shared `Discussion.attaches_to` docstring inherited across Mech repositories; `MediaRecipe` has no `causal_graphs` or `mechanism_graph` slot.

## Missing Prerequisites to Unblock Stage 2 (`causal_graphs`) (or Reclassify Scope)

1. **Domain & Architecture Decision (`culturemech-infra-0002` Step 1)**:
   - Confirm with parent KG-Microbe / Mech architecture whether growth-media records in CultureMech should natively represent directed causal mechanism edges (e.g., ingredient/perturbation -> transporter/cofactor/metabolic process -> organism growth phenotype) **or** whether `causal_graphs` should be formally classified in `workflow/parent/mech-cycle.yaml` / `workflow/mech-workflow.yaml` as `not_applicable` for composition-centric repositories.
2. **LinkML Schema Extension (`src/culturemech/schema/culturemech.yaml`)** *(if native Stage 2 is adopted)*:
   - Define a typed `CausalEdge` / `MechanismEdge` class with explicit `id`, typed `subject` (ingredient, cofactor, perturbation, or solution term), constrained causal `predicate` (`biolink:` / `RO:` causal relation enum), typed `object` (metabolic process `GO:`, cofactor `CHEBI:`, transporter/protein target, or growth phenotype), optional `organism_context` (`NCBITaxon:`), experimental condition scope, and mandatory claim-scoped `evidence` (`EvidenceItem` with `reference` `PMID:`/`DOI:`/`gomodel:`, `supports`, and verbatim `snippet`).
   - Attach multivalued slot `causal_graphs` (or `causal_edges`) to `MediaRecipe` without altering existing composition/role slots.
3. **Validation & OAK Target Configuration (`conf/id_label_targets.yaml`, `scripts/validate_strict.py`, `scripts/validate_id_label.py`)**:
   - Register any new ontology-grounded subject/object `(id, label)` pairs in `conf/id_label_targets.yaml` and enforce `EvidenceItem` completeness (`reference` + `snippet` + `supports`) in `scripts/validate_strict.py`.
4. **Maintained Writer & KGX Exporter (`scripts/`, `src/culturemech/export/kgx_export.py`)**:
   - Provide a schema-validating writer that updates `data/normalized_yaml/` and appends `curation_history` (`audit_writers.py` compliant), preserves generated-output ownership (`data/merge_yaml/merged/`, `app/`, `pages/`, `output/`), and exports verified causal edges in `src/culturemech/export/kgx_export.py` with unit tests.
5. **Repository-Local Skill & Profile Unblocking (`.claude/skills/`, `workflow/mech-workflow.yaml`)**:
   - Add a repository-local `.claude/skills/` skill for evidence-backed causal mechanism curation with explicit negative controls against fabricating edges from generic ingredient roles, add `tests/` coverage, and update `workflow/mech-workflow.yaml` Stage 2 `skill_paths` and `applicability` for the next cycle reload.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Either (A) native `CausalEdge` schema class, validator targets, maintained writer, KGX exporter, `.claude/skills/` curation skill, and unit tests are implemented and pass `scripts/validate_strict.py`, `scripts/audit_schema.py`, `scripts/audit_writers.py`, and `pytest`, **or** (B) parent coordinator policy explicitly reclassifies Stage 2 for CultureMech composition records without fabricating scientific fields.
- Authoritative inputs remain strictly in `data/normalized_yaml/`; no unverified causal edges are invented from role enums.
title: infra(stage-2): define native causal_graphs schema, writer, validator, KGX export, and skill prerequisites

## Summary

Structured record and category reviews (`reviews/structured/20261017T085038Z-review-yaml-record-thermovenabulum-medium-merged` and `reviews/structured/20261017T090039Z-review-yaml-category-thermovenabulum-family`, PR #632) identified four defects across the `THERMOVENABULUM_MEDIUM` family (`CultureMech:002143`, `CultureMech:000714`, `CultureMech:004016`, `CultureMech:006919`):

1. **Three chemically distinct DSMZ formulations share `name: thermovenabulum_medium`**:
   - **Group A — DSMZ Medium 962a** (`data/normalized_yaml/bacterial/DSMZ_962a_THERMOVENABULUM_MEDIUM.yaml` [`CultureMech:000714`] and `data/merge_yaml/merged/THERMOVENABULUM_MEDIUM.yaml` [`CultureMech:002143`]): Disodium fumarate (`1.6 G_PER_L`) + Meat extract (`0.5 G_PER_L`) + Yeast extract (`0.5 G_PER_L`).
   - **Group B — DSMZ Medium 1255** (`data/normalized_yaml/bacterial/KOMODO_1255_THERMOVENABULUM_medium.yaml` [`CultureMech:004016`], `data/normalized_yaml/bacterial/THERMOVENABULUM_medium.yaml` [`CultureMech:006919`], and `data/merge_yaml/recipe_batches/batch_082.yaml` index 18): D-Glucose (`3.6032 G_PER_L`) + Tryptone (`1.0 G_PER_L`) + PIPES (`3.0237 G_PER_L`) + `Na2S x 9 H2O` (`0.24018 G_PER_L`).
   - **Group C — DSMZ Medium 962** (`data/merge_yaml/recipe_batches/batch_039.yaml` index 14): 9,10-anthraquinone-2,6-disulfonic acid disodium salt (`8.24 G_PER_L`) + Na-acetate (`0.82 G_PER_L`).

2. **100x–1000x unscaled stock concentrations flattened into per-liter medium ingredients**:
   - All 6 records inline Wolin's trace element (`10 ml/L`, 100x stock) and Wolin's vitamin (`10 ml/L`, 100x stock, or `1 ml/L`, 1000x stock) solutions at unscaled 1 L stock concentrations (e.g., `MgSO4 x 7 H2O` at `3.0 G_PER_L` instead of `0.03 G_PER_L`; `Nitrilotriacetic acid` at `1.5 G_PER_L` instead of `0.015 G_PER_L`; `Pyridoxine hydrochloride` at `0.01 G_PER_L` instead of `0.0001 G_PER_L`).

3. **Duplicate `CaCl2 x 2 H2O` summed across basal medium and unscaled trace stock**:
   - In `data/merge_yaml/merged/THERMOVENABULUM_MEDIUM.yaml` (`CultureMech:002143`), `ingredients[3]` (`CaCl2 x 2 H2O`, `0.42640900000000004 G_PER_L`) sums the basal `0.33 G_PER_L` with an unscaled `0.096409 G_PER_L` stock entry, while `ingredients[14]` retains another `0.1 G_PER_L` `CaCl2 x 2 H2O` entry.

4. **Undeclared `merge_fingerprint` and `merged_from` slots in `data/merge_yaml/merged/THERMOVENABULUM_MEDIUM.yaml`**:
   - `scripts/merge_recipes.py` emits `merge_fingerprint` and `merged_from` on merged `MediaRecipe` records without declaring them in `src/culturemech/schema/culturemech.yaml`, causing `linkml-validate` to fail.
title: THERMOVENABULUM_MEDIUM family: 3 distinct DSMZ formulations share name, 100x-1000x unscaled stocks, and undeclared merge slots

## Summary

Adversarial review of `scripts/batch_review_recipes.py` during the 4-skill structured review (`reviews/structured/20261017T090539Z-review-recipes-and-categories-corpus-audit`, PR #632) uncovered three validation blind spots in `RecipeValidator`:

1. **`_validate_solution()` omits `P3.1` placeholder detection**:
   - `validate_recipe()` delegates `SolutionDescriptor` / `SolutionRecipe` files to `self._validate_solution(recipe, recipe_path)` at line 209 before reaching the `P3.1` placeholder check at line 286.
   - As a result, solution records containing placeholder ingredients or notes — such as `CultureMech:011215` (`data/normalized_yaml/solutions/mediadive_2054_Main_sol_1015.yaml`, which has a single composition entry `preferred_term: See source for composition`, `notes: Full composition available at source database`) — receive `0` `P3.1` findings.

2. **`check_placeholders()` ignores ingredient `preferred_term`**:
   - In `validate_recipe()`, `P3.1` only checks `recipe.get("notes", "")` and `ing.get("notes", "")`, not `ing.get("preferred_term", "")`.
   - Placeholder ingredients whose `preferred_term` is `"See source for composition"` while `notes` is `"Full composition available at source database"` (e.g., `CultureMech:000252` in `data/normalized_yaml/archaea/DSMZ_1399_HALOPHILIC_MEDIUM.yaml` and `CultureMech:011215` in `data/normalized_yaml/solutions/mediadive_2054_Main_sol_1015.yaml`) evade `P3.1` unless `preferred_term` is also checked.

3. **`_validate_solution()` ignores `chebi_term` grounding and null lists**:
   - Solution composition entries in `data/normalized_yaml/solutions/` and `SolutionRecipe` records frequently carry `chebi_term` (`{"id": "CHEBI:..."}`) alongside or instead of `mediaingredientmech_chebi_term`, and `composition: null` / `ingredients: null` can raise `TypeError` if not coerced to `[]`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Check `P3.1` placeholder patterns across `notes` and ingredient/composition `preferred_term` and `notes` in both `validate_recipe()` and `_validate_solution()`.
- [ ] Count `chebi_term` fallback in solution ingredient linkage (`_validate_solution()`) and safely handle `None` lists for `ingredients` / `composition`.
- [ ] Add regression tests in `tests/test_batch_review_recipes.py`.
title: batch_review_recipes.py: _validate_solution() omits P3.1 placeholder checks and ignores chebi_term / preferred_term placeholders

Found while re-checking #387 before closing it. #409 (`2e4566eaad`) strips invisible characters from TOGO component names, using `clean_component_name` in `src/culturemech/import/togo_importer.py`. No other importer does this, and U+00AD SOFT HYPHEN is still in the corpus.

A YAML walk of `data/normalized_yaml` on `main` at `41d4d39` finds 69 string values containing U+00AD. It finds none of the other characters that `_INVISIBLE` strips (U+200B, U+200C, U+200D, U+2060 and U+FEFF).

## Record names: 6 records, 12 fields

Each record below has U+00AD in both `preferred_term` and `term.label`:

| record (`data/normalized_yaml/bacterial/`) | id | source id |
|---|---|---|
| `mediadive_6188_3N_BBM_V_Bold_Basal_Medium_with_3_fold_Nitrogen_and_Vitamins_modified.yaml` | CultureMech:014887 | mediadive.solution:6188 |
| `mediadive_6197_MY75S_Malt_Yeast_Extract_75_Seawater_Agar.yaml` | CultureMech:014894 | mediadive.solution:6197 |
| `mediadive_6207_NCL_New_Cereal_Leaf-_Prescott_Liquid.yaml` | CultureMech:014905 | mediadive.solution:6207 |
| `mediadive_6209_0_01_NPA_New_Cereal_Leaf-_Prescott_Agar.yaml` | CultureMech:014906 | mediadive.solution:6209 |
| `mediadive_6210_modified_NCL_New_Cereal_Leaf-_Prescott_Liquid.yaml` | CultureMech:014907 | mediadive.solution:6210 |
| `mediadive_6224_0_01_RPA_Rye_Grass_-Prescott_Agar.yaml` | CultureMech:014920 | mediadive.solution:6224 |

For example, CultureMech:014887 is named `3N­BBM+V (Bold Basal Medium with 3­fold Nitrogen  and Vitamins; modified)`. An exact-string search for `3N-BBM+V` does not match it.

## Prose: 57 fields in 47 records

- 34 `preparation_steps[].description` values in 24 records, for example `air­-dried` in `bb_merds.yaml`.
- 23 root `preparation_notes` values in 23 MediaDive solution records.

## Where it comes from

The local raw MediaDive media captures spell `3N-BBM+V` with an ordinary hyphen. They are `data/raw/mediadive/mediadive_media.json` and `data/raw/mediadive_api/mediadive_api_media.json`. I did not find the raw solution payload these six records were built from. So it is unknown whether the MediaDive solution data carries the soft hyphen or an import step introduced it. That should be settled before deciding whether `term.label` should keep the source spelling.

## Suggested fix

1. Move `clean_component_name`, or at least its `_INVISIBLE` table, into a shared helper. Apply it wherever the MediaDive solution importer writes names and labels.
2. Repair the six record names. Append a `curation_history` event, as #409 did with `REMOVED_INVISIBLE_CHARACTERS`.
3. Decide whether to clean the prose fields. They are not identifiers, but they defeat exact-text search.
4. Add a read-only check that fails on these characters in name and label fields, so the next importer cannot reintroduce them.

Related: #387 (closed), #406 (closed), #409.
title: 6 MediaDive solution records and 57 prose fields still contain U+00AD SOFT HYPHEN (#409 only cleaned TOGO)

body:
Found in the second review of #605, at 86d6a1cc. Recorded here and left as they are, with reasons.

1. **Nameless inline stocks: KGX drops them, the occurrence scan counts them.** The closed schema allows `preferred_term: ""` on a nested solution.
   - `kgx_export.nested_solution_target` returns `(None, False)` for such a solution, because it cannot mint a node id. `_walk_solutions` then drops the stock and everything below it.
   - The occurrence scan counts the stock's components for its recipe, because they are still that recipe's ingredients. The two outputs would disagree on such input.
   - The corpus has none today. If one appears, the KGX side should keep the subtree. Making the scan drop real components to match would be the wrong fix.
2. **`blank:` placeholders and the `ingredients_list.tsv` order sort `component_field` as a string.** This affects `blank:<recipe_id>:<component_field>:<index>` keys (`scripts/ingredient_occurrences.py`, `build_unmapped_output` and the list builder). It only matters for blank labels in a recipe with 10 or more sibling stocks; there are no blank nested rows today. The order is deterministic either way.
3. **The `component_field` pattern accepts a trailing newline.** `^(ingredients|composition|(solutions/[0-9]+/)+composition)$` matches `"ingredients\n"` under Python's `re`, where `$` matches before a final newline. The values come from the scanner, never from users, and never contain a newline.
title: Nested-stock edge cases left as is: nameless stocks (KGX drops, scan counts), blank: ordering, pattern newline

body:
Found in the second review of #605, at 86d6a1cc.

## Problem

Each occurrence row's `concentration_value` and `concentration_unit` are relative to the row's own container:

- the medium, for a MediaRecipe's root `ingredients`;
- the stock, for a solution record's root `composition`;
- the stock, for an inline stock's `composition` (rows added by #605).

The summaries' `concentration_info` (`mapped_ingredients.yaml`, `unmapped_ingredients.yaml`, built by `_concentration_rows` in `scripts/ingredient_occurrences.py`) is a deduplicated set of `(value, unit, notes)` per ingredient. It has no field that says which container a value belongs to (`MappedConcentrationInfo` in `mapped_ingredients_schema.yaml`). So medium-level and stock-level values sit side by side, indistinguishable.

This predates #605. On `main` at 41d4d390, the TSV rows with a concentration are:

- 165,218 MediaRecipe root rows;
- 34,983 solution-record root rows, already stock-relative.

#605 adds 6,837 inline-stock rows of the same kind. On the full corpus, the second review found 218 mapped identities with numeric values that come only from inline stocks. One example is NaCl (CHEBI:26710), which now also lists `195.0 G_PER_L` from CultureMech:007718 `solutions/0/composition`.

I found no consumer of `concentration_info` in this repo.

## Options

1. Add a scope to each entry, such as the contributing `record_class` and whether the row is root or inline-stock, or simply its `component_field`.
2. Or limit `concentration_info` to medium-level rows, and leave stock-level values to the TSV.

Either choice is a schema and consumer decision, so #605 leaves `concentration_info` as it was and only documents the scope of the TSV columns.
title: Summary concentration_info lists medium-level and stock-level concentrations without saying which

body:
Found while reviewing #614, the KOMODO citation correction.

`data/raw/komodo/README.md` (Overview) says: "KOMODO is a standardized media database developed by DSMZ (Leibniz Institute)…".

According to the KOMODO paper, this is inaccurate: Oberhardt et al. 2015, *Nat Commun* 6:8493, doi:10.1038/ncomms9493, with affiliations as listed by Europe PMC. KOMODO was built by researchers at Tel Aviv University and the University of Maryland (Oberhardt, Zarecki, Gophna, Ruppin), with DSMZ co-authors (Gronow, Lang) and a Newcastle University co-author (Klenk). It was built by extracting the media recipes of the Leibniz Institute DSMZ collection, so DSMZ is the source of the recipes, not the developer of the database.

Proposed fix: say that KOMODO was built by Oberhardt et al. from the DSMZ media collection. This belongs in #614, which already corrects the same README's reference block.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
title: KOMODO README overview attributes KOMODO's development to DSMZ

body:
Found in the review of #605 at 96c5b0a6. #605 fixes it.

At 96c5b0a6, the scanner decided whether a nested solution is a reference using `kgx_export._index_records_under(input_dir)`. That had three problems:

1. **It depends on the input directory.** The index globs only `*/*.yaml`, one level below the input directory. `_index_records_under('data/normalized_yaml')` returns 4,785 term ids. With `data/normalized_yaml/bacterial` or `data` it returns 0. A scan started anywhere else silently expanded every `term.id` reference, which brings back the per-medium counting that #312 forbids.
2. **The index is fragile.** It is a regex over the first 600 characters of each file. It needs `id:` on line 1 and `term:` followed by `  id:` in block style. Today it is complete: 4,785 term ids, identical to a full parse, with no duplicates. A reordered or flow-style record would drop out silently, though. `lru_cache` keyed on the path string would also return a stale index in a long-lived process.
3. **The import is heavy.** Importing `kgx_export` pulls in koza (about 1.9 s, an optional extra). Without koza it prints `Warning: Koza not installed` on every aggregation.

**Fix in #605:** the scan builds its own index from the records it parses. It defers inline stocks until every file has been read, and skips a reference only when the referenced record emits rows in the same output. The scanner no longer imports `kgx_export`. A test pins its solution-record prefixes to `kgx_export`'s, and another covers a target deeper than one level as well as a scan of a subdirectory.
title: Nested-solution reference detection depended on the input directory, a regex index and a koza import

## Problem

#605 changes the occurrence contract, but three docs still describe the old one:

- `docs/unmapped_ingredients_guide.md:34`: "`component_field` is `ingredients` or `composition`".
- `docs/mediaingredientmech_enrichment.md:130`: "nested `solutions[].composition` is not expanded once per referencing medium. The pipeline records direct containment only."

## Also document

Nested rows put the stock's own concentration in `concentration_value` and `concentration_unit`. That concentration is relative to the stock, not the final medium, and it shares the columns used by root rows. Only `component_field` tells them apart. #604 asks to keep concentrations solution-scoped, so state this where the TSV columns are described.

body:
## Problem

#605 adds occurrence rows whose `component_field` is path-shaped, such as `solutions/0/composition` and `solutions/0/solutions/1/composition`. Both summary schemas declare `component_field` with `range: ComponentFieldEnum`, and the enum allows only `ingredients` and `composition`:

- `src/culturemech/schema/mapped_ingredients_schema.yaml:215`
- `src/culturemech/schema/unmapped_ingredients_schema.yaml:205`

So once the table is regenerated, `mapped_ingredients.yaml` stops validating against its own schema. `unmapped_ingredients.yaml` fails too as soon as a nested component is unmapped.

## Reproduction (at 96c5b0a)

A corpus with one MediaRecipe holding one inline stock:

```python
{"id": "CultureMech:000071", "name": "Nested stock canary", "category": "imported", "physical_state": "LIQUID",
 "ingredients": [{"preferred_term": "EDTA"}],
 "solutions": [{"preferred_term": "Inline stock", "composition": [{"preferred_term": "Biotin"}]}]}
```

- Steps: `scan_ingredient_occurrences`, then `build_mapped_output`, then `write_yaml_output`. Then validate with the same closed `JsonschemaValidationPlugin` setup as `test_imported_category_outputs_validate_against_closed_summary_schemas`.
- Result: 0 scan errors, then one schema error:

```
'solutions/0/composition' is not one of ['ingredients', 'composition'] in /mapped_ingredients/0/recipe_occurrences/0/component_field
```

## Why CI is green

- The closed-schema test's corpus has no `solutions[]`.
- No workflow validates the published mapped or unmapped YAML.

## Options

- Add a permissible value such as `solutions.composition` and carry the position in a separate field, as #604 suggested ("its own `component_field` … and path").
- Or turn `component_field` into a string with a pattern.

Either way, add a nested stock to the closed-schema test. This blocks #605.
title: Nested-stock occurrence rows from #605 fail the closed ComponentFieldEnum in the ingredient summary schemas

> **Corrected 2026-10-14.** The first version reported 145 components. It compared stocks nested below a reference with the top-level referenced record only. The stocks nested under Solution A and Wolfe's mineral solution, and Nitsch's trace elements under Castenholz basal salt solution, are themselves references, and their records carry those components. The correct count is 27, below. The missing record-to-stock links behind those cases affect graph reachability, not occurrence counts: see #608.

A reference here is a `culturemech_term`, or a `term.id` that a solution record carries. The reason given is that the record contributes its own composition, so expanding the reference would count it once per medium (#312, #337).

Found in the review of #605.

## Problem

An inline solution in a medium's `solutions[]` that references a standalone solution record is not expanded, by `term.id` or by a local `culturemech_term`. The occurrence table (#605) and the KGX export (`kgx_export.nested_solution_target`) both rely on the referenced record to contribute its own composition, once, as #312 and #337 require.

That only works if the inline copy carries nothing the referenced record lacks. On `main` at 41d4d390, it often carries more.

## Evidence

The table truncates no component lists. "Distille…" repeats come from each nested stock's own `Distilled water`.

## Three kinds

1. **The referenced record lacks the copy's nested stocks.** Solution A in CultureMech:002020, 002021 and 006688–006692 matches the composition of CultureMech:011207 or 011211. The inline copy, however, also nests *Trace element solution SL-10* and *Selenite-tungstate solution*. The target records have no `solutions`.
2. **The reference conflicts with the content.** Solution C in CultureMech:006689 carries `term.id: mediadive.solution:1776`. That id belongs to CultureMech:011213, which is `Na-DL-lactate` plus water, but the inline composition is `Na-acetate`. In CultureMech:006691 the same reference carries `Na-propionate`. Either the reference id is wrong, or MediaDive reuses one solution id for medium-specific variants.
3. **The referenced record is much smaller than the copy.**
   - CultureMech:000295's *Wolfe's mineral solution* references CultureMech:013012, which has 3 components (NiCl2, Na2SeO3, Na2WO4). The inline copy has 14 more, among them nitrilotriacetic acid, MgSO4, MnSO4, FeSO4, CoSO4 and ZnSO4.
   - The SL-4 references to CultureMech:013111 lose 7 metal salts in the same way.
   - The *Trace minerals* references lose `KOH solution`.

## Why #605 does not paper over this

Expanding the extra part, or every divergent reference, inside the aggregator would hide curation errors such as kind 2. It would also make the occurrence table disagree with the KGX graph. These are corpus fixes:

- complete the standalone record with its missing children (kind 1);
- correct or drop a wrong reference, so the stock becomes inline-only and is counted for its medium (kind 2);
- decide whether the small target is a different stock (kind 3).

## Also

- **Stale docstring.** `kgx_export.nested_solution_target` says the referenced solutions carry "no composition of its own, so nothing is lost". That is no longer true: 91 of them carry one.
- **Missing check.** Nothing detects this divergence. A check that compares each reference's inline payload with its target would stop it recurring silently. Report-only first, because #605's aggregation errors are all fatal.

Related: #577, #604, #605, #312, #337, MediaIngredientMech#879, MediaIngredientMech#891.


See also #607, #608 and #609, filed in parallel; they overlap this issue (they count 145 components where this one counts 138 by case-folded label).
title: 19 inline solution references carry 138 components that their referenced records lack, so no output counts them

body:
## Problem

`scripts/aggregate_ingredients.py` (at 41d4d39, which is current `main`) emits occurrence rows for a `MediaRecipe`'s top-level `ingredients[]` and for the `composition[]` of standalone solution records. It does not read `solutions[].composition[]` nested inside a `MediaRecipe`, nor the `solutions[]` nested inside those.

#577 (9976e05b) moved many recipes' ingredients into nested `solutions[]` to preserve formulation scope. Those ingredients no longer reach `output/ingredient_occurrences.tsv`, so every consumer of that table loses them.

## Evidence

All counts below come from `just aggregate-all-ingredients` run in a clean worktree at 41d4d39, compared with 8c79a66f.

- Of the YAML files under `data/normalized_yaml` that changed between 8c79a66f and 41d4d39, 360 recipes lost top-level ingredients while gaining `solutions[]`. That is 2,175 top-level ingredients in total.
- At 41d4d39, 2,598 recipes carry `solutions[]` with 8,233 nested components. In 136 of those recipes, `ingredients[]` is empty.
- `bacterial/bsk_medium.yaml` (CultureMech:001513) had 17 ingredients at 8c79a66f. It now has 0 top-level ingredients and 4 solutions holding 15 components, among them Proteose peptone no. 2 and Bovine serum albumin. The occurrence table has 0 rows for this recipe.
- `archaea/methanogenium_medium.yaml` (CultureMech:000295) went from 37 occurrence rows to 14. Its vitamin and trace-element solution components, lipoic acid among them, are gone.

## Downstream effect

MediaIngredientMech builds its recipe membership edges and `occurrence_statistics` from this table. MediaIngredientMech#879 rebuilt them from 41d4d39. Rows that were removed but are still genuine include:

- Proteose Peptone No. 2 (MICRO:0002393): 7 → 5 recipes;
- lipoic acid (CHEBI:16494): 25 recipes removed (the total still rises, because of label-index changes);
- sulfur (CHEBI:33403): 3 recipes removed.

The net edge count still rises by 3,595, which hides the loss. MediaIngredientMech#879 is on hold until this is fixed.

## Expected

Each component of a nested solution, at any depth, should produce an occurrence row for its enclosing recipe. It needs its own `component_field` (for example `solutions.composition`) and path, so a consumer can tell these rows from top-level ingredients and the formulation scope from #577 survives. Concentrations should stay solution-scoped, as #577 intends.

Related: #580 (regenerate the occurrence table after the MIM pin lands).

body:
**Where**

https://culturebotai.github.io/CultureMech/pages/media_growth_review.html (summary tiles, Review Status table and Reviewed Records table). 16 records are affected; examples are below.

**What happens**

The tiles show 33 "Records covered by proposals or applied evidence (0.2%)" and 33 "Records with applied growth metrics", but 49 "Records with supported applied evidence". The supported-evidence count is larger than the covered count that should contain it.

The 16 extra records (6 archaea, 10 bacterial) have SUPPORT evidence attached directly to a target organism (`target_organisms[].evidence`) and no `growth_metrics`. Examples: CultureMech:008908 Sulfolobus Medium (For DSM 5348), CultureMech:009111 Caldicellulosiruptor Medium (For DSM 10319) and CultureMech:009226 Sulfolobus Medium (Anaerobic) (For DSM 2162). Their record pages show this evidence under "Target organisms and growth evidence", each entry with Supports set to SUPPORT, and the schema describes the field as "Evidence supporting growth on this medium" ([culturemech.yaml lines 1157-1158](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/CultureMech/blob/41d4d390123c0d8320cd53e994470c88a1b86d8c/src/culturemech/schema/culturemech.yaml#L1157-L1158)). On the review page, the Review Status table counts them under "No review artifact in this build" (15,877), the Reviewed Records table leaves them out (33 rows), and searching it for CultureMech:008908 or CultureMech:009111 returns 0 rows. The page therefore counts these records as having supported applied evidence and, at the same time, as having no review artifact.

Cause at the deployed commit:

- `scripts/build_media_growth_review_manifest.py` adds organism-level SUPPORT evidence to `supported_growth_evidence_count` ([lines 92-94](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/CultureMech/blob/41d4d390123c0d8320cd53e994470c88a1b86d8c/scripts/build_media_growth_review_manifest.py#L92-L94)). The `applied_growth_evidence` status also requires `growth_metric_count` ([line 118](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/CultureMech/blob/41d4d390123c0d8320cd53e994470c88a1b86d8c/scripts/build_media_growth_review_manifest.py#L118)), so these records fall to `not_reviewed`.
- `scripts/build_media_growth_review_html.py` counts the supported tile over every manifest row, but computes the covered tile as the total minus `not_reviewed` ([lines 65-68](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/CultureMech/blob/41d4d390123c0d8320cd53e994470c88a1b86d8c/scripts/build_media_growth_review_html.py#L65-L68)) and leaves `not_reviewed` rows out of the table ([lines 84-86](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/CultureMech/blob/41d4d390123c0d8320cd53e994470c88a1b86d8c/scripts/build_media_growth_review_html.py#L84-L86)).

In `reports/media_growth_review_corpus_scope.md` (dated 2026-05-05), the applied-growth-metrics and supported-applied-evidence counts were equal (31 and 31). The gap appeared once records gained organism-level evidence without growth metrics; for example, CultureMech:008908 and CultureMech:009111 had no target organisms at commit 0fb7480 (2026-05-15), the last change to the manifest script.

**Expected**

Every record the supported-evidence tile counts is also counted as covered, so that tile is never larger than the covered tile, and those records appear in the Reviewed Records table instead of under "No review artifact in this build". Either records with supported organism-level evidence get a reviewed status (applied evidence or a separate one), or the supported-evidence tile counts the same population as the status rule and its label says what it counts.

**Reproduce**

1. Open https://culturebotai.github.io/CultureMech/pages/media_growth_review.html and compare the second tile (33) with the fourth (49).
2. Type CultureMech:008908 in the Reviewed Records search box. The count reads "0 reviewed rows shown".
3. Open https://culturebotai.github.io/CultureMech/pages/normalized/008908.html. Under "Target organisms and growth evidence", both organisms carry SUPPORT evidence (for example doi:10.1128/AEM.02019-07), and the record has no growth metrics.
4. Optionally, count the YAML under `data/normalized_yaml` at the deployed commit: 49 records have SUPPORT evidence under `target_organisms`, 33 have growth metrics, and the other 16 have only organism-level evidence.

body:
**Where**
All 6,320 merged pages listed on https://culturebotai.github.io/CultureMech/pages/index.html, for example
- https://culturebotai.github.io/CultureMech/pages/media/000039.html and https://culturebotai.github.io/CultureMech/pages/normalized/000039.html
- https://culturebotai.github.io/CultureMech/pages/media/006487.html and https://culturebotai.github.io/CultureMech/pages/normalized/006487.html

**What happens**
Each merged record is published under the ID of one of its normalized source records, so all 6,320 IDs on the merged index also identify a normalized page. Both pages show the ID in their title and header, and 6,306 of the 6,320 pairs show the same name, for example "3n_bbm_v (CultureMech:000039)". The two index pages share the title "CultureMech — Media index", and each lists CultureMech:000039, linking to a different page. The pages are not interchangeable. media/006487 is merged from CultureMech:006487 and CultureMech:001923 (1,455 merged records combine several sources; 4,865 have one). In a random sample of 400 ID pairs, 128 merged pages list different ingredient, concentration or ontology values from the normalized page with the same ID: media/000039 has 7 ingredient rows, the extra one a fragment of preparation text parsed as an ingredient, while normalized/000039 has 6. docs/RECIPE_ID_LIFECYCLE.md states that an issued ID is unique and that exactly one current YAML record carries an active ID, and data/culturemech_recipe_catalog.tsv maps each of these IDs to its normalized file only, so a reader citing CultureMech:000039 cannot tell which composition is meant. The differing compositions come from merge-layer drift (#396), but the shared identity is by design: the merger deep-copies the canonical source record, including its ID ("Root identity is canonical" in src/culturemech/merge/formulation.py), so a fresh merge would still give each merged ID a second page.

**Expected**
Each ID resolves to one page. Merged pages either get their own identifier or present themselves as a merged view of the listed normalized records, without taking a member's ID as their own, and link to the canonical normalized page.

**Reproduce**
1. Open media/000039.html and normalized/000039.html (full URLs above).
2. Both are titled 3n_bbm_v (CultureMech:000039), but their ingredient tables have 7 and 6 rows.
3. Open https://culturebotai.github.io/CultureMech/pages/index.html and https://culturebotai.github.io/CultureMech/pages/normalized/index.html: each lists CultureMech:000039, linking to a different page.

body:
**Where**
385 of the 6,320 merged record pages under https://culturebotai.github.io/CultureMech/pages/media/ (528 of the 10,634 sources listed across all merged pages), for example
- https://culturebotai.github.io/CultureMech/pages/media/000038.html (2asw)
- https://culturebotai.github.io/CultureMech/pages/media/000039.html (3n_bbm_v)
- https://culturebotai.github.io/CultureMech/pages/media/004662.html (yeast_extract_mineral_medium, listed twice)

**What happens**
The Provenance list on media/000038 reads "2asw (normalized source unresolved)", although the merged record's own ID, CultureMech:000038, is the normalized 2asw record (pages/normalized/000038.html, data/normalized_yaml/algae/2asw.yaml). Every unresolved source is a file stem shared by normalized records in different category directories: 2asw is both algae/2asw.yaml (CultureMech:000038) and bacterial/2asw.yaml (CultureMech:000415). The 528 entries involve 273 such stems, 271 shared by two records and 2 by three. In 523 of the 528, exactly one of the records with that stem is in the merged record's own category, and 261 of the 385 pages are single-source merges whose own ID is that record, as on 000038. The renderer causes this: `normalized_source_index()` in `src/culturemech/render_media_pages.py` keeps only stems that map to one ID, and `merged_from` stores bare stems, so every stem among the cross-category filename collisions (curation tracked in #151) loses its link. Issue #546, closed by #559, asked for links built from explicit source identity mappings; #559 links a source only when its stem names exactly one record.

The counts were computed from the repository at 41d4d39 with the renderer's rule, and they match the live site on all 385 pages and on 400 sampled merged pages predicted to resolve fully.

**Expected**
A merged source links to its normalized record whenever its identity is known, for example from the merged record's own ID for single-source merges or from source IDs recorded in `merged_from` at merge time. Only genuinely ambiguous sources stay marked unresolved.

**Reproduce**
1. Open https://culturebotai.github.io/CultureMech/pages/media/000038.html and scroll to Provenance.
2. Note "2asw (normalized source unresolved)" under "Merged from 1 source record.", while the page header shows CultureMech:000038.
3. Open https://culturebotai.github.io/CultureMech/pages/normalized/000038.html: it is the 2asw record with that ID.

body:
**Where**
https://culturebotai.github.io/CultureMech/pages/normalized/index.html

**What happens**
At a 390 px viewport the page is 747 px wide (scrollWidth 747, clientWidth 390), so it scrolls sideways. Recipe names wrap; the overflow comes from the list layout. The narrow-screen rule in style.css (max-width 600px) sets `columns: 1` on `ul.medium-index`, which still makes each list a multi-column container. In the bacterial section (14,329 entries, a list about 470,000 px tall), Chrome places the last entry, CultureMech:000908 zymomonas_mobilis_medium, in a second column at x = 403 px, level with the first entry; its bullet shows at the right edge beside "Fe-EDTA complex". In Chrome's mobile emulation the layout viewport widens to 747 px and the fixed Dark mode button moves to x = 645 to 731 px, off screen. Setting `columns: auto` on these lists in the console brings the page back to 390 px.

The spill depends on the list's exact height, so it is width-specific: of 14 widths tested from 320 to 599 px, only 390 px overflows (375, 393 and 414 px fit), and nothing overflows at 768, 1,280 or 1,440 px. This was measured in Chrome 155 and Chromium 151 on macOS; with other system fonts the affected width may differ. The same 747 px width was reported in #545, which #559 closed by making long names wrap; the overflow remains because of the column rule.

**Expected**
The index fits a 390 px screen without horizontal scrolling and the theme button stays on screen, for example by using `columns: auto` instead of `columns: 1` in the narrow-screen rule.

**Reproduce**
1. Open the page in Chrome with the device toolbar set to 390 px wide (at 375 or 414 px the page fits).
2. Scroll right, or compare document.documentElement.scrollWidth (747) with clientWidth (390).
3. Scroll to the bacterial heading: a bullet sits at the right edge beside the first entry. It is the last entry, CultureMech:000908, in an off-screen second column.

body:
Review finding on #591.
- Of the 19 flagged REJECTED rows, 12 label groups change. 3 were already unsafe-ambiguous, and 4 are shadowed by a MAPPED row in the same group, so "the rest were already refused" was false. "CoCl2 x 2/4 H2O → hexahydrate" was a misleading example.
- "20 MAPPED rows" came from an earlier parser version; the shipped parser gives 25.

Fix: correct the PR description.
title: PR #591 description overstated the guard's effect and miscounted MAPPED conflicts

body:
Review finding on #591. With #591's parser, 25 MAPPED rows have a label hydrate count that differs from the row's preferred term. One is a parser false positive, so 24 are genuine. Examples:
- `magnesium sulfate anhydrous` → CHEBI:31795 (heptahydrate)
- `Anhydrous sodium sulfite` → Na2SO3 x 5 H2O
- `sodium sulfate, anhydrous` → Na2SO4 x 10 H2O
- `NaH2PO4·H2O` → nah2po4_x_2_h2o

The guard also never reaches tombstones behind a MAPPED row in the same group. Example: `Cystein-HCl x 2 H2O (5% (w/v))` resolves via MAPPED to monohydrate CHEBI:91248.

MAPPED rows are MIM's curated answers, and the resolver contract is to honour them, so #591 deliberately leaves them alone. These are MIM data defects and belong with MediaIngredientMech#811. Overriding MAPPED answers in CultureMech would be a contract change, which needs a separate decision.
title: MIM MAPPED rows whose label hydrate contradicts the identity (out of #579 scope)

body:
Review finding on #591. Missing tests:
- the weak-normalization path reaching a hydrate-conflict group
- several groups where one is a hydrate conflict
- an identity whose ontology label states no count
- a tombstone shadowed by a MAPPED row earlier in its group
- the reason text in the preferred-term fallback case
- the parser false-positive strings from the parser issue

title: Test gaps in hydrate-guard tests

body: Review nit on #591. `_decision_for_groups` uses `assert conflict is not None`. Under `python -O` the assert is stripped, and a divergence would surface as a TypeError. Replace it with an explicit error. Also render a 0 count as "anhydrous" in the reason text.
title: Hydrate guard uses assert in production code; reports anhydrous as '0 H2O'

body:
Review finding on #591. Inert at the current pin (all 19 flagged REJECTED rows parse correctly), but it misfires if these strings get tombstoned.

False positives (wrong count):
- `copper sulphate(5.H2O)` → 1 (in the index, MAPPED)
- `pH 7.0 H2O` → 0
- `Borax H2O`, `Mix H2O`, `10x H2O` → 1
- `dist. H2O`, `Solution 2. H2O` → 1
- `MgSO4·7H2O·H2O` → 7, not None: the contradiction check is bypassed because finditer doesn't overlap

False negatives (guard silently skips):
- space or hyphen separators: `FeSO4 7H2O`, `CuCl2-2H2O`, `Na2S-9H2O`
- prefixes not in the table: hemipenta, hemihepta, octadeca
- German `-hydrat`

Proposed fix in #591: require the left side to be a chemical-formula token (starts with an uppercase letter and contains a digit or a second uppercase letter); scan with overlapping matches; add hyphen/space separators before a digit count, the missing prefixes, and `hydrat`.
title: label_hydrate_count false positives and false negatives

body:
Review finding on #591.

1. The code falls back to the tombstone row's `preferred_term` only when the identity has no qualifying `ontology_label` row. If an ontology label exists but states no count (447 of 475 identities with ontology labels), the check is skipped, even when preferred terms disagree with the label. The doc says "when the index has none". No current tombstone is affected.
2. `preferred_term` is per row, and the PR's own rationale is that preferred terms vary under one identity. CHEBI:32142 tombstones carry both "Trisodium citrate x 2 H2O" and "Sodium Citrate".
3. `ontology_label` rows are only counted when MAPPED, but a REJECTED ontology_label row still names the identity (e.g. "nickel chloride hexahydrate" → CHEBI:53542).

Proposed fix in #591: derive one count per identity, from ontology labels of any status first and otherwise from the consensus of its MAPPED preferred terms, and document that.
title: Hydrate guard's target-count derivation disagrees with its documentation

body:
Review finding on #591.

`#591` makes cross-hydrate tombstones fail closed, but keeps the recipe's local term as `AMBIGUOUS_LOCAL_FALLBACK`. KGX (`kgx_export.py` `_resolved_ingredient_id`) publishes only `decision.identifier`, so the fallback label never reaches the graph. For the 21 affected recipe rows, the fallbacks are anhydrous or generic identities according to the index itself:
- `Na2MoO4.H2O` → CHEBI:75215 (ontology label "sodium molybdate (anhydrous)")
- `MgSO4 x H2O` → CHEBI:32599 (records named "Magnesium sulfate" and "MgSO4 x 6 H2O")
- `NiCl2 x H2O` → CHEBI:34887 (records named NiCl2, NiCl2 x 2 H2O, NiCl2 x 5 H2O)

As written, #591 swaps one wrong hydrate for another. Proposed fix in #591: for a hydrate conflict, keep the local fallback only when its identity positively states the label's hydrate count; otherwise fail fully closed.
title: Hydrate-conflict tombstones fall back to recipe-local IDs that are also the wrong hydrate

body:
The required full job at f52f224a40 timed out at its unchanged 40-minute limit (#576). Python 3.13 currently uses coverage.py 7.13.1 with the default ctrace collector. This repository measures statement coverage, not branches, and does not configure coverage plugins or dynamic contexts. The installed library and its versioned documentation support sysmon statement coverage on Python 3.13.

Measured unchanged 804-test Geobacter module with both collectors: ctrace 371.14s, sysmon 151.95s; both 804 passed. CoverageData comparison found exactly the same 101 measured files and 333 executed lines, with no differing line sets. This is a diagnostic subset, not a full-suite pass. A broader equivalence run is underway.

Proposed fix: use the supported lower-overhead collector, with coverage correctness/floor regression checks. Preserve every test, source/omit scope, 17% coverage floor, 120-second test-call limit and 40-minute CI timeout. Re-run all required checks before merge. No parallel-test bypass or change to scientific data is proposed.

Source: https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/7.13.1/config.html#run-core

body: Adversarial follow-up for PR #577 and runtime blocker #576: tests/test_name_term_elements.py calls OAK entity_metadata_map separately for every required CHEBI term, redoing the annotation-property query each time. A live sample of the clean pytest process was dominated by SQLite reads. An exact comparison across all 234 IDs required by the current corpus found 229 formula values and five legitimately absent formulas, no multiple values, no differing answers, and no metadata errors. The old fixture took 333.44s including its corpus scan; entities_metadata_statements with the same formula predicate took 1.39s. Separately, the existing broad exception handler converts lookup failures to missing formulas, so an unavailable metadata query can silently remove checks. This was identified by code review, not a claim that current metadata queries failed. Acceptance: retain the same corpus pairs, formula source, predicate, first-value semantics, allowlist and mismatch assertions; use the supported bulk API; fail on query errors or wholly absent formula coverage; add isolated tests for missing individual formulas, duplicate IDs/values, wrong rows, empty coverage and failures; retain all full-suite/runtime/coverage gates.

title: PR concentration checks depend on ambient imports and misclassify dated curation packets

body:
Found while reviewing #537 (MIM label index refresh to 6643131b).

## Problem

`MIMLabelIndex._group_state` (`src/culturemech/ingredients/mim_label_index.py`) treats a `REJECTED` row as `mapped` whenever its identifier is held by a live MAPPED row. That is the intended merge-tombstone redirect. But at 6643131b, MIM tombstones carry labels from a *different hydrate* than the record they redirect to, so the redirect becomes a confident wrong identity:

| label | new answer | label implies |
|---|---|---|
| `MgSO4 x H2O`, `MgSO4 . H2O` (13 recipe rows) | CHEBI:31795 MgSO4·7H2O, REJECTED, `unique` | monohydrate |
| `Na2MoO4.H2O`, `Na2MoO4xH2O` (3 rows) | CHEBI:75213 Na2MoO4·2H2O, REJECTED, `unique` | monohydrate |

Under the previous pin (9f09e4fb), the MgSO4 labels were flagged ambiguous. Repository policy says hydrate counts are identity-significant, but the resolver has no check that the query label's hydrate count matches the target's `preferred_term`.

## Upstream

The data defect is MediaIngredientMech#811 (still open). KGX resolves at export time, so these edges are emitted until MIM fixes the tombstones.

## Possible fix (CultureMech side, defence in depth)

When a REJECTED tombstone redirects a label that has an explicit hydrate count different from the target preferred term's count, fail closed (AMBIGUOUS / local fallback) instead of returning a trusted answer. Add regression tests built from the rows above.
title: Resolver trusts MIM merge tombstones whose hydrate count contradicts the target identity

body:
# Official Recipe Evidence Is Rejected by Reference Validation

Related concentration-repair tracking: #150. This is distinct from #565's
source-check-to-ingredient binding defect.

## Reproduction

Observed on 2026-10-08 in the local concentration-curation worktree at baseline
`f8af2562c3ae51d5f9ed01a484f4a2971b6cd80f`, with
`linkml-reference-validator==0.1.6` and Python 3.13. The new curation records and
reports are not yet committed or published; the underlying public source and
matcher examples below do not require those record edits.

1. **Literal brackets are stripped as though they were citations.** For
   `https://togomedium.org/sparqlist/api/gmdb_medium_by_gmid?gm_id=M1124`, the
   source JSON names `Trace vitamins (see Medium [M190])`. An exact JSON snippet
   including that label and its 10 ml dose is rejected. The error instead
   searches for `Trace vitamins (see Medium  )`.
2. **HTML chemical subscripts change excerpt matching.** At
   `https://www.jcm.riken.jp/cgi-bin/jcm/jcm_grmd?GRMD=1084`, the exact rendered-text
   excerpt `40.0 g FeSO4·7H2O in 0.1 N H2SO4 solution and fill up to 100.0 ml.`
   fails the installed matcher. At JCM1282, `8% (w/v) NaHCO3 solution` also fails.
   Both match whitespace-normalized text extracted from the captured source
   HTML with BeautifulSoup. The chemical numbers must not be discarded.
3. **JSON dataset titles fall back to the URL.** For the TOGO M1153 endpoint,
   the verified `meta.name` is `Thiobacillus Prosperus Medium`. Reference
   validation instead extracts the URL as the title and rejects the correct
   supplied title. The same occurs for M142's `Pyrococcus Medium` and other
   receiving datasets.

The public-source snippet checks can be reproduced using
`SupportingTextValidator(ReferenceValidationConfig(cache_dir=...)).validate(snippet, url)`.
Use a fresh cache to distinguish parser behavior from stale cached content.

## Impact and Evidence

The seven-record nested-stock review adds 206 primary evidence entries.
All 206 snippets are literal matches to hash-pinned HTTP-200 captures; the
installed matcher accepts 200 and rejects six. All seven
`just validate-references <record>` commands fail, also including API title
mismatches. Independent literal checks are not represented as an automated
reference-gate pass.

Local reproducibility artifacts are under
`reports/ingredient_concentration_curation/20261008-m142-nested-traces/`:
`context.json`, `plan.json`, `reference-validation.json`, `audit.py`, and one
report per exact record path. No source quote was rewritten to hide a failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Preserve literal accession brackets in structured-source snippets; do not
  treat `[M190]` as removable Markdown citation syntax.
- Normalize HTML presentation of chemical subscripts consistently without
  losing formula digits, hydrate numbers, signs, units or decimal precision.
- Extract or explicitly support structured recipe titles from the official
  API metadata instead of comparing a verified title with a URL fallback.
- Add fixture-backed positive and negative regressions. Wrong ingredient,
  amount, unit, stock/final scope and title must still fail. Avoid a broad fuzzy
  matcher or disabling title/snippet checks to turn the gate green.
- Re-run the seven records and representative earlier JCM/TOGO cohorts; retain
  distinct reporting for source-access failure, unavailable metadata, a parser
  limitation and a genuine contradiction.

The corpus-wide merge/freshness failures are separate publication blockers.
title: Reference validation rejects exact official recipe evidence: brackets, chemical subscripts, and API titles

Adversarial review of PR #563.

The report renderer indexes manual source checks by path/field and guards only the old concentration. Reordering two ingredients with equal amounts can attach a quotation to the wrong chemical. Duplicate checks overwrite each other, unmatched checks disappear, and a missing snippet can still count as source-inspected. An old-value mismatch is discovered only after output files are opened/truncated.

Reproduced with synthetic fixtures in tests/test_concentration_review_reports.py (wrong ID/hash/name/identity, duplicate/unmatched overrides, missing snippet, and preflight output checks).

Required fix: preflight every override before any output write; require snapshot hash, record ID, ingredient identity/name, old value, exact snippet, reference and locator. Reject duplicate or unmatched checks. Preserve all 12 existing source decisions by explicitly binding them to their reviewed snapshot.

body:
The required `Changed Python quality + wheel smoke` check fails at the renderer type boundary on PR #559 head `1258379ae693528cc6a0c6f76bbcd9bcf83f162f`.

In `src/culturemech/render_media_pages.py`, `community_links() -> dict[str, str]` returns `json.loads(path.read_text())["links"]` directly. Mypy treats that expression as `Any` and reports:

```text
src/culturemech/render_media_pages.py:96: error: Returning Any from function declared to return "dict[str, str]"  [no-any-return]
```

Reproduction: run `just typecheck-renderer`. The failure is also recorded in [job 112060465655](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/CultureMech/actions/runs/37398623932/job/112060465655). Ruff, Black, skill validation and README statistics pass in that job; this is separate from the Black formatting defect in #561.

The local fix makes the bundled JSON return type explicit with `typing.cast(dict[str, str], ...)`, preserving runtime behavior. All nine bundled CommunityMech link entries were checked to have string keys and values, with complete equality before and after the change. No scientific records or link destinations change.

Local verification: renderer mypy passes; all eight changed Python files pass Ruff and Black; 16 renderer/website-audit tests pass; an isolated installed-wheel smoke check passes for the CLI, rendering, EDTA resolution and all nine packaged links. Three fresh render canaries are identical except for their build-signature comment. The untracked local record previews were refreshed by that same signature-only substitution; the Pages workflow renders its own record pages during deployment.

Acceptance:

- [ ] The required renderer typecheck passes without suppressing or disabling `no-any-return`.
- [ ] The packaged CommunityMech link snapshot and rendered record content remain unchanged.
- [ ] Required PR and merge-queue checks pass on the corrected head.

These results describe local verification; the correction has not yet been pushed or deployed.
title: Declare the bundled CommunityMech link return type so the renderer typecheck passes

body:
## Problem

The vendored MIM label index (`src/culturemech/data/mediaingredientmech/label_index.csv`) is pinned to MIM `9f09e4fb` (2026-09-03). MIM `main` is now 106 commits ahead, including the #312, #232, #669/#704 and #754 identity re-groundings and merges, so CultureMech still resolves recipe labels to superseded identities.

The pin can't be moved. A preview refresh against the current MIM `main` fails before any comparison:

```
$ uv run python scripts/refresh_mim_label_index.py 7a65c4e9173efc435b77c300b5f1fedc71bc5297
culturemech.ingredients.mim_label_index.LabelIndexError: row 3001 has unknown mapping_status 'AMBIGUOUS'
```

## Cause

`MAPPING_STATUSES = {"MAPPED", "UNMAPPED", "REJECTED"}` in `src/culturemech/ingredients/mim_label_index.py` is narrower than the producer's enum. MIM's `MappingStatusEnum` (`src/mediaingredientmech/schema/mediaingredientmech.yaml`) also permits `PENDING_REVIEW`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `NEEDS_EXPERT` and `AMBIGUOUS`. MIM's `docs/LABEL_INDEX_CONTRACT.md` does not narrow `mapping_status` to three values.

The offending row is one record:

```
CMC + PY + Horse Serum,preferred_term,UNMAPPED_0740,CMC + PY + Horse Serum,,AMBIGUOUS,unique
```

No CultureMech recipe uses this label (0 rows in `output/ingredient_occurrences.tsv`), so the mismatch affects no recipe. It only blocks the refresh.

## Proposed fix

- Accept MIM's full `MappingStatusEnum`, and keep failing closed on any value outside it.
- Treat the four undecided curation statuses as **no MIM identity**: never `mapped`, and never authoritative-unmapped suppression. A row whose curation is unfinished says neither "this is X" nor "this is nothing", so it resolves like an unsafe-ambiguity group. An explicitly labelled local fallback is kept, and otherwise the label is unresolved.
- Leave the pin refresh as a separate, reviewed step. This change only makes it possible.

Related: #417 (a pin bump must preserve resolution answers).
title: MIM label-index reader rejects MIM's own AMBIGUOUS/undecided mapping_status, blocking the pin refresh

body:
## Problem
There is no skill or command that gives a readable list of distinct ingredients across the corpus. `just aggregate-all-ingredients` writes the full occurrence TSV (~117 MB, one row per ingredient per record) and two YAML views that embed every occurrence (~128 MB mapped). A per-ingredient list currently needs an ad-hoc pandas step.

## Proposal
- Have `run_aggregation` also write `output/ingredients_list.tsv`: one row per distinct ingredient, using the **same grouping keys** as the mapped/unmapped views (resolved identifier for mapped, the unmapped group key otherwise), so totals reconcile exactly with `total_mapped_count` + `total_unmapped_count`.
- Columns: term, identifier, ontology source, mapping status, occurrence and distinct-recipe counts, source label variants, recipe categories.
- Expose it via `--list-output` and the `aggregate-all-ingredients` just recipe.
- Add a `list-ingredients` skill that routes to the recipe and explains the outputs.
- Tests and docs.
title: Add a one-row-per-ingredient list to the ingredient aggregation, plus a skill

body:
The support matrix declares ID/label validation enabled, but the `merge_yaml` target remains `severity: warn` at current main `4eb22545deb8be58d18782aca24e58046264433f`. The shared validator uses that setting to suppress every error-class finding for existing merged records, including nonexistent ontology IDs and unknown prefixes. A passing `validate-products` job therefore does not establish identifier integrity for this published recipe layer.

A read-only reproduction loaded the current validator and a copy of the actual `merge_yaml` target over one temporary YAML record. An offline adapter stub reported `ID_NOT_FOUND` for `CHEBI:299999`; enforcement returned 0. A `TYPO:1` prefix and a resolvable ID carrying the wrong label also returned 0. Changing only target severity to `error` returned 2 for each case. No production records were changed, and the reproduction concerns this validator's enforcement pass rather than the outcome of unrelated QC gates.

Add a blocking integrity policy for merged inputs:
- Missing ontology IDs, unknown prefixes, adapter failures, and malformed required input must fail CI independently of any temporary label-warning policy.
- Resolve or explicitly baseline the current label backlog with exact reviewed exceptions, so new incorrect pairs cannot silently extend it.
- Exercise the repository's actual merged-input configuration with negative tests and a passing valid control.
- Make the support declaration and CI documentation distinguish fully enforced fields from any remaining advisory label checks.

Coordinate changes through the CLAW-governed validator and its reviewed vendor pin. This is complementary to #396: reproducing the merge layer from normalized records and enforcing the identifiers in the resulting product are separate checks. #278 concerns scientific grounding correctness even when a label already agrees with its ID.

Evidence: [merged-input target](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/CultureMech/blob/4eb22545deb8be58d18782aca24e58046264433f/conf/id_label_targets.yaml#L243), [severity filter](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/CultureMech/blob/4eb22545deb8be58d18782aca24e58046264433f/scripts/validate_id_label_correspondence.py#L1038), and [CI caller](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/CultureMech/blob/4eb22545deb8be58d18782aca24e58046264433f/.github/workflows/label-correspondence.yaml).
title: Enforce identifier integrity for merged recipe inputs
