body: We found this while auditing the CultureBotAI X-Mech page (https://culturebotai.github.io/mechs/). The website tracks it in https://github.com/CultureBotAI/CultureBotAI.github.io/issues/147. Everything below was checked against `main` at [`2c88163`](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/CultureMech/commit/2c881635f73db02375cbd99f50ed72ac8f20c346) and the live site on 2026-09-25. --- ## 1. GitHub Pages is set to branch builds, and they overwrite the Actions deployment ### What is wrong There are two deployers for the site, and the wrong one runs most often. - **Pages source: legacy branch build of `main` at `/`.** ``` $ gh api repos/CultureBotAI/CultureMech/pages {"status":"built", "build_type":"legacy", "source":{"branch":"main","path":"/"}, ...} ``` - **The workflow deploys the real site.** [`.github/workflows/generate-pages.yaml`](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/CultureMech/blob/2c88163/.github/workflows/generate-pages.yaml) builds `app/data.js`, `pages/normalized/`, `pages/media/`, `pages/index.html` and `dashboard/`. It stages them into `site/` and deploys that with `actions/upload-pages-artifact` and `actions/deploy-pages`. It only runs on pushes that touch its `paths:` filter (lines 6-19), or on `workflow_dispatch`. Since #320 ([`5e8494b`](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/CultureMech/commit/5e8494b335), 2026-08-21), the built files are gitignored and no longer tracked: - `app/data.js` - `pages/index.html`, `pages/media/`, `pages/normalized/` - `dashboard/` On `main`, `pages/` holds only `media_growth_review.html`. A branch build of `main` therefore publishes the repository without any of those files. Every push to `main` triggers a branch build. For a push outside the path filter, that build is the only deployment, and it replaces the last Actions deployment. For a push inside the filter, both deployers run. The workflow wins only because it finishes about 10 minutes later. ### Evidence Deployments to the `github-pages` environment. Branch builds are created by `github-pages[bot]`. On `90a2ed477ed6a015ed59b9be3cf37d01a62ca4c3`,
`scripts/generate_sssom_mappings.py::canonical_label` silently catches exceptions
from configured OAK adapters and substitutes the recipe label. Generation can
succeed with noncanonical object labels, leaving the separate product validator
to report mismatches without explaining the failed lookup.

An offline reproduction injects an adapter whose `label()` raises
`RuntimeError("offline ontology adapter")`: looking up `FOODON:03315719` then
returns the fallback `Casein peptone` without any diagnostic. This differs from
the intended fallback for a prefix with no configured ontology adapter.

While verifying #484, a locally generated SSSOM product contained 11 fallback
label mismatches. Regenerating after the adapters became available cleared them;
`validate-products` now passes with 91 nonblocking warnings. The
[main-commit label check](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/CultureMech/actions/runs/35576623425)
also passed. This finding concerns missing failure diagnostics, not a currently
failing main gate or a request to relabel the recipe corpus.

The pending #484 branch fixes the finding locally:

- Warn once per configured ontology prefix, naming the first affected CURIE,

Adversarial review of the unpublished #484 repair found three reproducible hazards in `scripts/repair_rejected_peptone_groundings.py`:

- A Trypticase term aliased to a genuine detergent term changed both ingredients, while the audit recorded only Trypticase. The expected-document check also shared that alias and accepted the unintended change.
- Reading CRLF files as text normalized their line endings, making `before_sha256` disagree with the original bytes and rewriting untouched lines.
- A report path referring to a source recipe overwrote it with JSON, including in preview mode. Direct paths, symlinks in either direction, and hard links reproduced this.

Fixed locally before publication: the repair rejects an edit when its YAML node or an ancestor is shared, including the history sequence it appends to, while preserving unrelated aliases. It reads, hashes, and writes bytes, retains CRLF formatting, and rejects report/source collisions using resolved paths and file identity. All planned source files are also reread before the first write so a detected concurrent edit aborts the apply.

Validation: 28 focused tests pass, covering these cases, preservation, idempotence, count and MIM checks, and the three corrected repair templates; the corpus test is excluded from that count. Preflight failure leaves recipes unwritten. This is not a transactional batch: a later I/O failure can leave partial writes and reports the number completed.

Status: fixed locally for #484; pending publication. The destructive cases were demonstrated with temporary fixtures, not observed damage to the 109-record cohort.

The full source-bound ingredient build under #471/#472 exposed a scalability defect that the 32-point canary did not reveal. `generate()` attaches the complete graph receipt (including 171,954 ingredient occurrence entries) to `df.attrs['graph_receipt']`. `render_html()` then calls `DataFrame.iterrows()`. pandas 3 finalizes each row by deep-copying the DataFrame attributes, so the full nested occurrence ledger is copied once per ingredient.

The actual full build spent more than 12 minutes in this phase. A native process sample showed Python dictionary-copy work; a graceful interrupt produced the exact traceback `DataFrame.iterrows -> Series.__finalize__ -> deepcopy(other.attrs) -> copy._deepcopy_dict/_deepcopy_list`. The interruption occurred before artifact promotion, leaving the prior ingredient map unchanged.

Acceptance:

- Pass the large receipt directly to the HTML renderer instead of storing it in DataFrame attributes.
- Keep the full matching/occurrence receipt and truthful HTML provenance; do not drop evidence to improve performance.
- Add a bounded source-to-publication regression using a receipt that rejects deep-copying, so the actual old path fails without a large corpus or timing threshold.
- Verify a fresh-process mutation restoring the attachment fails, then rerun the actual full source build and validate HTML/points/receipt together.

Evidence: task workspace `culture-full-graph-process-sample.txt` and the first `culturemech-pacmap-full-graph.log`. Coordinated by CultureBotAI/culturebotai-claw#426.

body:
An adversarial review of the embedding rollout reproduced stale graph-vector reuse when compressed source bytes change while basename, byte length and integer mtime remain unchanged. These are currently the graph pickle cache identity fields; they do not establish source-content identity.

The reproduction uses a tiny valid TSV.gz with a header and CHEBI:1. First load: vector [1,0]. Replace the source row with [0,1], preserving byte length and mtime. The next ordinary load returns cached [1,0]. The same behavior was reproduced in CultureMech, MediaIngredientMech and CommunityMech in fresh temporary fixtures; no production source or cache was modified.

This matters for the new provenance work: hashing today's source alongside a stale cache would falsely attribute old vectors to new source bytes. Verified generation must parse and bind the actual selected source, or reuse a cache whose source digest, parser/filter policy and vector bytes are verified together. Existing unverified pickle caches must not be promoted merely by attaching a new receipt.

Acceptance: a regression changing source bytes while preserving size/mtime returns the new vectors (or refuses the old cache); a failed source parse/cache write preserves the previous valid state; freshly generated map receipts bind the actual parsed source and vector bytes. This is a concrete cache-identity subissue of the ongoing graph-provenance rollout coordinated in CultureBotAI/culturebotai-claw#426.
title: Bind graph cache reuse to source bytes before issuing provenance

body:
Found reviewing #453, when the derived-artifacts manifest gained two rows reading `UNKNOWN  no writer found`.

Every category and source index under `data/normalized_yaml/` is classified that way, not only the new ones:

```
data/normalized_yaml/bacterial_index.json                     UNKNOWN  no writer found
data/normalized_yaml/by_source_komodo_index.json              UNKNOWN  no writer found
data/normalized_yaml/by_source_mediadive_index.json           UNKNOWN  no writer found
...
data/normalized_yaml/recipe_index.json                        CURRENT_VIEW  generate_recipe_indexes.py
data/normalized_yaml/recipe_statistics.json                   CURRENT_VIEW  generate_recipe_indexes.py
```

`recipe_index.json` and `recipe_statistics.json` are recognised because the generator names them literally; the category and source indexes are written from f-strings (`f"{category}_index.json"`, `f"by_source_{source.lower()}_index.json"` in `scripts/generate_recipe_indexes.py`), so `audit_derived_artifacts.py`'s writer search, which matches literal filenames in script text, never sees them. They are the same artifact family, produced by the same `just generate-indexes` run, and `tests/test_recipe_indexes.py` already freshness-checks them; the manifest just cannot say so.

This is a slice of the wider figure from the last triage: 51 of 98 tracked derived artifacts are `UNKNOWN`, and only 10 of 26 `CURRENT_VIEW` artifacts are freshness-checked.

Suggested: let the writer search match a filename pattern per writer (the generator's two f-string shapes here), or let a writer declare the artifacts it produces, so the twelve index files inherit `CURRENT_VIEW` and the generator as their writer. The manifest is regenerated by `just audit-derived-artifacts` and gated by `test_the_manifest_matches_a_fresh_computation`, so the change is one regeneration away from landing.
title: audit-derived-artifacts finds no writer for the twelve category and source indexes because the generator names them with f-strings

body:
Found reviewing #451, in the regenerated `data/normalized_yaml/*_index.json`.

`scripts/generate_recipe_indexes.py` reads the MediaRecipe shape only: `name`, `ingredients`, `sources`. A solution record keeps its label in `preferred_term`, its reagents in `composition`, and its provenance in `term.id`, so every one of them is indexed as nothing:

```json
"CultureMech:013364": {"name": null, "ingredient_count": 1, "source": "unknown", ...}
```

Measured on `76b245ddcb`, `bacterial_index.json`: **4,773 `mediadive_*` entries with `name: null`**, all 4,773 with `source: unknown`, and `ingredient_count: 1` on every one, which is the `See source for composition` placeholder (#444) counted as a reagent, not the 35,009 real rows. The record added in #451 carries no placeholder, so it indexes as `ingredient_count: 0` with two real reagents. `by_source_unknown_index.json` holds 5,998 entries; these are most of them.

So the indexes, which `docs/recipe_indexes.md` presents as the corpus's lookup surface, describe 30% of the corpus as unnamed, unsourced and empty.

Suggested: index a record by `preferred_term` when `name` is absent, count `composition` rows when `ingredients` holds only the placeholder or is absent, and derive the source from `term.id`'s prefix (`mediadive.solution:` → mediadive) when `sources` is empty. `tests/test_recipe_indexes.py` checks counts, not content; a case that a solution record indexes with a name and its reagent count would pin the fix.
title: The recipe indexes describe 4,773 solution records as unnamed, unsourced and empty: the generator reads only the MediaRecipe shape

body:
Found while validating a new record for #449.

`just validate-terms <file>` prints a success line whether or not the validator ran:

```
$ just validate-terms data/normalized_yaml/bacterial/mediadive_5059_Iron_III_citrate_solution.yaml
Validating ontology terms...
error: Failed to spawn: `linkml-term-validator`
  Caused by: No such file or directory (os error 2)
✓ Term validation passed
$ echo $?
0
```

The recipe (`project.justfile:1277`) is a bash block with no `set -e`, so the `uv run linkml-term-validator …` failure is swallowed and the trailing `echo` reports a pass with exit 0. `label-correspondence.yaml` already says the tool is dev-only and that CI uses `just validate-products` instead, so this is the local path only, but it is the one a curator runs on a single file, and it cannot tell them the check did not happen.

Two smaller things in the same recipe: it validates with `-t MediaRecipe`, so a `SolutionRecipe`-shaped record (the 4,784 MediaDive solutions, and the one above) would be checked against the wrong class even when the tool is present; and `validate-terms-all` next to it has the same shape.

Suggested: `set -euo pipefail` at the top of both recipes, and route the target class through `scripts/record_kinds.py`'s shape detection as `validate_strict` does.
title: just validate-terms reports a pass when linkml-term-validator is not installed

body:
Found sizing #374 against the MediaDive transform, and left out of #439 and #443 on purpose.

The MediaDive transform kg-microbe merges today carries a reagent's quantity in two typed edge columns:

```
subject  predicate  object  relation  primary_knowledge_source  knowledge_level  agent_type  value  unit
mediadive.solution:1  biolink:has_part  CHEBI:15377  BFO:0000051  infores:mediadive  observation  manual_agent  1000.0  ml
```

39,755 of its 48,434 `has_part` edges carry a `value`/`unit` pair. Our export packs the same fact into one qualifier string:

```
CultureMech:009646  biolink:has_part  MICRO:0000182  ...  concentration="10.0 G_PER_L"
```

A consumer that sums, converts, or filters by amount can read theirs directly and has to parse ours. When the export replaces the MediaDive transform (#374), every downstream reader of `value`/`unit` on a `has_part` edge loses the column.

Suggested: emit `value` and `unit` as edge columns from `concentration.value` / `concentration.unit` (unit as the enum token, which is already a closed set), keep the `concentration` qualifier for one release so nothing downstream breaks on the same day, and add the two columns to `_QUALIFIER_COLUMNS` and `kgx.yaml` so `tests/test_kgx_tsv_export.py::test_every_qualifier_type_the_transform_emits_has_a_column` covers them. With #443 in, 200,859 `has_part` edges carry a concentration today, so this is the largest single content difference left between the two exports.
title: has_part edges carry the quantity as one qualifier string; the MediaDive transform kg-microbe ingests carries value and unit columns

body:
Found while fixing #442.

Every one of the 4,774 MediaDive solution records carries, beside its real `composition`, an `ingredients` list of exactly one row:

```yaml
ingredients:
- preferred_term: See source for composition
  concentration:
    value: variable
    unit: VARIABLE
data_quality_flags:
- incomplete_composition
```

Measured on `main` at `4c9e47dac5`: 4,774 records, 4,774 placeholder rows, 0 grounded; the same records hold 35,009 grounded `composition` rows. The placeholder is the single string behind the `PLACEHOLDER` class in `just audit-ungrounded-ingredients` (4,775 rows, a third of everything that audit reports, #372 and #407), and the `incomplete_composition` flag on these records is false: their composition is complete, it is in the other list.

Consequences today:

- the ungrounded-ingredient backlog reads 4,775 rows larger than it is, and its ratchet (`--max-names 3217`) carries a name that is not an ingredient;
- `incomplete_composition` cannot be used to find records that are actually incomplete without first excluding these;
- any consumer that reads `ingredients` for a solution record sees "see source" and stops, which is how the exporter emitted nothing for them until #442.

Suggested: drop the placeholder row and the flag from records whose `composition` is non-empty (a bulk mutator; dry-run and a canary first), and have `validate_strict` or a corpus test refuse a placeholder ingredient beside a non-empty composition so the shape cannot return. The `SolutionRecipe` shape should not need an `ingredients` list at all; worth checking whether the importer wrote it to satisfy a MediaRecipe-shaped validator that no longer applies.
title: 4,774 MediaDive solution records carry a 'See source for composition' placeholder ingredient beside a complete composition, and are flagged incomplete

body:
Found reviewing #439.

#439 gives the 4,784 MediaDive solution records a node each. Their contents still do not reach the graph. `transform()` walks `ingredients[]` and `solutions[].composition[]`, and never a record's top-level `composition[]`, which is where a `SolutionRecipe`-shaped record keeps its reagents:

```
solution records with a top-level composition:   4,784
composition rows in them:                        35,009   (never walked)
solution records that are a has_part subject:    0 of 4,986
```

The other 202 solution records, the curated `record_kind: SOLUTION` ones with `MediaRecipe` shape, do go through `ingredients[]`; they emit nothing because none of the 202 carries a grounded ingredient, which is a curation gap rather than an exporter one.

So a solution node today is a labelled point with no composition, and a medium that references it by name gets no depth through it. For #374 this is the content that matters most: the MediaDive transform's 45,225 `solution → ingredient` edges are the bulk of its composition depth, and the corresponding rows are sitting in these records.

Two smaller things in the same area, both visible in #439's diff:

- 202 solution records carry a `medium_type`. `nodes()` types them `biolink:ChemicalMixture` (correct) and then still mints a `medium_type_*` node and a `has_attribute` edge for them, which is a medium's attribute on a mixture. Addressed in #439.
- `is_solution_record` in the exporter duplicates `scripts/record_kinds.py` (0 disagreements across 15,877 records today). A shared module under `src/` would stop them drifting.

Suggested: walk top-level `composition[]` for solution records with the existing `ingredient_to_edge`, carrying `value`/`unit` as #374 wants, and gate the export on the count of solution records that emit at least one `has_part` so the 0 above cannot come back.
title: Solution records mint a node but no composition: transform() never walks top-level composition, 35,009 rows

body:
Found reviewing #439, which keys record nodes on the record id and leaves nested solutions as the last name-keyed nodes in the export.

A solution nested inside a medium record (`solutions[]`) has no id of its own, so `_create_solution_id` mints `culturemech:solution_{sanitized preferred_term}` and node emission dedupes on that. Two media that nest a solution with the same name but a different composition share one node, and both compositions' `has_part` edges attach to it.

Measured on the corpus at `2dbbd042df`, fingerprinting each nested solution by its (ingredient id, value) set:

| | count |
|---|--:|
| distinct nested solution names | 1,566 |
| names carrying more than one distinct composition | **51** |
| `Vitamin solution` | 15 compositions |
| `Trace element solution` | 15 |
| `Trace elements solution` | 10 |

So `culturemech:solution_Vitamin_solution` is one node holding the union of fifteen different vitamin stocks, and a consumer reading its composition sees a solution that exists nowhere.

This is the same defect #438 fixed for records, one level down, and it was pre-existing. It is deliberately not folded into #439: the right id needs a decision. Two shapes:

1. **Scope to the parent**: `CultureMech:NNNNNN_solution_{name}` (or a `has_part` from the parent to a parent-suffixed node). One node per (medium, nested solution); a stock shared verbatim by 178 media becomes 178 nodes, which is what the corpus says today.
2. **Key on composition**: name plus a fingerprint of the composition, so identical stocks collapse and different ones do not. Mirrors `merge_recipes.unique_filename`. Closer to the truth, but the fingerprint moves whenever a grounding is repaired, so the id is not stable.

Where a nested solution is also a standalone solution record (the 4,784 MediaDive ones, and the `SOLUTION_NAME` class in `just audit-ungrounded-ingredients`), the best answer is neither: link the medium to the record's own `CultureMech:` id. That is the #372 residual and would remove most of the population here.

The `test_a_solution_shared_by_two_media_emits_its_composition_once` test in `tests/test_kgx_tsv_export.py` pins the current sharing behaviour for the identical-composition case and would need to say which of the above it means.
title: Nested solutions are still name-keyed: 51 names carry several compositions and merge into one node each

body:
Found reviewing #439.

After #439 the export emits record nodes as `CultureMech:NNNNNN` (the record's own id, whose schema pattern is `^CultureMech:(?!000000)\d{6}$`) while every auxiliary node it mints stays under `culturemech:` (`medium_type_*`, `application_*`, `state_*`, nested `solution_*`, and variants). The schema declares only one prefix:

```yaml
# src/culturemech/schema/culturemech.yaml:12
culturemech: https://w3id.org/culturemech/
```

So one namespace now travels under two CURIE prefixes that differ only in case. CURIE prefixes are case-sensitive to every consumer that matters here: kg-microbe's `prefixmap.json` declares neither today (#374), and when it registers one it will not resolve the other. `generate_sssom_mappings.py:35` mints a third population, `culturemech:Distilled_water`, for unmapped ingredients.

#439 kept the record id verbatim on purpose: it is the identifier `just check-id-catalog` pins and the one every other artifact in the repository spells that way, and inventing a lower-cased twin of a permanent id is its own hazard. But the split should be a decision, not an accident of history.

Options:
1. Declare `CultureMech` alongside `culturemech` in the schema prefixes, both expanding to `https://w3id.org/culturemech/`, and register both in kg-microbe under #374. Cheapest; leaves two spellings.
2. Move the auxiliary nodes to `CultureMech:` so the export uses one prefix. Touches docs and tests again; auxiliary ids are not permanent, so this is free.
3. Move record ids to `culturemech:` in the export only. Rejected above: two spellings of a permanent id.

Suggested: 2, then 1's kg-microbe registration for the single remaining prefix.
title: The KGX export now spans two CURIE prefixes for one namespace: CultureMech: for records, culturemech: for everything else

body:
Found while sizing #374 against the MediaDive transform it is meant to replace.

`kgx_export.py` mints every record's node id from the record **name**, and never reads the record's own `id`:

```python
# kgx_export.py:113 (transform) and :320 (nodes)
medium_id = f"culturemech:{_sanitize_id(str(record.get('name') or ''))}"
```

Node emission dedupes on that id (`koza_transform`, `_EMITTED_NODE_IDS`), so records that sanitize to the same string collapse into one node and their edges merge. Measured on `main` at `d954e1b618`:

| record kind | records | distinct node ids | collapsed |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| media | 10,891 | 7,710 | **3,181** |
| solutions | 4,986 | 199 | **4,787** |

The worst media case is 29 records on `culturemech:defined_freshwater_medium_coso4` (the #392 slugs). The solution case is structural: 4,784 MediaDive solution records carry `preferred_term` and no `name:` key, so `nodes()` returns early for all of them (`if not name: return`) and emits **no node**, while `transform()` still emits their `has_part` edges from the empty id `culturemech:`. The Aug 29 export shows 1,405 solution nodes against 4,986 records for this reason.

Two further consequences:

- A rename changes the node id, so the id is not stable across exports even though `CultureMech:NNNNNN` is permanent by repository rule and pinned by `just check-id-catalog`.
- Every one of the 15,877 records carries an `id`; none is missing (measured). The permanent identifier exists and is simply unused.

For #374 this is disqualifying: kg-microbe would ingest 7,909 nodes for 15,877 records and could not tell.

Suggested: key record nodes on the record's `id`, with the display label falling back from `name` to `preferred_term`. Auxiliary vocabulary nodes (`culturemech:medium_type_*`, `application_*`, `state_*`) are not records and can keep their spelling. Variant links (`culturemech:{variant_name}`) resolve to a *name*, so they need to resolve to the target record's id or they dangle once media nodes are id-keyed. Update `docs/KGX_SEMANTIC_MODEL.md`, whose examples show `culturemech:LB_Broth`.
title: KGX export keys node ids on the record name: 7,968 records collapse, and 4,784 solution records emit no node at all

body:
Two CI gates in this repository now demand opposite things of the same bytes.

- `scripts/check_vendored_sync.py` fails unless every vendored artifact is **byte-identical** to claw's canonical copy at the pinned revision.
- `scripts/check_changed_python.py` fails unless every **changed** Python file is ruff-clean and black-formatted.

A vendored file that changes is therefore required to be reformatted and required not to be. Re-vendoring `scripts/validate_id_label_correspondence.py` (claw#369, re-pinned in #436) hit it: three ruff findings under this repository's config in a file that cannot be edited here.

```
scripts/validate_id_label_correspondence.py:96:1   UP035  Import from `collections.abc` instead: `Iterator`
scripts/validate_id_label_correspondence.py:606:30 E741   Ambiguous variable name: `l`
scripts/validate_id_label_correspondence.py:612:17 E741   Ambiguous variable name: `l`
```

`EXCLUDED` already named `scripts/check_vendored_sync.py`, so the intent was understood -- but as one hand-written path, which held only while no *other* vendored file changed. Seven vendored Python files exist here and six were unlisted, each a latent instance of the same failure:

```
scripts/_edison_capture.py            tests/test_id_label_empty_adapter.py
scripts/chem_formula.py               tests/test_id_label_plausibility.py
scripts/deep_research_contract.py     tests/test_id_label_unknown_prefix.py
scripts/validate_id_label_correspondence.py  tests/test_provider_triage_contract.py
tests/test_curation_timestamp_schema.py      tests/test_skill_frontmatter.py
```

#436 lists all of them, which unblocks the re-pin and closes the six other holes. It is still a restatement: the authoritative set is claw's `vendored_artifacts.json`, the same manifest `check_vendored_sync.py` already reads, and a list that must be edited whenever a vendored artifact is added or removed will drift the way this one did.

## What to do

Derive the exclusion from the vendored manifest rather than restating it. `check_vendored_sync.py` already resolves the artifact set for this consumer at the pinned ref; exposing that set to `check_changed_python.py` keeps one source of truth. Failing that, a test asserting the literal set equals the manifest's Python artifacts would at least make the drift loud.

Worth noting the finding is *not* that the vendored file should be lint-clean. Its lint findings belong to claw, under claw's configuration; this repository has no standing to fix them and must not, because that would break byte-identity.
title: The changed-Python gate and the vendored-sync gate demand opposite things of the same file

body:
Found reviewing #431.

`CULTUREBOTHT_ROOT` names the *wrapper* directory, and the code appends the 
repository name to it:

```python
CULTUREBOTHT_ROOT = Path(os.environ.get("CULTUREBOTHT_ROOT", REPO_ROOT.parent / "CultureBotHT"))
...
default=CULTUREBOTHT_ROOT / "CultureBotHT",
```

The doubling is faithful to the real layout, which genuinely nests 
(`.../KG-Hub/KG-Microbe/CultureBotHT/CultureBotHT`), so this is a contract 
problem rather than a wrong path. The obvious reading of a variable called 
`<PROJECT>_ROOT` is "the root of that project". Anyone who sets it to the 
repository, which is the thing they actually have a path to, gets 
`<repo>/CultureBotHT` and a not-found error naming a directory one level below 
what they typed. The docstring explains the nesting, but the failure surfaces at 
the shell, not in the source.

The sibling default is separately dead under the current layout: the Mech 
checkouts moved to `.../ontology/Mechs/` on 2026-09-07, `CultureBotHT` is not 
among them, and it still sits under the old `KG-Hub/KG-Microbe/` tree. So the 
default resolves to nothing on this machine and the variable is the only working 
route, which makes its contract the whole interface.

Compare `COMMUNITYMECH_ROOT` in the same PR, which names the repository directly 
and appends only `data/embeddings`. The two new variables read the same and mean 
different things.

Nothing depends on the current spelling yet, since both variables ship in #431, 
so the contract is free to fix now and expensive later.

Suggested: let `CULTUREBOTHT_ROOT` name the repository, matching 
`COMMUNITYMECH_ROOT`, and keep the nesting only in the sibling fallback.
title: CULTUREBOTHT_ROOT names the wrapper directory while COMMUNITYMECH_ROOT names the repository

body:
Found reviewing #431.

Both new environment overrides use `os.environ.get(NAME, default)`. That default 
applies only when the variable is *absent*. Exported-and-empty is a distinct and 
common shell state, and it yields `Path("")`, which is `Path(".")`:

```
>>> os.environ['X'] = ''
>>> Path(os.environ.get('X', 'fallback'))
PosixPath('.')
>>> Path(os.environ.get('X', 'fallback')) / 'data' / 'embeddings'
PosixPath('data/embeddings')
```

So `COMMUNITYMECH_ROOT=` turns the embeddings fallback into a cwd-relative 
`data/embeddings/...`, and `CULTUREBOTHT_ROOT=` turns the importer default into 
`CultureBotHT/` under the cwd. Both then fail as "not found" pointing at a path 
the user never named, which is the confusing failure the sibling fallback exists 
to avoid. An empty export happens easily, e.g. `export COMMUNITYMECH_ROOT=$UNSET_VAR`.

Affected:
- `scripts/generate_ingredient_umap.py:38`
- `scripts/import_from_culturebotht.py:36`

Suggested: treat empty as absent, `os.environ.get(NAME) or default`.
title: An exported-but-empty COMMUNITYMECH_ROOT or CULTUREBOTHT_ROOT silently becomes the working directory

body:
Found reviewing #431.

`scripts/generate_ingredient_umap.py:29` keeps `_REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).parent.parent`, 
unresolved. The other two scripts the PR touched both use `.resolve()`:

| script | root |
|---|---|
| `export_mediadive_composition.py:20` | `Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent` |
| `import_from_culturebotht.py:33` | `Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent` |
| `generate_ingredient_umap.py:29` | `Path(__file__).parent.parent` |

Before #431 this did not matter: `_REPO_ROOT` was only joined downward, into the 
checkout, where an unresolved prefix is harmless. The PR makes it load-bearing 
*upward* by deriving a sibling from it:

```python
_COMMUNITYMECH_ROOT = Path(os.environ.get("COMMUNITYMECH_ROOT", _REPO_ROOT.parent / "CommunityMech"))
```

`_REPO_ROOT.parent` is the parent of wherever the symlink lives, not the parent of 
the real checkout, so under a symlinked checkout the sibling lookup searches the 
wrong directory and the embeddings fallback silently misses. Line 48 derives the 
claw workspace the same way and inherits it.

Suggested: add `.resolve()`, matching the two siblings.
title: generate_ingredient_umap derives a sibling checkout from an unresolved __file__

Found reviewing #424, in that PR's own change, before merge.

The first version of `tests/test_record_directories.py` grouped tracked records by their category directory and asserted every group name is a `CategoryEnum` value. It attributed a path by `parts[2]` and required `len(parts) >= 4`, so a record sitting **directly** under `data/normalized_yaml/` (three parts) fell out of the check without failing anything.

That location matters more than it looks. `validate-strict` and the ChEBI consistency audit use `rglob("*.yaml")` and would see such a record; but twelve scripts walk `*/*.yaml` (`git grep` count on `main`), including `audit-ungrounded-ingredients`, `audit-merged-duplicates`, the concentration-plausibility audit (per category directory) and `generate_recipe_indexes.py`. A stray top-level record would validate and then be missing from every audit's row count and from every index.

Fixed in #424 before merge: a fourth assertion lists tracked YAML at depth 3 and fails with the paths. Mutation-checked with an intent-to-add `data/normalized_yaml/probe.yaml`, which fails it by name.

One trap worth recording from doing that: `git ls-files -- 'data/normalized_yaml/*.yaml'` returns **all 15,877 records**, because `*` in a git pathspec matches across `/`. The depth filter has to be applied to the listing, not expressed in the pathspec.

Found reviewing #420 before merge.

`scripts/validate_claude_skills.py` now decides path existence with `git ls-files` and `git check-ignore`. Two paths in it assume more than the script checks:

1. **Outside a git checkout it dies with a traceback.** `_tracked_paths` runs `git ls-files -z` with `check=True`; in a directory that is not a repository (an sdist, a copied tree) that is `CalledProcessError: ... returned non-zero exit status 128`, not a validation error. Reproduced with `ROOT` pointed at a temp directory holding one skill.
2. **Only one error path survives a `SKILLS_DIR` outside `ROOT`.** #420 added `_display()` so the missing-path message does not raise `ValueError` from `Path.relative_to`, and the new tests rely on it. The other six messages (`use <skill>/SKILL.md layout`, `missing SKILL.md`, frontmatter errors, `missing version`, `name must match directory`) still call `relative_to(ROOT)` directly, so a test that exercises one of them through the same helper would crash the same way.

Neither affects the CI run, which always has a checkout and skills under `ROOT`. Both are the same shape: the script assumes an invariant it could state. Fixed in #420 by turning the git failure into a plain validation error and routing every message through `_display`.

Also noted, not a defect today: the "an ignore pattern reaches into this directory" rule reads only the root `.gitignore`. The repository has no nested ignore files (`git ls-files | grep '/\.gitignore$'` is empty), so nothing is missed; if one is ever added, the rule would not see it.
