body:
Found reviewing #378.

`repair_utex_ingredients.py` rewrites ingredients that already exist in a
record. It does not **add** rows the capture has and the record lacks, because
it iterates the record's ingredient list, not the capture's.

Measured against the fresh capture:

| | count |
|---|---|
| ingredients in the new UTEX capture | 510 |
| ingredients in the repaired records | 497 |
| **not represented in the corpus** | **13** |

The old fetcher dropped them because its guard was
`if ingredient and amount` — a row whose Amount cell was blank was discarded
entirely. The header-aware parser keeps them (a blank amount is a real state:
509 of 510 have an amount, one does not).

## Why it was left out of #378

Adding an ingredient is a different operation from repairing one. The repair
can prove every change it makes against a matched capture row; an insertion
has to decide where in the list the new entry goes and cannot be checked the
same way. Bundling it would have made the 497 verified repairs harder to
review.

## What is needed

Identify the 13, confirm each against its UTEX page, and insert with a
`curation_history` event. Small enough to check by hand.

Re-derive the list with:

```
uv run python -c "
import json,yaml
from pathlib import Path
raw={r['id']:r for r in json.load(open('data/raw/utex/utex_media.json'))['recipes']}
for f in sorted(Path('data/normalized_yaml').glob('*/*.yaml')):
    d=yaml.safe_load(f.read_text())
    uid=next((r['reference'].split(':',1)[1] for r in (d.get('references') or [])
              if isinstance(r,dict) and str(r.get('reference','')).startswith('UTEX:')), None)
    if uid in raw and len(raw[uid]['composition']) != len(d.get('ingredients') or []):
        print(f.name, len(d.get('ingredients') or []), '->', len(raw[uid]['composition']))
"
```

(requires a fresh `just fetch-utex` — the capture is gitignored)
title: The UTEX re-fetch captured 13 ingredients the records still do not have

body:
`tests/test_workflow_dependency_paths.py`, added in #375, discovers the
workflows it checks:

```python
for path in sorted(WORKFLOWS.glob("*.yaml")):
```

GitHub Actions accepts `.yml` and `.yaml` interchangeably, and `.yml` is the more
common convention in the wild — it is what most templates and generators emit.

All 10 workflows here are `.yaml` today, so this is latent rather than live:

```console
$ ls .github/workflows/ | sed 's/.*\.//' | sort | uniq -c
  10 yaml
```

## Why it is worth fixing rather than noting

The guard's whole purpose is to cover a workflow the moment it lands, rather
than requiring someone to remember to add it to a list. Discovery is the design.
A discovery rule that misses half the legal filenames re-introduces exactly the
gap it was written to close, and does it silently — the new `.yml` gate would be
unfiltered-for-dependencies, the guard would keep reporting 9 passed, and nothing
would say a workflow had been skipped.

It is also the same failure shape as the finding it guards against, one level up:
something looks covered because the thing checking it never looked.

`test_the_guard_is_not_vacuous` does not catch it either. It asserts a floor of 8
discovered blocks and the five known workflow names, all of which stay true when
an unseen `.yml` file is added.

## Fix

Glob both suffixes:

```python
paths = sorted({*WORKFLOWS.glob("*.yaml"), *WORKFLOWS.glob("*.yml")})
```

## Related limitation, not proposed for fixing here

The guard protects the dependency entries *inside* existing `paths:` blocks. It
does not pin the number of blocks, so deleting one from an existing workflow
removes a parametrised case and still passes. Pinning block counts would be
brittle against legitimate workflow changes, so this is recorded as a known
boundary rather than a defect.

Found while adversarially reviewing #375.
title: test_workflow_dependency_paths globs only *.yaml, so a .yml workflow would be silently unguarded

body:
kg-microbe has **no CultureMech transform**, and `culturemech:` appears in
neither `kg_microbe/transform_utils/prefixmap.json` nor `custom_curies.yaml`.
The only mentions anywhere in that repo are `NEXT_TASKS.md`, `docs/MAPPING_AUDIT.md`,
`scripts/consolidate_chemical_mappings.py` and one test — none of them an ingest.

So the export currently produces a well-formed graph that nothing consumes. All
9,375 nodes carry the `culturemech:` prefix.

## What would join, if anything ingested it

`database_reference_to_edge` emits **3,325 `biolink:same_as -> mediadive.medium:`**
edges. That is the whole bridge, and it is a decent one: it is derived from the
records' own source references rather than from a match heuristic.

## What does not join, and should be said out loud

`kg_microbe_match` — the field whose entire purpose is to name the corresponding
kg-microbe medium — **is never read by the export**. `grep kg_microbe_match
src/culturemech/export/kgx_export.py` returns nothing. 494 records carry one.

Given #286 (7 of 8 sampled `mediadive.medium:` values point at an unrelated
medium: LB -> THERMUS THERMOPHILUS MEDIUM, 119 records -> SOIL EXTRACT MEDIUM)
its absence from the export is currently protective. But it is protective by
accident, not by decision, and nothing records that. If #286 is fixed and someone
wires the field in, they will not find a note explaining why it was left out.

## Suggested work, in order

1. Decide with kg-microbe whether it wants a CultureMech ingest at all, or
   whether CultureMech's contribution should reach the graph by enriching the
   existing MediaDive media instead. That decision determines everything below.
2. If ingest: register the `culturemech:` prefix and add the transform there.
3. Either way, record in `kgx_export.py` why `kg_microbe_match` is not exported,
   linked to #286, so the omission is a documented decision rather than a gap.

The composition depth is the thing worth moving: 110,558 `has_part -> CHEBI`
edges is a real contribution that the graph does not have today.

Found while auditing whether the KGX export is ready for kg-microbe ingestion.
title: Nothing ingests the KGX export: kg-microbe has no CultureMech transform and no culturemech: prefix

body:
The export declares nodes only for the ids it mints, on the stated basis that
everything else comes from kg-microbe's ontology ingests:

> CHEBI, NCBITaxon, MICRO, FOODON and TOGO objects are supplied by KG-Microbe's
> ontology ingests, which carry the authoritative labels; minting
> half-populated rows for them here would put a competing, name-less node into
> the merge.

That reasoning is sound, and it holds for CHEBI, MICRO, NCIT, ENVO, UBERON, mesh
and cas. It does not hold for six prefixes that appear in **no** kg-microbe
prefixmap or constant.

## Measured

Object prefixes in the full-corpus export (163,864 edges), checked against
`kg_microbe/transform_utils/prefixmap.json`, `custom_curies.yaml` and
`transform_utils/constants.py` at `origin/master`:

| prefix | edges | known to kg-microbe |
|---|---:|---|
| CHEBI | 110,558 | yes |
| FOODON | 6,769 | **no** |
| komodo.medium | 3,637 | **no** |
| mediadive.medium | 3,325 | yes |
| MICRO | 3,622 | yes |
| TOGO | 2,917 | **no** |
| kgmicrobe.compound | 602 | yes |
| MEDIADB | 469 | **no** |
| ENVO | 293 | yes |
| cas | 222 | yes |
| NCIT | 202 | yes |
| kgmicrobe.ingredient | 156 | yes |
| jcm.grmd | 51 | **no** |
| mesh | 20 | yes |
| BTO | 2 | **no** |

**~13,845 edges** point at ids nothing in the merge will define. The comment's own
example list names FOODON and TOGO as covered; neither is.

## Two different problems in one bucket

- **FOODON and BTO** are real ontologies kg-microbe simply does not ingest.
  Either it should, or those 6,771 ingredient edges need remapping to something
  it does.
- **komodo.medium, TOGO, MEDIADB, jcm.grmd** are source-registry cross-references
  emitted as `biolink:same_as` by `database_reference_to_edge`. They are useful
  provenance, but as bare `same_as` targets with no node they are dangling by
  construction, not by oversight — nobody is ever going to ingest
  `jcm.grmd:`. These probably belong as node properties (`xref`) rather than
  edges.

## Suggested next step

Split the decision: confirm with kg-microbe whether FOODON is ingestible, and
separately decide whether registry cross-references should be edges at all. Then
either mint minimal nodes for what stays, or move it off the edge surface.

Found while auditing whether the KGX export is ready for kg-microbe ingestion.
title: ~13,845 KGX edges point at prefixes kg-microbe does not declare (FOODON, komodo.medium, TOGO, MEDIADB, jcm.grmd, BTO)

body:
`kgx_export.py` deliberately mints no ingredient nodes:

> We declare nodes for the six id shapes we mint and NOTHING else. CHEBI,
> NCBITaxon, MICRO, FOODON and TOGO objects are supplied by KG-Microbe's ontology
> ingests, which carry the authoritative labels.

That is right for *grounded* ingredients. It leaves nothing for ungrounded ones,
and kg-microbe models them explicitly —
`kg_microbe/transform_utils/constants.py`:

```python
INGREDIENT_CATEGORY = "biolink:ChemicalEntity"          # Generic chemical, use only when ontology ID unknown
COMPLEX_INGREDIENT_CATEGORY = "biolink:ComplexMolecularMixture"  # peptone, yeast extract, etc.
```

So the consumer has a category reserved for exactly the case we drop.

## Measured

```
ingredient rows across ingredients[], composition[], solutions[].composition[]
  total       208,130
  with an id  183,813  (88.3%)
  ungrounded   24,317  (11.7%)
```

Every one of those 24,317 hits `if not chem_id: return None` in
`medium_to_ingredient_edge` / `solution_to_ingredient_edge` and disappears — no
node, no edge, no counter, no line in any report. The export prints its node and
edge totals and nothing about what it declined to emit.

## Why it matters

- A medium whose composition is half ungrounded exports as a medium with half a
  composition, and looks complete. Nothing downstream can tell the difference
  between "this medium has 4 ingredients" and "this medium has 9, of which we
  could ground 4."
- It is silent by construction, so the number can drift in either direction and
  no gate moves. 11.7% is measured today; nothing pins it.
- The complex-ingredient case is the one kg-microbe most wants from us — peptone,
  yeast extract and their kin are exactly what `COMPLEX_INGREDIENT_CATEGORY`
  exists for, and exactly what resists CHEBI grounding.

## Options

1. **Mint `biolink:ChemicalEntity` nodes** for ungrounded ingredient names, keyed
   on a sanitized `culturemech:ingredient_<name>` id, matching what kg-microbe
   would do. Preserves the composition, at the cost of ids that carry no ontology
   commitment.
2. **Report but do not emit** — add the drop count and a per-name breakdown to the
   export summary and a ratchet, so the loss is visible and bounded even if we
   decide not to publish the nodes.
3. **Both**, which is probably right: emit the nodes and gate the count, so the
   graph is complete and grounding progress is measurable.

Whichever we pick, the current behaviour — dropping 11.7% of the corpus's
composition with no signal — should not be the one we keep by default.

Found while auditing whether the KGX export is ready for kg-microbe ingestion.
title: KGX export silently drops 24,317 ungrounded ingredient rows (11.7%), which kg-microbe has a category for

body:
`just kgx-export` — the tracked full-corpus recipe — fails immediately:

```console
$ just kgx-export
ValueError: Cannot open local or remote file:
  .../CultureMech/src/culturemech/export/data/normalized_yaml/algae/1_1_dyiii_pea_gr_medium.yaml
  Check the URL/path, and that the file exists, and try again.
error: recipe `kgx-export` failed on line 1702 with exit code 1
```

Note the path: `src/culturemech/export/` + `data/normalized_yaml/...`. koza resolves
record paths relative to the **config file's** directory
(`src/culturemech/export/kgx.yaml`), not the working directory. The justfile
passes the relative default:

```
normalized_yaml_dir := "data/normalized_yaml"
```

With an absolute path it works:

```console
$ uv run --extra koza python scripts/export_kgx.py \
    --records-dir "$PWD/data/normalized_yaml" --output-dir "$PWD/output/kgx"
Reading 15877 records from /Users/.../data/normalized_yaml
✓ KGX export complete: 9,375 nodes, 163,864 edges
```

## Why nothing caught it

`just kgx-export-sample` passes for the wrong reason — it builds its records dir
with `mktemp -d`, which is absolute:

```
tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
cp -r "{{normalized_yaml_dir}}/{{category}}" "$tmp/"
... --records-dir "$tmp"
```

So the canary recipe exercises a path the real recipe never takes. That is the
worst arrangement available: the sample greens up, and the thing it is supposed
to de-risk is broken.

No workflow runs the export either — `tests.yaml` syncs `--extra koza` so
`tests/test_kgx_export.py` runs, but nothing invokes the corpus export, so CI
could not have noticed.

## Fix

Resolve `--records-dir` and `--output-dir` to absolute paths in
`scripts/export_kgx.py` before handing them to koza, so the recipe works from
any working directory and the sample and full paths behave identically. A
regression test should drive the driver with a relative path.

Found while auditing whether the KGX export is ready for kg-microbe ingestion.
title: just kgx-export is broken: koza resolves --records-dir against the config file's directory, not the CWD

body:
#365's commit message and PR body both state that bumping oaklib forces linkml
1.9.4 -> 1.11.1, and that "the two move together or neither moves." That is
stronger than the truth, and MediaIngredientMech is the counterexample.

## What is actually true

The click cap was introduced in linkml **1.9.4**, and only exists in the 1.9.x
line at that version:

| linkml | click constraint |
|---|---|
| 1.9.3 | `click>=7.0` — **no upper bound** |
| 1.9.4 | `click<8.2,>=8.0` |
| 1.11.1 | `click>=8.2` |

oaklib >=0.7.3 requires `llm`, which pulls `sqlite-utils>=4.0` -> `click>=8.3.1`.
So what was unavoidable was moving **off linkml 1.9.4** — not moving *up*.
Downgrading to 1.9.3 was a third option I did not test and did not mention.

MediaIngredientMech's `origin/main` proves it resolves: `linkml>=1.7.0,<1.10`
alongside `oaklib>=0.7.2`, and its lock holds linkml **1.9.3**, click **8.3.1**,
llm 0.33, sqlite-utils 4.2.1, oaklib 0.7.4 — all consistent.

## Why this matters beyond the wording

The forced linkml jump is the whole reason #365 also carries regenerated
dataclasses and a regenerated JSON schema. Had linkml stayed at 1.9.3, the PR
would have been the pin-only change the scope actually asked for.

I am not proposing to revert. linkml 1.11.1 is current, all 7 checks passed on
3.10 and 3.14, `just test` is green at 1691 passed, and the regenerated diffs
were verified to be generator-only. Moving forward is defensible — it just was
not *forced*, and the record should not claim it was.

## What to do

- Correct the claim here, so the next dependency decision starts from the real
  constraint (`linkml != 1.9.4` when oaklib >= 0.7.3), not a false one.
- Note the fleet is now split: CultureMech and TraitMech on linkml >=1.11.1,
  MediaIngredientMech capped `<1.10` for an independent reason (linkml-runtime
  1.10 dropped `Format.JSON`, breaking `linkml-validate` startup). That split is
  deliberate on MIM's side but nobody has written down that it is intentional
  across the fleet.

Found while extending the #362 sweep to the sibling repos.
title: #365 overstates the linkml coupling: only 1.9.4 caps click, so the upgrade was not forced

body:
None of CultureMech's four gate workflows watch `pyproject.toml` or `uv.lock`:

```bash
for w in validate-strict chebi-consistency concentration-plausibility label-correspondence; do
  n=$(sed -n '/paths:/,/^[a-z]/p' .github/workflows/$w.yaml | grep -cE "pyproject|uv\.lock")
  echo "  $w: $n"
done
#   validate-strict: 0
#   chebi-consistency: 0
#   concentration-plausibility: 0
#   label-correspondence: 0
```

So a pure dependency change cannot trigger the gates that a dependency change is
most likely to break. `label-correspondence` is the sharpest case: it runs the
OAK id↔label check and caches `~/.data/oaklib`, so it is the gate that would
notice an oaklib regression — and it is the one a lockfile edit cannot start.

## This nearly bit us in #365

#365 bumped oaklib and it looked well covered — 7 checks, all green. But the
gates ran only because the linkml upgrade forced regenerated schema artifacts,
and `src/culturemech/schema/**` *is* in the filters. Had the scope stayed
"oaklib pin only" as originally intended, the same PR would have run `tests.yaml`
(no path filter) and nothing else.

That is a coincidence standing in for a gate.

## The fleet already found this twice

- MediaIngredientMech#495 — "Dependency bumps cannot trigger the oaklib-heavy CI
  gates: uv.lock and pyproject.toml are outside every path filter"
- TraitMech#566 — "label-correspondence's paths filter excludes pyproject.toml
  and uv.lock, so the blocking OAK gate never runs on a dependency change"

Filing here for parity; the fix is presumably the same in all three.

## Fix

Add `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` to the `paths:` list of each gate workflow.
Cheap, and it makes the dependency-change path exercise the same gates as a
corpus change.

Worth checking at the same time whether this interacts with #277 (path filters
see only the first 300 changed files) — a dependency bump is small, so the 300
limit is not the binding constraint here, but the two share a mechanism.

Found while extending the #362 oaklib sweep to the sibling repos.
title: Dependency changes cannot trigger any corpus gate: pyproject.toml and uv.lock are in no workflow's paths filter

body:
Found while reviewing #365.

`pyproject.toml` L136 carries a pytest warning filter scoped to a module in `funowl`:

```toml
"ignore:Failing to pass a value to the 'type_params'.*:DeprecationWarning:funowl\\.terminals\\.TypingHelper",
```

#365 **removes `funowl` from `uv.lock`** — it was a transitive dependency that the
linkml 1.9.4 -> 1.11.1 bump drops:

```
funowl in main lock : 1
funowl in #365 lock : 0
```

The filter becomes dead config. It is harmless — pytest matches the `module` field as a
regex against a warning's origin and does not require the module to be importable, so
nothing errors. But it is a rule that can never fire again, and stale entries in a
`filterwarnings` list are exactly the kind of thing that accumulates until nobody is
willing to touch the list.

Worth removing in a follow-up sweep of that block rather than blocking #365.

## Related, smaller

#365's description enumerates the dropped transitive packages as "`yamllint`, `funowl`,
`stringcase`, `bcp47`, `distro`". The actual set is those **plus `path`**:

```
bcp47  distro  funowl  path  stringcase  yamllint
```

The PR's conclusion is unaffected — I checked, and `path` is not imported anywhere in
`scripts/`, `src/` or `tests/`, nor invoked as a CLI tool outside Python. Recording it
only so the audit trail matches what actually changed.
title: Stale pytest filterwarnings entry for funowl, which #365 removes from the lock

body:
Found while reviewing #365.

`src/culturemech/schema/culturemech.schema.json` on `main` contains **two `$ref`s to
`#/$defs/Term`, but never defines `Term`.**

```
$ git show origin/main:src/culturemech/schema/culturemech.schema.json | grep -c '"#/\$defs/Term"'
2
# ... and 'Term' is absent from $defs (90 definitions, none named Term)
```

Both sites are the `term` slot (around L3012 and L3199 of the generated file). Against a
strict JSON Schema validator that resolves references, this file does not load — the
schema is unusable for exactly the validation it exists to provide.

## Status: incidentally fixed, not deliberately

#365 regenerates the artifacts under linkml 1.11.1 (metamodel 1.7.0 -> 1.11.0), and the
newer generator emits the abstract base classes 1.9 omitted. `Term` is now defined, so
the dangling reference resolves. I confirmed the structural diff is otherwise clean:

- **0** keys removed
- **1** key changed (`metamodel_version`)
- 21 added (the `Term` and `Descriptor` definitions, plus `format: "uri"` on two slots)

So #365 repairs this as a side effect of a dependency bump. Nobody set out to fix it,
and **nothing stops it coming back** — the next generator change that drops a base class
reintroduces a silently broken schema.

## Suggested guard

A test that loads the generated schema and asserts every `$ref` resolves. Roughly:

```python
refs = {r for r in walk(schema) if r.startswith("#/$defs/")}
missing = {r for r in refs if r.split("/")[-1] not in schema["$defs"]}
assert not missing, f"dangling $ref(s): {sorted(missing)}"
```

`tests/test_dataclasses_current.py` already guards artifact *staleness*; this guards
artifact *internal consistency*, which is a different failure and the one that actually
bit here.

Note `Descriptor` is now defined but referenced zero times — harmless dead output from
the same generator, not worth chasing, but it means "defined" and "referenced" are worth
checking as separate properties.
title: Nothing guards the generated JSON schema against a dangling $ref (the Term one is fixed)

body:
#365 moves `oaklib` to `>=0.7.3` so `sqlite:obo:` selectors resolve against
`https://semanticsql.berkeleybop.io` instead of the raw S3 bucket upstream is
retiring. Nothing in the repo defends that.

## What can silently undo it

- A future `uv lock` that resolves oaklib lower — the declared floor is the only
  thing stopping it, and nothing asserts the lock agrees with the floor.
- Someone widening the floor back toward `>=0.5.0` while chasing an unrelated
  resolution conflict. The old value survived from before the CDN existed and
  nothing marked it as load-bearing.
- The failure is invisible until the bucket goes away: on 0.6.23 everything
  still *works* today, so no test, no gate and no error message distinguishes a
  correct pin from a reverted one until it breaks everywhere at once.

There is no runtime signal either — `SEMSQL_SQLITE_URL_BASE` is read once at
import and the wrong value just produces a different download URL.

## The repo already has the pattern

`tests/test_deep_research_client_pin.py` exists for exactly this shape, and its
docstring names the reason:

> It was found six releases stale at 0.2.4 … That is the wrong moment to
> discover it.

It asserts two things — that the declared floor is high enough, and that
`test_the_lockfile_agrees_with_the_floor`, because "a floor the lock does not
satisfy is a floor in name only."

## Proposed fix

The same two assertions for oaklib, plus a third that is cheap here and pins the
actual property rather than a proxy: import `SEMSQL_SQLITE_URL_BASE` and assert
it is not the S3 host. That last one keeps working even if upstream renames the
constant's default again.

The floor is 0.7.3 rather than the 0.7.2 that introduced the CDN, because 0.7.2
declares `requires_python <3.14` and this project supports `<3.15` with 3.14 in
the CI matrix. A test is the right place to record that, since the reason is not
visible from the version number.

Found while adversarially reviewing #365.
title: Nothing pins the oaklib floor, so the semantic-sql CDN fix can be silently reverted

body:
Found in the adversarial review of #363, which retires the `manage-ingredient-hierarchy` skill.

Deleting that skill left **five** references to it. `tests/test_markdown_links.py` caught **one** — the only one written as a markdown link:

```markdown
- [`manage-ingredient-hierarchy`](../manage-ingredient-hierarchy/SKILL.md) — MediaIngredientMech integration
```

The other four were bare backtick mentions and passed every gate:

| file | shape |
|---|---|
| `CLAUDE.md:117` | prose list of grounding skills |
| `.claude/skills/next-tasks/SKILL.md:129` | hand-off list |
| `.claude/skills/create-recipe/SKILL.md:438` | "related skills" list |
| `.claude/skills/generate-ingredient-umap/SKILL.md:139` | cross-reference |

All five are fixed in #363. The gap is that only one shape is checked, and `CLAUDE.md` — the file agents read first — is exactly the kind of place the unchecked shape lives.

## This generalises

Bare mentions are the *dominant* form, not an exception. Counting `` `skill-name` `` occurrences across markdown:

```
8  manage-identifiers
7  match-kg-microbe
7  audit-schema-gaps
5  review-recipes
5  deep-research-medium
5  create-recipe
3  id-label-correspondence
2  scrape-jcm-media
```

So renaming or retiring any skill leaves a similar trail, and the count above is what a future retirement has to find by hand.

## Fix

Extend the markdown guard: collect the set of directories under `.claude/skills/`, then assert that every `` `name` `` in markdown which *looks* like a skill reference resolves to one.

The matching rule needs a little care — a backticked token is not necessarily a skill name — so the cheap version is to check only tokens that match an existing-or-recently-deleted skill naming pattern (`kebab-case`, contains a hyphen) and are listed in a "related skills"/hand-off context. A stricter alternative is to require skill cross-references to be markdown links, which makes the existing test sufficient and needs no new matching heuristics; that is a docs-convention change rather than a test change.

I'd take the second: it makes one guard cover both shapes instead of adding a fuzzier second guard.
title: Bare skill mentions are unvalidated: deleting a skill leaves 4 of 5 references dangling

body:
`uv.lock` pins **oaklib 0.6.23**, which resolves `sqlite:obo:` selectors against the raw
S3 bucket that INCATools/semantic-sql is about to lock down. This repo needs to move to
oaklib >= 0.7.2 before that happens.

## Background

INCATools/semantic-sql is retiring public access to the raw S3 bucket that serves the
pre-built semantic-sql SQLite databases:

- INCATools/semantic-sql#112 — "Eliminate S3 bucket access" (open)
- INCATools/semantic-sql#110 — vendor-neutral URL (closed, delivered)
- INCATools/semantic-sql#115 — migrating direct raw-S3 consumers (open)

Traffic analysis in #112 shows the remaining raw-bucket load is dominated by
Python `urllib` from cloud CI on **OAK <= 0.7.1** — the pre-0.7.2 raw-S3 code path.
When `AllUsers` is removed from the bucket, those consumers break.

## The mechanism

oaklib **>= 0.7.2** changed the default in `src/oaklib/constants.py`:

```python
SEMSQL_SQLITE_URL_BASE = os.environ.get(
    "OAKLIB_SEMSQL_SQLITE_URL_BASE", "https://semanticsql.berkeleybop.io"
)
```

Below 0.7.2 the `sqlite:obo:` selector resolves against
`https://s3.amazonaws.com/bbop-sqlite`. At or above 0.7.2 it resolves against the CDN,
with `OAKLIB_SEMSQL_SQLITE_URL_BASE` available as an escape hatch for a mirror.

## Current state in this repo

| | value |
|---|---|
| `uv.lock` | `oaklib` **0.6.23** |
| `pyproject.toml` L35 | `"oaklib>=0.5.0"` |
| `.py` files importing oaklib | 13 (`get_adapter`) |
| `sqlite:obo:` selectors | `conf/id_label_targets.yaml` (CHEBI, NCBITaxon, ENVO, UBERON, NCIT, FOODON) |
| hardcoded raw-bucket URLs | none found |

## Gotcha specific to this repo

**`oaklib>=0.7.2` alone is not enough here.** The CI matrix in `.github/workflows/`
tests Python **3.14**, but oaklib 0.7.2 declares `requires_python <3.14`. Only 0.7.3
widened it to `<3.15`. Resolving the floor at 0.7.2 on the 3.14 job will fail.

Latest stable is **0.7.4** (2026-08-03), `requires_python >=3.10,<3.15` — covers the
whole 3.10-3.14 matrix.

## Proposed change

1. `pyproject.toml`: `"oaklib>=0.5.0"` -> `"oaklib>=0.7.2"`
2. `uv lock --upgrade-package oaklib` (expected to land 0.7.4)
3. Run the test suite — the API surface in use is small (`get_adapter`,
   `datamodels.vocabulary`), but 0.6.23 -> 0.7.4 is a minor-version jump and warrants
   a real run rather than a lockfile-only change.

## Verification

After the bump, confirm the resolved default rather than trusting the version number:

```bash
uv run python -c "from oaklib.constants import SEMSQL_SQLITE_URL_BASE; print(SEMSQL_SQLITE_URL_BASE)"
# expect: https://semanticsql.berkeleybop.io
```

Filed as part of a three-repo sweep; CultureMech, MediaIngredientMech and TraitMech all
pin 0.6.23 identically.
title: Bump oaklib to >=0.7.2 (0.7.4) — raw S3 bucket for semantic-sql is being retired

body:
`project.justfile` hardcodes the gate before passing arguments through:

```
audit-mim-sssom *args="":
    uv run --extra dev python scripts/audit_mim_sssom_divergence.py \
        --max-divergent 5 --max-split 44 {{args}}
```

so the documented investigative flag from #338 runs straight into the gate:

```console
$ just audit-mim-sssom --match-synonyms
FAIL: 84 divergent names > baseline 5. A new grounding disagrees with MIM's
published SSSOM; reconcile it or agree the change with MIM.
exit 1
```

Both halves of that are wrong. No new grounding was introduced — the corpus is
byte-identical to the run that passes. The flag widened what the audit can *see*
from 14.5% to 29.5% of names, and the baselines were calibrated against
label-only matching. So the message accuses the curator of a change they did not
make and points them at a reconciliation that is not needed.

The failure is quiet in the bad direction too: `--match-synonyms` through `just`
looks like the gate caught something real, which is exactly the reading that
would prompt someone to "fix" it by raising the baseline to 84 — permanently
destroying a gate that is currently doing its job at 5.

## Proposed fix

The two are incompatible by construction, so make that explicit rather than
leaving it to the message. Refuse to run a gate together with `--match-synonyms`
and say why: baselines are calibrated for label-only matching, and the flag is
for investigation, not for gating. A curator who wants both numbers runs the
gate and the investigation as two commands.

Found while adversarially reviewing #338.
title: just audit-mim-sssom --match-synonyms fails the gate and blames a grounding change that never happened

body:
`load_sssom`'s docstring on `fix/mim-synonym-matching-304` bakes in a measured
breakdown:

>     47 names (3,227 rows)  differ only in hydration state
>      3 names   (709 rows)  differ only in stereochemistry
>     24 names   (924 rows)  substantive

and the surrounding prose says "the 74 extra DIVERGENT names". Re-measured today
against the same MIM SSSOM (`mapping_set_version: 2026-08-18`) and current
`main`:

| | in the docstring | measured today |
|---|---:|---:|
| extra DIVERGENT names | 74 | **79** |
| hydration-only | 47 / 3,227 rows | **49 / 3,744** |
| stereochemistry-only | 3 / 709 rows | 3 / **547** |
| substantive | 24 / 924 rows | **27 / 4,198** |

The corpus moved underneath the numbers — #348 (pinned MIM label index) and #349
(media content remediation) both landed after they were taken. The row counts
are the worst of it: the substantive bucket is off by 4.5x.

This is the same defect class as #356, in a different file: a durable artifact
asserting a transient measurement with no date and no way to notice it has
rotted. Someone reading this docstring in three months will quote 74 and be
wrong, and nothing will tell them.

## What does not need changing

The *argument* is unaffected and still holds. The extra findings are still
dominated by hydration-state differences, and the decisive case is still true —
re-verified today:

```
   233  Potassium dihydrogen phosphate  ours=potassium dihydrogen phosphate  mim=calcium sulfate dihydrate
```

That is still the reason the flag stays opt-in, and it is still unambiguous and
still wrong (MediaIngredientMech#464).

## Proposed fix

Date-stamp the measurement, or replace the exact counts with the shape that does
not rot ("roughly doubles coverage; the extra findings are dominated by
hydration-state differences, with a minority substantive"). Keep the
`Potassium dihydrogen phosphate` case in full, since it is an argument rather
than a statistic.

Found while adversarially reviewing #338.
title: load_sssom docstring's divergence breakdown is already stale (74 vs 79 names; row counts off by up to 4.5x)

body:
`scripts/audit_mim_sssom_divergence.py` on `fix/mim-synonym-matching-304` adds
two filters over MIM's `other` column, and #338's body presents them under the
heading "Two filters that mattered":

```python
_CAS_TOKEN = re.compile(r"^cas\s*:", re.IGNORECASE)
_TRAIT_TOKEN = re.compile(
    r"^(?:produces|degradation|hydrolysis|reduction|oxidation|utilizes"
    r"|electron\s+(?:acceptor|donor)|(?:carbon|nitrogen|sulfur|energy)\s+source"
    r"|aerobic\s+catabolization|anaerobic\s*\w*|fermentation|assimilation"
    r"|respiration)\s*:",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
```

Neither changes a single finding. Running the full audit against the current
corpus with both filters disabled produces byte-identical results:

```
with both filters   : {'INTERNAL_SPLIT': 44, 'MISSING_GROUNDING': 132, 'DIVERGENT': 84} matched_names=1046
with NEITHER filter : {'INTERNAL_SPLIT': 44, 'MISSING_GROUNDING': 132, 'DIVERGENT': 84} matched_names=1046
```

## Why they are unreachable

The filters drop 1,727 CAS tokens and 50 trait tokens, but a dropped token can
only matter if it would otherwise have matched one of our ingredient names. It
cannot. The trait prefix is part of the token, so `carbon source: acetate`
normalizes to `carbon source acetate` — which is not, and will never be, an
ingredient name in this corpus. Same for `cas: 7447-40-7`. Measured directly:

```
alias index size: with trait filter=9664  without=9710  delta=46
leaked trait tokens that MATCH one of our ingredient names: 0
```

The real protection is elsewhere and is doing all the work: an alias mapping to
more than one CHEBI id is dropped, and a label always beats an alias.

## Why it is worth fixing rather than shrugging at

`_TRAIT_TOKEN` is a hand-maintained vocabulary of MIM's trait prefixes. It has
to be kept in sync with a column in another repository, and nothing here will
ever fail if it falls out of sync — the same dead-code-with-a-false-guarantee
shape as the `reset_node_dedup()` removal in #333. Presenting it as load-bearing
is worse than the code itself, because the next person reads "filtered" and
stops looking.

Related: `_CAS_TOKEN` anchors at `^`, so an embedded marker survives —
`KCl(CAS: 7447-40-7)` is indexed as the alias `kcl(cas`. Five such tokens exist
today. Harmless for the same reason the rest is, but it shows the filter tests
token *shape* and cannot see content.

## Proposed fix

Keep the filters — MIM#464 shows `other` is genuinely contaminated and the
column's shape is not stable, so the guard encodes real intent — but stop
claiming they matter. State the measured reachability with its date, and pin it
with a test so the claim cannot quietly become false again. Report the filter
yield (kept vs dropped) alongside the coverage line, so blocklist rot is visible
instead of requiring a one-off script to detect.

Found while adversarially reviewing #338.
title: MIM audit's CAS and trait alias filters change no finding, but #338 presents them as load-bearing

body:
`.claude/skills/review-open-issues/SKILL.md` Step 1 ends:

> Read every issue body and its comments; for a long queue, inspect related
> groups **in parallel** but preserve one disposition per issue.

Carried over verbatim from MicroGrowLink. "In parallel" is unqualified, and the
most natural reading for an agent is to fan out subagents over issue groups.

That is the wrong default here:

- Subagent fan-out is opt-in in this org's sessions, not something a skill
  should authorize implicitly.
- The queue is small — 20 open issues as measured today — so the cost the
  sentence exists to manage is not present. Fan-out would spend more than the
  sweep it accelerates.
- Fanning out actively undermines the skill's own core convention. The
  dependency graph in Step 2 and the duplicate grouping in Step 2 both need one
  reader holding the whole queue at once. Split across agents, each sees its
  own group and none can rank across them — which is exactly the first-page
  sampling the skill forbids, arriving by a different route.

## Proposed fix

Say what the parallelism is: batching independent `gh`/`git` calls in one
round, not spawning agents. Or drop the clause — at this queue size it buys
nothing and only creates the ambiguity.

Found while adversarially reviewing #354.
title: review-open-issues says to inspect issue groups 'in parallel' without saying what that means

body:
The port in #354 replaced CultureMech's v1.0.0 Step 2 ("Group and dedupe") with
MicroGrowLink's one-line version. Two concrete pieces of guidance were lost.

## 1. The grouping criteria

v1.0.0 named how to decide that two issues are the same finding:

> Issues filed from the same review pass (same PR, same session) often overlap —
> several may describe the same root cause from different angles. Group by:
> - shared PR/commit reference in the title or body,
> - same file/function named,
> - near-identical failure scenario.
>
> Note groups explicitly in the report; do not silently merge them (a human may
> want to close duplicates deliberately, not have them hidden).

The new text keeps only "Group issues that share a root cause, but do not hide
the individual issue numbers." That preserves the *rule* and drops the *test*.

This matters more here than the generic wording suggests: this repository's
queue is largely filed in batches by adversarial review passes, so the
same-PR-reference and same-file heuristics are the ones that actually fire.

## 2. The closure command

v1.0.0 Step 6 gave the exact mutation, so that an authorized close is executed
consistently with its evidence attached:

```bash
gh issue close <N> --comment "<reason>"
```

The new Mutation boundary section states the policy (one at a time, cited
evidence, no unattended bulk close) but no longer shows the command.

## Proposed fix

Restore both into the new structure — the criteria as a short list under Step 2,
the command in the Mutation boundary section. Neither conflicts with anything
the port added.

Found while adversarially reviewing #354.
title: review-open-issues port dropped the dedupe criteria and the issue-close command from v1.0.0

body:
`.claude/skills/review-open-issues/SKILL.md` Step 3 says:

> A committed report under `data/import_tracking/reports/` is derived and can
> lag; `data/merge_yaml/` is derived from `data/normalized_yaml/` and **is
> currently drifted**.

"Currently" was true when written — `project.justfile`'s `audit-merge-freshness`
comment records the layer as drifted. But the skill's own Conventions section
says state claims rot ("Titles are claims and they drift", "The queue moves
during the sweep"), and this is a durable document asserting a transient fact
with no expiry.

The failure is asymmetric. If the drift is repaired and the sentence stays, a
triager reads "currently drifted" and discounts a `merge_yaml` number that is
now correct — or, worse, treats a *fresh* drift report as already-known
background instead of a new regression.

## Proposed fix

Name the check instead of the outcome: point at `just audit-merge-freshness`
and let the run decide. The general rule the sentence is teaching — derived
layers can lag their source, so verify before quoting — holds regardless of
today's answer, and survives the fix.

Same treatment for the `data/import_tracking/reports/` half, which is already
phrased correctly as "can lag" rather than "is stale".

Found while adversarially reviewing #354.
title: review-open-issues bakes a transient 'currently drifted' state claim into a durable skill

body:
`.claude/skills/review-open-issues/SKILL.md` Step 4 ends with:

> Prefer the gates over prose as evidence: `just validate-strict`,
> `just assign-ids-check`, `just audit-derived-artifacts`,
> `just audit-unparsed-composition`, `just audit-concentration-plausibility`,
> `just check-chebi-grounding`, `just check-mim-label-index`, and
> `just audit-merge-freshness`. An issue asserting a defect that one of these
> already blocks is P2 unless it shows the gate is porous.

Five of those eight do not block anything. Measured against
`.github/workflows/` on `docs/adapt-review-open-issues-skill`:

| recipe | workflow | trigger |
|---|---|---|
| `validate-strict` | validate-strict.yaml, tests.yaml | pull_request |
| `audit-concentration-plausibility` | concentration-plausibility.yaml | pull_request |
| `check-chebi-grounding` | chebi-consistency.yaml, concentration-plausibility.yaml | pull_request |
| `audit-merge-freshness` | merge-yaml-freshness.yaml | **schedule only** |
| `assign-ids-check` | — | **none** |
| `audit-derived-artifacts` | — | **none** |
| `audit-unparsed-composition` | — | **none** |
| `check-mim-label-index` | — | **none** |

`merge-yaml-freshness.yaml` says so in its own header comment: "This runs on a
schedule, NOT as a blocking per-PR gate." The other four appear in no workflow
file at all — they only run when a human types the command.

## Why it matters

The rule downgrades an issue to P2 on the strength of a gate that never fires.
The four ungated recipes cover ID collisions, derived-artifact drift, unparsed
composition reaching the graph, and the pinned MIM label index — four of the
repository's most consequential invariants, and precisely the ones where a
silent regression is hardest to notice later.

So the skill would take a live defect in an unguarded area and rank it *below*
a documentation issue, citing a check that did not run.

## Proposed fix

Split the list by what actually blocks a PR, and scope the P2 downgrade to the
blocking set. The on-demand audits stay listed as the cheapest decisive
evidence a triager can run — just not as proof the defect is contained.

## Verification

```bash
for r in validate-strict assign-ids-check audit-derived-artifacts \
         audit-unparsed-composition audit-concentration-plausibility \
         check-chebi-grounding check-mim-label-index audit-merge-freshness; do
  hits=$(grep -rln -- "$r" .github/workflows/ | tr '\n' ' ')
  echo "$r :: ${hits:-NOT IN CI}"
done
```

Found while adversarially reviewing #354.
title: review-open-issues Step 4 treats five non-blocking recipes as CI gates, so real defects get downgraded to P2

## Current state

The media-content manifest finds 204 stock-solution descriptors without an asserted working concentration across 99 media. Of these, 140 carry one or more non-asserted candidates; 64 have no candidate at all. This issue owns the source-research lane for those 64, not automatic promotion of the 140 candidates.

A missing working concentration means the stock composition cannot be converted into the final medium formulation. Guessing a customary dose would silently corrupt the recipe.

## Work

1. Produce a stable worklist for the 64 descriptors with exact record and solution locations.
2. Resolve each addition volume or dilution from the citing medium's own catalogue sheet or primary publication.
3. Record source evidence and units; distinguish stock preparation volume from stock addition volume.
4. Apply only source-backed values and regenerate the master manifest.
5. Keep unresolved entries explicit and lower a dedicated ratchet as reviewed batches land.

Related but distinct: #150 covers already-flattened stock cocktails whose stock-strength ingredients sit at media level.
title: Resolve 64 stock-solution additions with no concentration evidence

body:
## Problem

CultureMech advertises MIM hierarchy enrichment and hierarchy-aware merge
behavior, but the interface is dormant:

- `src/culturemech/enrich/hierarchy_importer.py` reads four MIM-root files:
  `ingredient_families.yaml`, `ingredient_roles.yaml`,
  `ingredient_merges.yaml`, and `ingredient_variants.yaml`;
- none of those files exists in MediaIngredientMech;
- current normalized CultureMech YAML has no populated `parent_ingredient` or
  `variant_type` values;
- `scripts/enrich_with_hierarchy.py` and hierarchy-aware paths in
  `merge/merge_recipes.py` can proceed after loading zero families;
- advertised hydrate/salt hierarchy modes consequently fall back to ordinary
  behavior without making the missing contract obvious.

This is separate from
[MediaIngredientMech #448](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/448):
CultureMech does not consume MIM's former live record slots. #448 retires that
zero-use MIM schema/API; it exposes that this separate file-based importer has
never had a working producer contract.

## Decision and scope

Prefer retirement of the dormant interface. If it is retained, first define a
versioned machine-readable producer/consumer contract and fail closed when its
source is absent or empty.

Do not populate recipe data, merge chemical forms, or reinterpret CultureMech
recipe variants as part of this infrastructure issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No supported command reports hierarchy enrichment/merge success when its
      source is missing or empty.
- [ ] Hierarchy-aware merge/enrichment flags are removed or fail closed; there
      is no silent fallback to baseline behavior.
- [ ] `parent_ingredient` / `variant_type` schema and docs are removed if unused,
      or backed by a versioned, tested contract.
- [ ] Missing-source and empty-source tests prove that no recipe file is written.
- [ ] The current normalized corpus remains unchanged unless separately curated.
- [ ] Documentation distinguishes ingredient chemical-form relations from
      CultureMech recipe families and variants.
- [ ] The obsolete clone URL/path assumptions in
      `scripts/enrich_with_hierarchy.py` are removed or updated.
- [ ] Coordinate with #218 and #219 for merge-output context without duplicating
      their collision/freshness scope.
title: Retire or fail closed the dormant MIM hierarchy importer and hierarchy-aware merge modes

body:
## Problem

The mapped and unmapped ingredient aggregators traverse only top-level
`ingredients` and derive display names from `name`. For `SolutionRecipe`, the
schema defines `composition` as authoritative and `ingredients` as an optional
placeholder/stub. As a result, current aggregation omits every real
stock-solution component, counts placeholder rows as unmapped, loses stable
`CultureMech:<id>` provenance, and can silently skip malformed files. The
mapped export also caps occurrence examples at 50 while downstream code derives
counts from that list.

A traversal-only patch is insufficient: canonical composition rows commonly
store the upstream `mediadive.compound:*` in `term` and the chemical grounding
in `chebi_term`; current “contains colon” logic would wrongly publish the
upstream compound ID as the ontology mapping.

## Evidence

- Corpus: 15,877 records, all with stable CultureMech IDs.
- 4,784 solution records contain 35,009 authoritative `composition` rows.
- Their legacy `ingredients` fields contain only 4,774 rows, every one `See
  source for composition`; 10 omit `ingredients`.
- 30,614 composition rows pair `term.id = mediadive.compound:*` with
  `chebi_term.id = CHEBI:*`.
- Current mapped output clips all 189 ingredients occurring more than 50 times
  to 50 examples.

Relevant code and schema:

- `scripts/aggregate_mapped_ingredients.py:88-173,207-209,242-249`
- `scripts/aggregate_unmapped_ingredients.py:110-185`
- `src/culturemech/schema/culturemech.yaml:509-572,756-778`
- `project.justfile:2620-2652`

## Scope / acceptance criteria

- [ ] Select components by record contract: `MediaRecipe.ingredients` and
      `SolutionRecipe.composition`. Do not concatenate dual fields or count
      solution placeholders.
- [ ] Use `preferred_term` for canonical recipe display, with an explicitly
      tested compatibility fallback only for legacy media records.
- [ ] Include root `CultureMech:<id>` in every direct ingredient-occurrence row;
      preserve source path and ingredient index.
- [ ] Define and test grounding precedence consistent with #260: never classify
      `mediadive.compound:*` as an ontology grounding merely because it contains
      `:`; preserve source ID separately from `chebi_term`/MIM linkage.
- [ ] Emit a lossless uncapped occurrence artifact. If examples are retained
      for display, store them separately and never derive occurrence or
      distinct-recipe counts from the sample.
- [ ] Count direct containment only: solution to ingredient once per solution
      recipe; do not expand it once per referencing medium (#312).
- [ ] Surface parse/schema errors in a machine-readable report and exit nonzero
      on unhandled input; no silent skips when `--verbose` is absent.
- [ ] Add mixed-schema fixtures covering a media recipe, a solution with
      composition plus placeholder, a solution without `ingredients`, repeated
      ingredient positions, duplicate recipe names with distinct IDs, more than
      50 occurrences, and mediadive `term` plus CHEBI `chebi_term`.
- [ ] Assert deterministic ordering and byte-identical reruns, no duplicate
      occurrence key, no orphan recipe ID, and exact occurrence and
      distinct-recipe counts.

## Coordination

Related: #336 (ID lifecycle contract), #260 (grounding source), closed #232
(intentional solution placeholders), and #312 (direct versus transitive KGX
edges). Blocks CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech#449 and any safe importer
rebuild after CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech#453.
title: Ingredient aggregators read solution placeholders instead of authoritative composition

body:
## Problem

MediaIngredientMech issues CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech#447 and #449 need
to store durable references from ingredient records and occurrence edges to
CultureMech recipes. CultureMech has recipe IDs, but consumers do not have a
documented external contract covering their lifecycle.

Closed #144 established an important precedent: recipe IDs survived while
paths moved, and the stale ID-to-path registry had to be repaired. It did not
define the guarantees an external consumer can rely on when a recipe is
renamed, moved, merged, split, or deleted.

Without that contract, MIM can copy an ID but cannot validate whether it is
canonical, current, redirected, or safe to retain across releases. Falling
back to display names or paths would recreate the ambiguity that #447 is meant
to remove.

## Scope

- Declare the canonical recipe-ID field and serialized syntax used by external
  consumers.
- Guarantee uniqueness and define whether issued IDs are immutable and never
  reused.
- Define lifecycle behavior for renames/path moves, merges, splits, and
  deletions, including tombstones or redirects where appropriate.
- Publish a versioned, machine-readable catalog containing at least ID,
  current display name/path, lifecycle status, and successor/redirect when one
  exists.
- Validate the catalog against the recipe corpus in CI.
- Document how downstream repositories should pin or record the catalog/release
  version used to verify a reference.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every current recipe has exactly one canonical externally usable ID.
- [ ] CI rejects duplicate IDs and reuse of an issued ID for another recipe.
- [ ] Name and path changes do not invalidate the recipe reference.
- [ ] Merge/delete behavior is machine-readable through a tombstone or redirect
      policy; split semantics are documented.
- [ ] A versioned catalog lets consumers resolve an ID without parsing recipe
      filenames or fuzzy-matching names.
- [ ] The producer and consumer documentation link to the same lifecycle
      contract.

## Downstream dependencies

- CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech#447 — stable, typed recipe references
- CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech#449 — lossless ingredient-to-recipe edges

This issue defines producer guarantees only; it does not require MIM's schema
or data model to be implemented here.
title: Publish a stable external lifecycle contract for CultureMech recipe IDs

body:
## Adversarial review finding

The provider-triage implementation is now committed on `main` in all five Mech repositories, but there is no fleet-level behavioral contract protecting the parts that should agree.

Current GitHub blob identities are all different:

| repository | `scripts/deep_research_provider.py` blob |
|---|---|
| CultureMech | `790223960de2c9758e57903e08bdc5b3c2303852` |
| TraitMech | `9f57334b525e680f2acfca644c31008cafdd7b72` |
| MediaIngredientMech | `d00d1851eed987575ce2d4895f8605642712431b` |
| CommunityMech | `2dcdf2595ee1aa3b89d408d325991b205e3e594d` |
| proteintraitsmech | `3bd6e03a76a394d5b1285297b9b5760fbb987133` |

Some divergence is correct: each Mech has custom research focuses, and TraitMech exposes a richer `configured` / `available` / `routable` availability model with injected environment state. Other behavior should remain aligned: absolute fit semantics, negative-score ordering, provider filters, allowlists, no-paid policy, selected-provider JSON consistency, deterministic ties, and credit-free inspection.

The existing byte-exact vendored-sync mechanism is therefore the wrong gate for this script. It would either reject valid domain specialization or leave common routing semantics ungoverned.

This supersedes the future-looking portion of #287. That issue was correctly closed when these files existed only as untracked local copies; they are now public and the premise has materially changed.

## Proposed scope

1. Define a small provider-triage contract fixture covering shared inputs and observable outputs.
2. Run the same fixture against every Mech implementation without invoking a provider.
3. Keep focus definitions, domain weights, provider descriptions, and target resolution local.
4. Document intentional extensions, including TraitMech's richer availability state, without requiring the other Mechs to erase them.
5. Add a fleet check or reusable test package so a routing-policy change cannot silently drift.

## Acceptance criteria

- All five implementations pass the same contract for fit normalization and deterministic ordering, including all-negative raw scores.
- Provider-filtered output cannot select or recommend a provider omitted from its ranking.
- Allowlists and no-paid-provider policy have the same externally visible semantics.
- Inspection and contract tests perform no provider call and spend no provider credits.
- Domain-specific focuses and weights remain local and schema-validated.
- Intentional implementation differences are listed in one maintained compatibility document.

Found during the five-Mech alignment and adversarial provider-assignment review.
title: Define a fleet behavioral contract for provider triage

body:
Flagged by dynamic-review on #317: this PR adds real validation/behavior fixes to the canonical hub copy of \`scripts/deep_research_provider.py\` that were discovered only while porting the file's existing feature set to the spokes, and originate here first (not in any spoke):

- coercing capability dict keys with \`str()\` before diffing against \`_ALL_CAPABILITIES\`, closing a \`TypeError\` when YAML 1.1 parses an unquoted key like \`no:\` as bool \`False\` mixed with a real string key
- rejecting \`--allow ""\` (explicit empty string) as invalid instead of silently falling through to unfiltered \`allow=None\`
- a distinct "no provider passes the current --allow/--no-paid filters" message when policy, not missing credentials, emptied a recommendation

If the spoke copies still have the same unguarded \`sorted(unknown_caps)\` or the same \`if args.allow:\` truthiness check, they remain exposed to the same \`TypeError\`/silent-empty-allowlist bypass.

This repo's own convention (per CultureMech#287) treats \`deep_research_provider.py\` as vendored to ProteinTraitsMech, MediaIngredientMech, and CommunityMech but explicitly outside the automated vendored-sync drift contract — so nothing detects this drift automatically; it needs deliberate porting, same as prior fixes (ProteinTraitsMech#505/#506, MediaIngredientMech#413/#399, CommunityMech#658/#641).

Note: as of this issue being filed, this exact set of fixes has already been ported to proteintraitsmech (#514) and MediaIngredientMech (#418) in the same session as #317 — check those PRs' state before assuming this is still open for those two repos. CommunityMech (#662) should be checked/ported too if not already current.
title: Sync PR #317's hub-only deep_research_provider.py fixes to the 3 spoke Mechs

## Priority

P2 — bounded compatibility and resource-management cleanup.

## Problem

The passing test suite emits 53 warnings, including actionable project-owned warnings:

- `PyPDF2` is deprecated in favor of `pypdf`.
- `src/culturemech/import/togo_importer.py:79` contains an invalid escape sequence that will become stricter in future Python versions.
- Domain-growth tests report multiple unclosed SQLite connections.
- The project allows any Python `>=3.10`, but classifiers/tool targets stop at 3.12 while local execution on 3.14 exposes additional compatibility warnings.

Third-party LinkML/Pandas warnings should be separated from warnings owned by this repository.

## Proposed work

- Migrate imports/dependency declarations from `PyPDF2` to `pypdf` and test PDF paths.
- Fix invalid string escapes and run warning-sensitive tests on supported Python versions.
- Ensure SQLite connections/cursors are closed deterministically with context managers or explicit ownership.
- Define the actually supported Python range and test it in a small CI matrix.
- Configure CI to fail on newly introduced project-owned warnings while filtering documented third-party warnings narrowly.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No project-owned deprecation, syntax, or resource warning appears in the test suite.
- [ ] PDF extraction tests pass with `pypdf` and `PyPDF2` is removed.
- [ ] SQLite resource warnings are covered by regression tests.
- [ ] `requires-python`, classifiers, Ruff/Black/Mypy targets, and CI versions agree.
- [ ] Third-party warning filters are specific and documented.
title: Eliminate project-owned test warnings and define Python compatibility

- [ ] Contributors have a fast test target with feedback materially faster than the full corpus suite.
- [ ] Full corpus/integration tests remain available and run in CI where appropriate.
- [ ] Generated dataclasses do not distort lint or coverage reporting.

## Priority

P1 — local agent permissions are over-broad and tracked hooks are machine-specific/fail-open.

## Problem

The local-only `.claude/settings.local.json` currently grants commands including `sudo rm`, Homebrew uninstall/install, repository creation, unrestricted `uv run`, and many stale path-specific shell fragments. Although ignored, it is the active policy on this checkout and creates unnecessary local risk.

The tracked hooks under `.claude/hooks/` hardcode one developer's orchestration path. `pre-edit` and `pre-commit` allow the operation when lock checking errors, so a missing script or broken environment silently disables the coordination guarantee.

## Proposed work

- Prune the active local permission file to minimal, current, task-scoped commands.
- Document a minimal-permissions example without committing credentials or personal paths.
- Read the orchestration root from an environment variable/configuration rather than a hardcoded absolute path.
- Define two explicit modes: hooks disabled because orchestration is not configured, versus hooks enabled and lock checks required.
- When enabled, fail closed on lock-check errors and print an actionable diagnostic.
- Test hook behavior for unlocked, locked, missing-config, and checker-error cases.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No tracked hook contains a developer-specific absolute path.
- [ ] Enabled lock enforcement cannot silently degrade to allow-on-error.
- [ ] Unconfigured installations receive a clear, intentional disabled-mode result.
- [ ] Shared documentation recommends a narrow permission policy and explains that `settings.local.json` remains untracked.
- [ ] Hook tests cover all exit-code branches.

## Note

The local permission cleanup itself is intentionally not a repository diff because `settings.local.json` is ignored; the issue should record that manual action when completed.
title: Harden Claude permissions guidance and orchestration hooks

## Priority

P1 — ingestion can report success after partial failure and local paths make recipes non-portable.

## Problem

`RawYAMLConverter.convert_directory()` catches every per-file exception, prints it, and returns success (`src/culturemech/convert/base.py:92-98`). A pipeline can therefore publish a partial conversion while appearing green. Empty matches also return successfully without a machine-readable result.

`project.justfile` also embeds developer-specific absolute paths for cmm-ai-automation, MicrobeMediaParam, and KG-Microbe embeddings (`project.justfile:17-18`, `project.justfile:2539`). Documentation currently tells users to edit the justfile locally.

## Proposed work

- Return/record converted, skipped, and failed counts from directory conversion.
- Exit nonzero when any conversion fails, with an explicit opt-in such as `--keep-going` for diagnostic batches.
- Decide whether zero matched inputs is an error by default; provide an explicit `--allow-empty` when appropriate.
- Make external paths arguments or environment-configurable defaults and validate them before work begins.
- Avoid embedding absolute source paths and wall-clock timestamps in reproducible intermediate output where stable relative provenance is available.
- Add failure-mode tests to representative converters/import recipes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One corrupt input causes the default conversion command to exit nonzero.
- [ ] Partial-output behavior is explicit, summarized, and tested.
- [ ] No developer-specific absolute path remains in tracked build recipes.
- [ ] Missing external inputs fail with actionable setup instructions.
- [ ] CI covers a successful batch, a corrupt file, and an empty input set.
title: Make ingestion fail on partial conversion and remove machine-specific paths

body:
## Priority

P1 — the published site can silently serve stale data, and cleanup deletes tracked files.

## Problem

- The normalized corpus currently contains 15,877 YAML records, while tracked `app/data.js` contains 15,827 entries and was last regenerated in April 2026.
- `pages/normalized/` contains 15,828 tracked generated files (~235 MB), matching the older corpus rather than the current one.
- `.github/workflows/generate-pages.yaml` copies `app/` and `pages/` into the deployment artifact but does not rebuild browser data or normalized pages.
- The workflow does not trigger for general `app/**` changes.
- `just clean` runs `rm -rf pages/*` and `rm -f app/data.js`, deleting tracked artifacts and producing a massive dirty worktree (`project.justfile:2421-2429`).
- The optional `culturebotai-claw` checkout can fail while the renderer silently emits pages without composition graphs.

## Proposed work

- Define which web artifacts are canonical inputs and which are reproducible outputs.
- Rebuild every published derived asset in CI from the same declared data layer.
- Add record-set/freshness tests between source YAML, browser data, and generated page indexes.
- Add deployment triggers for all source files that affect the site.
- Stop tracking reproducible per-record HTML after confirming CI can regenerate it.
- Restrict `clean` to explicit ignored paths, with a guard that refuses to delete tracked files.
- Make missing optional rendering dependencies visible; either fail or publish an explicit degraded-build notice.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A clean checkout can reproduce the complete Pages artifact with locked dependencies.
- [ ] CI fails when browser/page record coverage differs from its source corpus.
- [ ] `just clean` leaves `git status --short` unchanged on a clean checkout.
- [ ] `app/data.js` and per-record pages are either generated in CI or covered by a freshness gate.
- [ ] Deployment triggers cover `app/**`, renderer/template changes, and the selected data source.
- [ ] The generated-output retention/removal policy is documented.

## Risk / coordination

Removing tracked generated HTML is a large deletion and should be reviewed as a dedicated commit after the replacement CI build is green.
title: Make published web artifacts reproducible, fresh, and safe to clean

body:
## Priority

P1 — user-facing commands are broken or render the wrong file.

## Problem

The rendering interface has three independent correctness defects:

1. `culturemech render` imports the deleted `culturemech.render` module and raises `ModuleNotFoundError` (`src/culturemech/cli.py:35-53`).
2. `just gen-page FILE` passes only `dirname(FILE)` plus `--limit 1`, so it renders the alphabetically first YAML in the directory instead of the requested file (`project.justfile:1730-1737`).
3. `_category_section()` hardcodes links as `media/<slug>.html`. That works only for the default `pages/` + `pages/media/` layout and is wrong for `pages/normalized/` and `pages/single/` (`src/culturemech/render_media_pages.py:193-201`).

The installed package is also incomplete: `[tool.setuptools.package-data]` omits `templates/style.css` and `templates/_partials/*.j2`.

## Proposed work

- Expose one callable rendering API in `culturemech.render_media_pages` and have both Click and argparse/just entry points call it directly.
- Add an explicit single-file option (`--file`) rather than emulating it with directory + limit.
- Calculate page links relative to `index_dir` and `out_dir`; do not hardcode `media/`.
- Include CSS and recursive Jinja partials in built wheels/sdists.
- Remove or update references to the retired `culturemech.render` module.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `culturemech render --help` and a one-record smoke render succeed from an installed wheel.
- [ ] `just gen-page path/to/X.yaml` renders X, regardless of neighboring filenames.
- [ ] Index links work for the canonical, normalized, and single-page layouts.
- [ ] A wheel-install smoke test confirms templates, partials, and CSS are present.
- [ ] CLI and renderer regression tests run in CI.

## Dependency

Coordinate with the stored-XSS fix so the consolidated API does not preserve unsafe output behavior.
title: Consolidate and repair the rendering CLI and single-page workflow
