2. For artifacts declared in `CHECKABLE`, use the declared command as the writer
   rather than re-deriving it by grep. It is already known exactly.
3. Record **all** candidate writers rather than the first, so ambiguity is visible
   instead of silently resolved. An artifact with two plausible writers is
   information a curator wants.
title: audit_derived_artifacts records ITSELF as the writer of the artifacts it checks

body:
From review of #199.

That PR removes the `deprecated:` annotations and rewrites `medium_type` as a
maintained axis, but four places still describe the old state — one of them
repeating a claim #195 disproved:

**1. `tests/test_composition_type.py:140`**

> "`medium_type` is deprecated and #154 removed its last reader, but it is still…"

Wrong on both counts now. It is not deprecated, and #154 did not remove its last
reader — `kgx_export` emits one edge per record from it, plus `browser_export`,
`umap_generator`, `dsmz_resolver` and `multi_database_crossref`. That sentence is
how the "safe to drop" premise propagated into #165 in the first place.

**2. `MediumCompositionTypeEnum.UNDEFINED` description** (schema, and therefore the
generated dataclasses):

> "Replaces the deprecated MediumTypeEnum value COMPLEX."

"Replaces" is now wrong in the sense that matters — both slots are populated and
maintained. It should say the composition axis is primary and COMPLEX is its
single-valued counterpart.

**3. `scripts/migrate_medium_type_axes.py`** — docstring and a curation note it
writes into records: "Derived … from deprecated medium_type=". That note is
persisted into `curation_history`, so the stale wording is being written into new
records.

**4. Same file's module docstring** — "Backfill the multi-axis vocabulary from the
deprecated medium_type slot."

None of these change behaviour. They matter because this is the fourth
documentation-drift instance this week, and the first one directly caused a wrong
architectural conclusion: #165 proposed deleting a slot the KG depends on, on the
strength of a comment.
title: Un-deprecating medium_type left four places still calling it deprecated

body:
From review of #195.

`test_medium_type_never_contradicts_composition_type` passes against a corpus with
**0 contradictions**, so every assertion in it is currently trivially satisfied.
Nothing in the file demonstrates the guard detects the defect it was written for.

That matters because the check has two moving parts that can quietly fail open:

- the mapping is parsed from schema descriptions with
  `re.search(r"Migrates to composition_type=(\w+)")`. Reword the schema
  description and `composition_mapping` empties. `test_the_schema_still_documents_a_composition_mapping`
  guards the two known keys, so this is partly covered — but only those two.
- `REFINEMENTS` is hardcoded. Widening it wrongly (say `DEFINED -> {DEFINED,
  UNDEFINED}`) would silently accept the exact #164 defect, and no test would
  notice.

I verified by hand, outside the test file, that the guard flags
`medium_type=DEFINED` / `composition_type=UNDEFINED` (the #164 shape) and the
reverse, while accepting `COMPLEX/UNDEFINED` and the `COMPLEX/SEMI_DEFINED`
refinement. That verification should live in the suite rather than in a
transcript.

Fix: add negative tests over synthetic records — the mapping logic factored into a
function the tests can call with constructed input, in the `audit_parsed()` style
used elsewhere in this repo, so it needs no fixture files and no corpus scan.
title: The medium_type guard has no test proving it can fail

body:
Introduced by me in #193. This is #121's defect reproduced in a new report.

`triage_missing_compositions.py` populates `cited_medium_in_local_dump` by
listing `data/raw/mediadive/compositions/`. That path is **gitignored**:

```
.gitignore:106:  data/raw/**/*.json
```

So the tracked report is a function of whoever last ran it:

```
on my machine       428 rows, cited_medium_in_local_dump=yes: 217
in a fresh worktree 428 rows, cited_medium_in_local_dump=yes:   0
```

Verified by running the same script in a clean worktree of `origin/main`.

This is precisely what #121 fixed for the deep-research prioritizer: a report that
scanned an untracked directory reordered completely on a different machine,
producing a diff indistinguishable from real change. The lesson was "everything
downstream must be a pure function of tracked data", and I did not apply it.

**Why it slipped through review.** `test_corpus_baseline` asserts the row COUNT
(428), which is identical either way — the machine-dependence is entirely in a
column no test reads. CI is green and the report is wrong there.

It also means the number in the docstring and PR description ("217 of them cite a
medium number that resolves to a composition file") is unreproducible by anyone
else, which undercuts the argument that column exists to make.

## Fix options

1. **Drop the column.** Its purpose is documenting the trap, and the docstring
   already does that in prose. The count can be stated as a one-off measurement
   with the date and source, not regenerated per-run.
2. **Emit it only when the dump is present**, and write a header/sentinel making
   the absence explicit rather than silently rendering every row as "no".
3. **Track a small derived index** of available composition ids (a few KB), so the
   column becomes a pure function of tracked data.

(1) is smallest and matches the report-only intent. (3) is the most useful if
anything downstream ever wants to act on it.

Either way a test should assert the report does not vary with the presence of
`data/raw`, since that is the property that actually broke.
title: missing_compositions.tsv is a function of gitignored data/raw — 217 rows on my machine, 0 on a fresh clone

body:
From review of #193.

`SOLUTION_NAMED` requires a specific word before "solution":

```python
r"\b(?:trace\s+(?:element|salts|metal)s?|vitamin|mineral|selenite|tungstate|"
r"salts?)\b.*\bsolution\b|\bsolution\s+[A-Z]\b|^\d+\s*x\s+|\bstock\b"
```

So it matches "Trace element solution" but not these, all of which are plainly
stock solutions imported as media records:

```
Amino acid solution (medium 78)
Chelated iron solution (medium 737)
Chelated Iron solution (medium 748)
Co-factors solution (medium 843)
Ferric Quinate Solution (medium 380)
Haemin solution (medium 104)
Heavy metal solution (medium 867)
LIP-solution (medium 391)
Micronutrient solution SL8 (medium 1128)
Na-sesquicarbonate solution (medium 31)
Phosphate buffer (10x) (medium 1341)
Artificial sea water from a marine aquarium salts mixture
```

34 unflagged names contain a solution-ish word; at least 12 are unambiguous.

The enumeration is the bug. Any name ending in "... solution" is a solution
regardless of which reagent precedes it, and there is no way to enumerate the
reagents in advance — "haemin", "quinate", "sesquicarbonate" were never going to
be on a hand-written list.

**Why it matters.** The 162 figure is the report's central claim: that most of
these records are mis-typed rather than media with a missing recipe. Undercounting
it makes the data-quality problem look worse than it is, which is the same error
#175 and #181 both already made.

Fix: match `\bsolutions?\b` directly, keep the `Solution A` / `10x` / `stock`
branches for names that do not use the word, and add "buffer" — `Phosphate buffer
(10x)` is a stock by any reading.

Worth checking for false positives afterwards: a medium legitimately named
"... solution" (Ringer's, Hank's BSS) would then be flagged. In this report that
is arguably still correct — every row here has no composition — but the column
name claims something specific and should stay true.
title: looks_like_a_solution misses 34 records by enumerating words instead of matching 'solution'

body:
From review of #179.

`assess()` returns `PROPOSED` when the parse round-trips, the values are
plausible, and no name looks like a truncated formula. But it never checks
whether the **unconsumed tail still contains an ingredient** — and for 9 of the 14
PROPOSED records, it does:

```
NBRC_14      parsed=3   tail='Agar15gpH 8.2*Dilute artificial seawater...'
NBRC_280     parsed=4   tail='Agar20gpH 7.0'
NBRC_229     parsed=5   tail='Agar20gpH 7.3'
NBRC_245     parsed=5   tail='Agar (if needed)20gpH 7.6'
NBRC_1287    parsed=4   tail='Agar15gpH 7.0Biphenyl crystal is supplied...'
NBRC_382     parsed=5   tail='Distilled water1LpH 7.0'
NBRC_892     parsed=4   tail='Distilled water1LpH 7.1-7.5'
NBRC_948     parsed=3   tail='Distilled water1LpH unadjusted*Sterilize...'
NBRC_869     parsed=4   tail='Distilled water200mlpH 7.6*Filtered, aged seawater...'
```

Cause: tokenising stops at the last quantity+unit pair before a `pH` marker,
because `pH 7.0` is not a quantity token. The final ingredient is then swept into
the tail along with the pH text and any footnote.

**Why this matters.** `PROPOSED` reads as "this parse is safe to apply". A curator
acting on it would write a composition missing its last ingredient. That is
usually **agar** — which changes the medium from solid to liquid — or **distilled
water**, the solvent basis the whole recipe is relative to.

This is the round-trip lesson from #166 in a new place. `round_trips()` returns
True because `items + tail == text`, so nothing is invented — but nothing being
invented is not the same as everything being extracted. Round-trip proves the
parse added nothing; it says nothing about completeness.

**Fix:** downgrade to `HOLD: ingredient remains in the tail` whenever the tail
still matches a quantity+unit pattern. That moves 9 records from PROPOSED to HOLD,
leaving 5 PROPOSED and 20 HOLD.

**Detection trap, for whoever writes the check:** the tail is
`Agar15gpH` — there is no word boundary between the `g` and the `p`, so
`\d+\s*(?:mg|ml|g|l)\b` **matches nothing**. I hit exactly this while scoping the
issue and initially measured "0 of 14". `score_review_need.py` already carries a
comment about this for the same reason. Use a lookahead
(`(?=[A-Za-z(\[]|\s|$)`), not `\b`.
title: 9 of 14 PROPOSED parses silently drop an ingredient into the unconsumed tail

body:
From review of #190.

#190 and #187 between them removed three full-corpus rescans from the test suite,
and #179 removes a fourth. But the pattern has now recurred **five times**, and
nothing stops the sixth.

`tests/conftest.py` provides session-scoped `corpus` / `media_records` fixtures
precisely for this. They are opt-in: a new corpus guard that writes its own
`rglob("*.yaml")` and re-parses ~15,900 records is perfectly valid code, passes
review, and costs ~100s. Five of those cancelled the pytest job at the 40-minute
ceiling — with every test passing, so the PR reads as broken when it is not.

That failure mode is the problem. A slow test does not announce itself; it
surfaces as an unrelated PR's CI being cancelled weeks later.

**Remaining surface.** Four test modules still glob the corpus directly:

```
conftest.py             2   (legitimate — this IS the fixture)
test_recipe_indexes.py  3
test_id_registry.py     1
test_record_kinds.py    1
```

Those may be cheap or unavoidable; they have not been measured. Worth checking
before assuming they are fine.

**Three audit scripts still have no parsed-records entry point**, so any future
guard over them has no choice but to rescan:

```
audit_chebi_consistency.py
audit_missing_roles.py
audit_writers.py
```

Two candidate guards:

1. A test asserting no module under `tests/` outside `conftest.py` calls
   `rglob("*.yaml")` on `data/normalized_yaml` — cheap, and names the fixture in
   its failure message.
2. A `--durations` budget in CI failing if any single test exceeds ~30s.

The first is narrower and self-documenting. The second catches slow tests that
are slow for other reasons.

Not urgent — with #187, #190 and #179 landed the suite is ~237s. Filed so the
sixth instance is a caught regression rather than another cancelled job.
title: Nothing prevents a 6th corpus-rescanning test; the fixture exists but is opt-in

body:
From review of #187, and it is the direct cause of the #179 CI failure.

`test_corpus_count_matches_the_documented_baseline` takes **118s** because it
re-parses all ~15,900 records. It is now the fifth such test:

```
118.7s  test_selective_agent_mismatch::test_corpus_count_matches_the_documented_baseline  (#187, new)
102.5s  test_unparsed_compositions::test_every_crammed_record_gets_a_verdict               (#179, new)
100.8s  test_composition_type::test_no_defined_record_carries_a_bulk_undefined_component
 97.5s  test_review_need::test_most_of_the_corpus_is_not_flagged_as_severe
 94.7s  test_review_need::test_known_bad_records_rank_near_the_top
```

That is ~8.5 minutes of the local 9m10s run spent parsing the same corpus five
times. `tests/conftest.py` already provides session-scoped `corpus` /
`media_records` fixtures built for exactly this — that change took the suite from
590s to 239s — but each of these tests calls its script's own `collect()`
instead, so none of them use it.

The consequence is not theoretical: #179's pytest job was CANCELLED at the
40-minute ceiling with all 662 tests passing. It is a timeout, not a failure.

Fix: give each audit script a `audit_parsed()`-style entry point taking
already-parsed records (this PR's script and `audit_composition_type` already
have one) and have the corpus tests feed it the session fixture. Raising
`timeout-minutes` again would treat the symptom; the last raise was 20 -> 40 and
the ceiling was reached again within a fortnight.

Blocks #179.
title: A 5th full-corpus test pushes the pytest job further past the 40-minute CI ceiling

body:
From review of #187.

`named_concentration()` searches a ±40 character window around the agent and
returns the first match. When a name lists two agents, the window reaches back
past a comma and picks up the PREVIOUS agent's value:

```
name: "LB + 50 ug/ml Kanamycin, 100 ug/ml Ampicillin medium"
got:  ampicillin=50 ug/ml; kanamycin=50 ug/ml
want: ampicillin=100 ug/ml; kanamycin=50 ug/ml
```

This is the #166 failure class, in the one tool written specifically to avoid it.
The whole premise of the audit is that it does not invent chemistry — the column
is documented as "recoverable from tracked data, not invented" — and here it
emits a confident, wrong, plausible-looking concentration under exactly that
label. A curator acting on the TSV would apply 50 ug/ml ampicillin to a medium
whose source says 100.

**Current corpus impact: none.** Only one record populates `named_conc`
(`lb_50_ug_ml_kanamycin_medium`, single agent, correct). So this is latent rather
than live — but 6 of the 17 records name multiple agents, and any of them gaining
a concentration upstream would silently produce a wrong value.

Fix: attribute a concentration only within the name segment that contains the
agent — split on `,`, `+`, `;` and `and` first — and emit nothing when the segment
holds no concentration. Silence is the correct output; a guess is not.
title: named_conc attributes the WRONG concentration when a name lists two agents

body:
From review of #182.

`data/import_tracking/reports/axis_research_batch.json` is a tracked derived
artifact holding 200 `file_path` entries into `data/normalized_yaml/`. Nothing
references or validates it — no test, no CI gate.

This is the same systemic pattern already fixed four times: recipe indexes (#125),
the id registry (#144), the chebi report (#157), markdown links (#161). Records get
recategorized — as 629 archaeal media were in #114 — and stale paths silently stop
resolving.

The failure here is quieter than usual: the runner's tiered resolver (#173) falls
back from path to filename to name, so a moved record still resolves and the batch
appears healthy. A record that is *deleted or renamed* fails only at submission
time, partway through a multi-hour run.

Suggested guard: a test asserting every `file_path` in the batch resolves to an
existing record, skipped when the file is absent, in line with the existing
artifact tests.

Related: #145, #168 (the remaining unguarded artifacts).
title: Committed axis_research_batch.json can rot when records move, with no guard

body:
From review of #182.

`per = args.size // len(strata)` floors, so any `--size` not divisible by the
stratum count silently returns fewer records than asked:

```
$ uv run python scripts/sample_axis_research_batch.py --size 25
asked 25, got 24
```

`--size 200` happens to divide evenly, which is why this did not surface in use.

The per-stratum table is printed, so the shortfall is visible to someone adding
up the column — but the total is never stated as a discrepancy, and the tool
reports "Drew 24 records" without noting 25 were requested.

This is the "no silent caps" case: if a tool bounds coverage, it should say what
it dropped, since a silent shortfall reads as full coverage.

Fix: distribute the remainder across strata (largest-pool-first), or warn
explicitly that `--size N` was rounded down to M.
title: sample_axis_research_batch silently returns fewer records than --size requests

body:
From review of #182.

`scripts/sample_axis_research_batch.py` (159 lines) ships with no test file, unlike
every other script added recently.

The untested logic is not incidental. The round-robin interleave is what makes the
claim "every prefix is stratified" true, and that claim is the entire basis for
running a 25-record probe and treating it as representative. If the interleave
regressed to concatenation, `--limit 25` would silently draw all 25 from one
stratum — the probe would still complete, still report fill rates, and still look
correct.

Worth pinning:

- every prefix is stratified (the load-bearing property)
- strata are disjoint — no record appears twice
- the same seed and corpus reproduce the same batch
- a stratum smaller than the per-stratum quota draws all of it and warns
- `--size` not divisible by the stratum count (see the sibling issue)
title: sample_axis_research_batch has no tests; interleaving is load-bearing and unpinned

body:
From review of #182.

`scripts/sample_axis_research_batch.py` tells the user, in both its module
docstring (line 36) and its final printed hint (line 154):

```
just research-media-edison-batch data/import_tracking/reports/axis_research_batch.json
```

That is the **growth-research** recipe. It renders `media_growth_research.md`
into `research/media/` — so following the tool's own instructions produces
growth-research reports under axis filenames in the growth directory, which is
precisely the collision #182 was written to prevent.

The correct recipe, added in the same PR, is `research-media-edison-axis`.

Severity: the failure is silent. The wrong template still yields plausible
literature reports, and the run costs ~345s/record, so a 200-record batch would
complete "successfully" having researched the wrong question and marked 200
slugs done for growth research they never had.

Fix: point both the docstring and the printed hint at
`just research-media-edison-axis`.

Root cause: the hint predates the axis recipe. It was written when `--template`
was going to be passed to the batch recipe, and was not updated when the separate
recipe was introduced mid-review.

This is the fourth instance in recent work of a docstring describing behaviour
the code does not have (#180 and two others). The existing guard checks that
named recipes *exist* — `research-media-edison-batch` does exist — but not that
a script names the recipe it is actually for. Worth considering whether that gap
is closable.
title: sample_axis_research_batch prints the WRONG recipe, steering users into the collision PR #182 fixes

body:
Found by the Edison axis-classification probe (#152), not by any existing gate.

Asked to classify `lb_rifampicin_medium`, the model declined to assign
`functional_role: SELECTIVE` and explained why:

> the supplied ingredient list contains no rifampicin entry or concentration.
> Do not assign SELECTIVE...
>
> Rifampicin is a genuine selective pressure (doi:10.1128/mbio.03168-22), but that
> general fact does not establish that it is present in this specific formulation

It also declined `GENERAL_PURPOSE`, flagging the conflict rather than picking a
side: the name implies antibiotic selection, the composition is antibiotic-free.

That is correct. The record's ingredients are Distilled water, Yeast extract,
NaCl, Agar, Bacto Tryptone — plain LB. The selective agent is in the name only.

## Scope

13 records are named for a selective agent absent from their ingredient list:

| agent | n |
|---|--:|
| kanamycin | 6 |
| ampicillin | 3 |
| nalidixic acid | 3 |
| streptomycin | 2 |
| rifampicin | 2 |
| cefpodoxime, ciprofloxacin, chloramphenicol | 1 each |

11 of the 13 are `lb_*_medium` with exactly 5 ingredients — the plain-LB base —
so this looks like one systematic import defect across the LB+antibiotic family
rather than 13 independent omissions:

```
bacterial/am3_nalidixic_acid_kanamycin_medium.yaml      kanamycin, nalidixic acid
bacterial/am3_nalidixic_acid_medium.yaml                nalidixic acid
bacterial/lb_50_ug_ml_kanamycin_medium.yaml             kanamycin
bacterial/lb_ampicillin_cefpodoxime_kanamycin_medium.yaml  ampicillin, kanamycin, cefpodoxime
bacterial/lb_ampicillin_kanamycin_medium.yaml           ampicillin, kanamycin
bacterial/lb_ampicillin_medium.yaml                     ampicillin
bacterial/lb_chloramphenicol_medium.yaml                chloramphenicol
bacterial/lb_kanamycin_hygromycin_medium.yaml           kanamycin
bacterial/lb_kanamycin_medium.yaml                      kanamycin
bacterial/lb_nalidixic_acid_ciprofloxacin_medium.yaml   nalidixic acid, ciprofloxacin
bacterial/lb_rifampicin_medium.yaml                     rifampicin
bacterial/lb_streptomycin_medium.yaml                   streptomycin
bacterial/lb_streptomycin_rifampicin_medium.yaml        rifampicin, streptomycin
```

`lb_50_ug_ml_kanamycin_medium` is the sharpest case: the source recorded a
concentration (50 µg/mL) in the name, so the value existed upstream and was lost
in transform rather than never present.

## Why this matters beyond 13 records

These records currently assert a composition that is not the medium they name.
Anything consuming them — growth-condition inference, ingredient grounding, the
axis classification this probe was meant to produce — gets a wrong answer with no
signal that it is wrong. A `functional_role` assigned from the name would launder
the defect into the schema.

## Proposed check

A gate comparing selective agents named in `name`/`original_name` against
`ingredients[].preferred_term`, with `--max-allowed` per the existing convention.

Two traps for whoever writes it, both hit while scoping this:

- Match on **word boundaries**. A substring matcher reported 28 records because
  `streptomyc` matches the genus *Streptomyces* (8 false positives, e.g.
  `GYM_Streptomyces_Medium`) and `bile` matches `alkalispirillum_mobile_medium`
  (8 more). More than half the initial hits were artifacts of the matcher.
- Presence in the name proves the agent belongs; absence from a finite agent list
  proves nothing. The gate bounds a known family, it does not certify the rest.

## Fix

Not attempted here. Recovering the concentrations needs the upstream TOGO/NBRC
records, and inventing plausible ones is precisely the failure mode of #166.
title: 2 media named for a selective agent their composition omits (both DSMZ 309; was 17, 15 were false positives)

body:
## Found reviewing #179

`scripts/repair_unparsed_compositions.py` was written to repair the 25 crammed NBRC compositions, then deliberately reduced to report-only after the repair was shown unsafe — a parse can round-trip and still write a non-existent compound (`KH2PO` at 40.85 g/L instead of `KH2PO4` at 0.85).

Two artefacts of that change survived:

**1. The docstring documents a flag that no longer exists.**

```
Usage::

    just repair-unparsed-compositions              # report what would change
    just repair-unparsed-compositions --apply
```

`--apply` was removed. The recipe is also named `report-unparsed-compositions`, so neither line in that block is runnable.

**2. The filename says the opposite of what the tool does.**

`repair_unparsed_compositions.py` cannot repair anything — a test asserts it has no write path, and the module docstring explains at length why repairing is unsafe without the NBRC catalogue. A reader reaching for a repair tool finds one that refuses, and someone tidying up later may well "restore" the missing `--apply`.

## Why this matters more than a naming nit

The whole point of the change is that **writing to these records is unsafe**. A name promising repair is an invitation to add the write path back. The test guarding against that (`test_the_tool_cannot_write`) checks for `path.write_text`, which a differently-shaped write would slip past — so the name is doing real defensive work, not cosmetics.

## Fix

Rename to `report_unparsed_compositions.py`, matching the recipe, and correct the usage block. Being fixed in #179.

## Note

This is the third instance this week of a docstring describing behaviour the code does not have — see also the `verify-schema-pin` reference in #106 and the `--merge-audits` flag claimed by `score_review_need.py` before #176. Worth considering a check that every `just <recipe>` and `--flag` mentioned in a script docstring actually exists; all three were caught by review rather than by tooling.
title: A tool that provably cannot repair is named repair_*, and its docstring still documents the --apply flag that was removed

body:
## Found reviewing #176

`score_review_need.py` emits any record scoring above zero. That makes the report **6,643 rows — 60% of the 11,094 media** — and most of it is not actionable:

```
band     n      dominant signals
70+      66     no ingredient grounded x66, no media_term x66
50-69   127     no ingredient grounded x127, only 1 ingredient x93
30-49   632     no pH and no temperature x460, no ingredients x362
15-29   940     no pH and no temperature x805, no media_term x348
1-14   4878     no pH and no temperature x4332
```

**4,332 of the 4,878 low-band records (89%) carry *only* the "no pH and no temperature" signal.**

That signal fires on 51.4% of the corpus. It was deliberately weighted lowest (5) precisely because it is the norm rather than a defect — but weighting is not enough, because any non-zero score puts a record in the file. So a record with nothing wrong except a missing optional slot sits in a report titled "needs review", and a curator opening the TSV wades through thousands of them.

## Why it matters more than it looks

The point of the scorer is that the yield-based prioritizer renders the damaged tail invisible. A report that is 60% noise reintroduces the same problem one layer up: the 42 genuinely broken records are buried under 4,332 that merely lack a pH value.

## Fix

Do not let a norm-level signal alone qualify a record. Either:

1. Require at least one signal that is not `no pH and no temperature` — conditions then act as a tiebreaker among records that are already suspect, which is what its weight of 5 was meant to express; or
2. Add a `--min-score` with a default above the conditions-only value.

(1) is more precise: it distinguishes "incomplete in a way that is normal here" from "incomplete in a way that is not", rather than relying on an arbitrary cutoff.

Expected effect: ~6,643 rows to ~2,300, every one carrying a substantive signal.

Being fixed in #176.
title: review-need report is 60% of the corpus because a norm-level signal alone qualifies a record

body:
## Surfaced by the review-need ranking

Two adjacent failure modes, both meaning the record carries no recipe at all:

```
362  records with zero ingredients
101  records whose only ingredient text is "See source for composition"
---
463  records (4.2% of 11,094 media) with no usable composition
```

The 101 are strikingly uniform — every one uses that exact string, so this is one import path, not scattered curation gaps.

## Why this was not visible before

`prioritize_deep_research_candidates.py` **hard-filters zero-ingredient records** before scoring, and rewards recipe completeness thereafter. That is correct for its purpose — ranking where deep research will pay off — but it means the damaged tail is invisible to the only ranking the repo had. These 463 records have never appeared at the top of anything.

`validate-strict` does not catch them either: `ingredients` is not required, so an empty list is schema-valid.

## Included in the 463

`bacterial/test_medium_123.yaml` — `original_name: "Test Medium 123"`, sole ingredient "See source for composition", holding `CultureMech:000306`. A test fixture that reached the production corpus and was assigned a real id.

## What to decide

Per group, and they may differ:

1. **Recoverable?** The `notes` on several say "Imported from BacDive cultivation data", so the source may still have the composition and a re-import could fill them.
2. **Or honestly empty?** If the source genuinely has no composition, the record should say so — a `data_quality_flags` entry — rather than carrying one fake ingredient that pollutes every text scan. The placeholder string already matches ingredient searches, which is how it turned up here.
3. **Or spurious?** `test_medium_123` should probably not exist. Deleting it means retiring a CultureMech id, which is a separate decision (cf. #144).

## Reproduce

```
just score-review-need --top 40
```

They occupy the 70-80 band. Ranking, signals and weights are in `scripts/score_review_need.py`.
title: 226 media have no usable composition (was 463, then 428 — 202 were mis-typed stock solutions)

body:
## Found reviewing #173

`resolve_media_file` globs `data/normalized_yaml/*/*.yaml` and calls `read_text()` on every file, for **every** resolution:

```
resolve("lb_broth")                        0.99s
resolve("CultureMech:009646")              0.73s
resolve("data/.../lb_broth.yaml")          0.00s   (path short-circuit)
```

Roughly **1 second per non-path target**, because each call re-reads ~15,900 files to do a substring pre-filter before parsing candidates.

## Why it matters now

#173 fixes the resolver so slug-driven batches work at all — 2,291 slugs previously raised. The immediate consumer is `research_media_edison.py --batch`, which calls `resolve_media_file` once per entry. So the fix that unblocks batches also makes their startup cost linear in *batch size × corpus size*:

```
100-target batch   ~100 s of pure resolution
500-target batch   ~8 minutes before the first API call
```

That is invisible next to Edison's per-record latency (minutes), so it is not urgent — but it is pure waste, and it will bite anything that resolves in a loop without an API call to hide behind.

It also made a review check impractical: comparing old and new resolver behaviour across 600 sampled targets exceeded a 10-minute timeout.

## Cheap fix

Build the index once and reuse it. A module-level cache keyed on the corpus mtime, or an explicit `build_index()` returning a `{identifier: path}` map that batch callers construct once and pass in. `research_media_edison.py --batch` and `research_organism_recipe_edison.py --batch` are the two call sites that would benefit most.

The tiered structure #173 introduces makes this straightforward: the tiers are just three dicts.

## Not a regression

The old resolver had the same cost; #173 neither improves nor worsens it. Filing separately because the fix is orthogonal to the correctness change and should not be bundled into it.
title: resolve_media_file is O(corpus) per call — a 100-target batch re-reads the corpus 100 times

body:
## Found reviewing #171

`--promote-semi-defined` promotes an UNDEFINED record only when *every other ingredient* carries a CHEBI id — positive evidence that the base is defined, rather than inferring it from "nothing else matched". Of 809 candidates, 612 clear that bar and **197 do not**.

Those 197 are the interesting ones. They have exactly one undefined component below 0.5 g/L — the SEMI_DEFINED shape — and are held back solely because a sibling ingredient is ungrounded. Either:

- the sibling is a defined chemical that simply needs grounding, in which case the record becomes promotable and this is a **grounding** task; or
- the sibling is an unrecognised extract, in which case the record is correctly UNDEFINED and the **word list** should learn the name.

Both outcomes are useful, and which applies is decidable per record by looking at the ingredient.

## The problem

They are recorded **nowhere**. `--promote-semi-defined` prints aggregate counts to stdout and exits:

```
Promoted 612 UNDEFINED record(s) -> SEMI_DEFINED.
Not promoted, by reason:
   5885  not exactly one undefined component
    358  1 g/L is not 'a small amount'
    ...
```

`composition_type_conflicts.tsv` covers only the DEFINED-with-undefined-components direction (46 rows). Nothing names the 197, so reproducing them means re-deriving the rule by hand.

That is the opposite of how the sibling audits behave — `concentration_plausibility.tsv` and `filename_collisions.tsv` both write a per-record row with a verdict column precisely so the actionable subset is addressable.

## Suggested fix

Have `--promote-semi-defined` write a per-record report with a verdict column, covering promoted records *and* near-misses with the reason. The near-miss rows should name the ungrounded ingredient(s), since that is the thing a curator acts on.

Being fixed in #171.
title: SEMI_DEFINED promotion leaves no record of the 197 near-misses it declined

body:
## Found reviewing #169

#169 adds a baseline gate for implausible concentrations and documents the baseline in a `project.justfile` comment:

```
# Baseline history (#150): 11,540 rows across 3,914 records at the time the gate
# was added ... LOWER the baseline as records are repaired
[group('QC')]
audit-concentration-plausibility *args="":
    uv run --extra dev python scripts/audit_concentration_plausibility.py {{args}}
```

**The recipe never passes `--max-allowed`.** Running `just audit-concentration-plausibility` reports and exits 0 regardless of the count. The comment reads as though the recipe gates; it does not.

Compare the convention it claims to follow, which hardcodes the baseline into the recipe:

```
check-chebi-grounding *args:
    uv run python scripts/audit_chebi_consistency.py \
        --out reports/chebi_consistency.tsv --max-allowed 101 {{args}}
```

## Where the gate actually lives

In `tests/test_concentration_plausibility.py`, as `CONCENTRATION_BACKLOG_BASELINE = 11_540`. That is a real gate — pytest runs on every PR with no path filter — so the protection exists. It is the *documentation* that is wrong, plus a missed layer: the recipe is also absent from any workflow, so there is no non-pytest path that enforces it.

## The trap in fixing it naively

Adding `--max-allowed 11540` to the recipe puts the number in **two** places that must be lowered together as the backlog is repaired. Miss one and either the gate stops biting (justfile stale-high) or local runs fail while CI passes (justfile stale-low). That is the same drift class as #144 and #157.

## Suggested fix

Wire the recipe *and* assert the two agree, so drift is impossible:

1. `--max-allowed <baseline>` in the recipe, matching `check-chebi-grounding`.
2. A test parsing the baseline out of `project.justfile` and asserting it equals `CONCENTRATION_BACKLOG_BASELINE`.

(2) is the part that matters. Without it, two hardcoded copies of a number that is *expected to change* is a drift bug waiting to happen — and this repo has now produced four of those.

Being fixed in #169.
title: The concentration baseline lives in two places and the justfile recipe doesn't enforce it

body:
## Same shape as #157, found while fixing it

`reports/chebi_consistency.tsv` (#157) was tracked, script-generated, and never checked — so it rotted 73/82 lines behind the corpus. Auditing its siblings turned up two more tracked reports with a script that writes them:

| file | writer |
|---|---|
| `reports/media_content_review_manifest.tsv` (+ `.json`) | `scripts/propose_media_variant_links.py` |
| `reports/media_growth_review_manifest.tsv` (+ `.json`) | `scripts/build_media_growth_review_html.py` |

Both are tracked. Neither has a freshness check. Neither was regenerated during the recategorizations in #115 / #120 / #137 / #143 or the composition-type restamp in #164, all of which changed records these manifests describe.

I have **not** verified whether they are actually stale — doing so means running each generator, which has side effects beyond the report (the variant-links script proposes links; the growth-review script builds HTML). That is why this is a separate issue rather than folded into #157.

## The classification question is the real one

#145 asks which derived artifacts must be refreshed. #157 established that there are at least three kinds, and the right remedy differs for each:

1. **Consumed artifacts** — indexes (#125), id registry (#144). Guard that they match the corpus; a correct committed copy has value because things resolve through them.
2. **Dated snapshots** — `reports/label_plausibility_2026-07-19.tsv`, `reports/archive/*`. Must **not** be refreshed; their old paths and counts are an accurate record of what ran.
3. **Regenerable diagnostics with no reader** — `chebi_consistency.tsv`. Should not be tracked at all; untracking removes the failure mode rather than policing it.

These two manifests need sorting into one of those buckets. `gap_fix_backlog.tsv` and `label_plausibility_after_fixes.tsv` have no writer in the repo at all, which probably makes them category 2 — but "no writer found" may just mean the generator was deleted, and that is worth confirming rather than assuming.

## Suggested first step

For each: identify whether anything reads it. That is the question that decided #157 — a diagnostic with no reader should not be tracked, while a consumed artifact should be guarded. `chebi_consistency.tsv` turned out to have zero readers across scripts, justfiles, workflows and docs.
title: Two more tracked reports are script-generated with no freshness check (#145, 5th/6th instance)

body:
## A whole recipe crammed into a single `preferred_term`

`data/normalized_yaml/.../NBRC_1197.yaml` has an ingredient whose name is:

```
Substrates*10mMKH2PO40.85gNa2HPO4·7H2O4.9g(NH4)2SO40.5gMgSO4·7H2O...
```

That is the source recipe's whole composition block — several ingredients, each with its own quantity and unit — concatenated into one field with the whitespace stripped. It is an import parse failure, not a real ingredient.

## Scope: this appears to be the only one

Scanning every non-solution record for a `preferred_term` longer than 40 characters containing two or more embedded quantity+unit pairs:

```python
MANGLED = re.compile(r"\d+\s*(g|mg|ml|l)\b.*\d+\s*(g|mg|ml|l)\b", re.I)
# -> 1 hit, corpus-wide
```

So this is a single bad record rather than a systemic pattern — cheap to fix by hand, and worth fixing precisely because it is isolated enough not to need tooling.

## Why it matters beyond one record

1. The record's real ingredients are **not represented** — they exist only inside this string, so the medium has no usable composition.
2. It pollutes text matching. It was found because the substring "Tryptone" inside it matched an undefined-component scan in #164; anything else grepping `preferred_term` will match it spuriously too.
3. It will not be caught by concentration or grounding audits, because the field it corrupts is the name.

## Suggested fix

Split it back into proper ingredient entries from the NBRC source, or — if the source is not readily available — replace it with a single honest placeholder and flag the record as having an unparsed composition, so downstream consumers see "unknown" rather than one nonsense ingredient.

A cheap guard would be a test asserting no `preferred_term` contains two or more embedded quantity+unit pairs. It would have caught this at import.

Found while auditing composition_type in #164.
title: One ingredient name is an entire unparsed recipe: 'Substrates*10mMKH2PO40.85gNa2HPO4·7H2O4.9g...'

body:
## Introduced by #164, and worth deciding deliberately

#164 restamps 239 records `composition_type: DEFINED -> UNDEFINED` because their ingredient lists contain chemically undefined components. Those records still carry the **deprecated** `medium_type: DEFINED`, so the two slots now disagree.

Measured on the corpus, excluding stock-solution records:

```
before #164   agree 11,092   disagree     0
after  #164   agree 10,853   disagree   239
```

Every disagreement is the same shape: `('DEFINED', 'UNDEFINED')`.

## This is a newly visible inconsistency, not a new error

`medium_type: DEFINED` was **already wrong** on these records — that is what #158 documents, and the #148 migration mapped it across faithfully. #164 corrects the live slot and leaves the deprecated one carrying the original error.

So no information is lost. But the corpus went from a 100% invariant to 239 violations, and "the two slots agree" is exactly the kind of thing someone would reasonably write a guard for.

## The real question: should `medium_type` still be in the corpus?

It is deprecated in the schema, and #154 removed `TaxonomyClassifier`, its last reader. Nothing in the pipeline branches on it now. Three options:

1. **Drop `medium_type` from all 11,092 records.** Cleanest — a deprecated slot with no readers and a known-wrong value on 239 records is a trap, not an asset. Largest diff.
2. **Keep the slots consistent.** Restamp `medium_type: DEFINED -> COMPLEX` on the 239, per the schema's own mapping (`UNDEFINED` "replaces the deprecated MediumTypeEnum value COMPLEX"). Restores the invariant, but writes to a deprecated slot and so implies it is maintained.
3. **Leave the disagreement**, documented, on the grounds that a deprecated slot has no claim on correctness.

#164 takes option 2 as the conservative in-PR choice — it leaves no contradiction behind and is mechanical. Option 1 is probably right long-term and is what this issue tracks.

Whichever is chosen, a guard asserting the two slots agree (or that `medium_type` is absent) would keep it settled.
title: Restamping composition_type leaves the deprecated medium_type contradicting it on 239 records

body:
## Problem

`.claude/skills/review-recipes/SKILL.md` links to three sibling skills by their **old** filename:

```
../create-recipe/skill.md
../manage-identifiers/skill.md
../manage-ingredient-hierarchy/skill.md
```

Those files are now `SKILL.md`. On macOS (`core.ignorecase=true`) the links resolve; on Linux they 404.

Being fixed directly in #160 — the point of this issue is that **nothing would have caught it**, and it is the second instance of the same class in as many commits.

## Why it slipped

#160's rename commit deliberately fixed the `../skill.md` links in `review-recipes/reference/`, reasoning that a bare `git mv` would break them. It did exactly that — and missed the three in the parent `SKILL.md`, because both the old and new paths open fine on the machine doing the work.

That is the same root cause as the rename itself: a case-only difference is invisible on a case-insensitive filesystem, so neither the author nor a local test can see it. The only reliable detector is a case-sensitive check, which has to be written deliberately.

## Reproduce

```python
import re, pathlib
root = pathlib.Path(".claude/skills")
for md in root.rglob("*.md"):
    for m in re.finditer(r"\]\(([^)]+\.md)\)", md.read_text(errors="replace")):
        t = m.group(1)
        if t.startswith(("http", "#")):
            continue
        r = (md.parent / t).resolve()
        # membership in the parent listing, NOT r.exists() — exists() lies on macOS
        if not r.parent.is_dir() or r.name not in {p.name for p in r.parent.iterdir()}:
            print(md, "->", t)
```

Note `r.exists()` is useless here: it returns `True` on macOS for a wrong-case path. The check has to compare against an actual directory listing.

## Suggested fix

A test asserting every relative Markdown link in the repo resolves **case-sensitively**. It is cheap, it rides the existing pytest gate, and it covers `docs/`, `.claude/skills/` and any README — all of which can rot the same way whenever a file is renamed.

Scope worth deciding: `docs/archive/` is a historical record and its links arguably should not be enforced, the same call #160 made when it left that directory alone.
title: Nothing checks intra-repo Markdown links for case, so Linux-only breakage stays invisible on macOS

body:
## 284 records assert `composition_type: DEFINED` while listing chemically undefined ingredients

`MediumCompositionTypeEnum.DEFINED` means "every component and its exact quantity
is known". 11.5% of the records carrying it contradict that in their own
ingredient list.

Scanning `preferred_term` on every ingredient for undefined components (yeast
extract, peptone, tryptone, casamino acids, beef/meat/malt extract, proteose,
brain-heart infusion, casein hydrolysate, soytone, blood, serum, rumen fluid,
liver extract, tryptic soy):

```
DEFINED   : 2480
  containing an undefined component : 284  (11.5%)
UNDEFINED : 8612
  exactly one undefined component   : 3116
  two or more                       : 3716
  none recognized                   : 1780
```

Examples, none of them borderline:

```
medium_465_modified_for_dsm_10063.yaml       -> casamino, meat extract, peptone, proteose, yeast extract  (35 ingredients)
for_dsm_13514.yaml                           -> peptone, yeast extract       (17 ingredients)
medium_457_modified_for_dsm_11565.yaml       -> meat extract, peptone        (28 ingredients)
MEDIADB_460_Defined_freshwater_medium_CoCl2.yaml -> tryptone, yeast extract  (31 ingredients)
```

The `medium_457_modified_for_dsm_*` family is a large cluster of near-identical
records that all carry the same contradiction, so the 284 are concentrated
rather than uniformly scattered — a modest number of source recipes probably
accounts for most of them.

## Not introduced by #148

The migration mapped `medium_type: DEFINED` → `composition_type: DEFINED`
faithfully and never invented a value. The error was already present in
`medium_type`; #148 restated it on a slot whose description is explicit about
what DEFINED means, which is what makes it detectable now. Note
`MEDIADB_460_Defined_freshwater_medium_CoCl2` has "Defined" in its *source
name*, so at least some of these came in mislabeled from upstream.

## Suggested handling

Most of these are probably `SEMI_DEFINED` rather than `UNDEFINED` — a defined
base plus a named undefined supplement is exactly that case, and `SEMI_DEFINED`
is currently emitted on zero records (#152).

Worth doing as a detector plus a review pass rather than a blind flip, since the
keyword list above will have both false positives (an ingredient named "peptone
water" used as a diluent) and false negatives (undefined components not on the
list). The detector belongs next to the implausible-concentration checks from
#118/#135.

Found while reviewing #148. Companion to #152, which covers the axes that ship
empty; this one covers a value that ships wrong.
title: 284 DEFINED records (11.5%) list chemically undefined ingredients

body:
## `reports/chebi_consistency.tsv` is tracked, regenerated by a CI gate, and stale

Running `just check-chebi-grounding` on a checkout of current `main` rewrites the
tracked report:

```
reports/chebi_consistency.tsv | 155 ++++++++--------
1 file changed, 73 insertions(+), 82 deletions(-)
```

The diff is not cosmetic — it is drift in the underlying corpus:

```
-A_name_multi_chebi  na2moo4 x 2 h2o  {'CHEBI:75213': 3196, 'CHEBI:75215': 137}
+A_name_multi_chebi  na2moo4 x 2 h2o  {'CHEBI:75213': 3224, 'CHEBI:75215': 143}
-A_name_multi_chebi  nano3            {'CHEBI:63005': 334, 'CHEBI:59148': 245}
+A_name_multi_chebi  coso4 x 7 h2o    {'CHEBI:53470': 766, 'CHEBI:91244': 5}
```

Counts have moved and whole rows have appeared and disappeared, so the committed
file describes a corpus that no longer exists. Reproduced on `main`, independent
of #148 — the axis backfill adds a `composition_type` line and cannot affect
CHEBI grounding counts.

## Why it does not fail CI

`chebi-consistency.yaml` runs `just check-chebi-grounding`, which gates on a
`--max-allowed` threshold for the *current* corpus. It never compares its output
to the committed TSV, so the file can rot indefinitely while the job stays green.
Anyone reading `reports/chebi_consistency.tsv` in the repo — rather than
re-running the gate — gets stale numbers.

## The fourth instance of #145

Same shape as the recipe indexes (#125), the id registry (#144) and the
generated dataclasses (#149): a derived artifact with no drift guard. Three of
those four are now closed; this is the remaining one.

## Fix

Either stop tracking it (it is reproducible from the corpus in one command), or
regenerate it in the gate and fail when it differs from the committed copy — the
pattern `tests/test_recipe_indexes.py` and `tests/test_id_registry.py` already
use. Tracking it *and* not checking it is the combination that produces silent
rot.

Found while reviewing #148; deliberately not fixed there, since regenerating it
would have put unrelated corpus drift into that PR's diff.
title: reports/chebi_consistency.tsv is tracked but never checked, and is stale on main (#145, 4th instance)

body:
## 12 recipes in `justfile` pin an absolute Homebrew interpreter

#155 fixed the one recipe #148 introduced. Reviewing it turned up 12 more that
predate that branch:

```
$ grep -c '/opt/homebrew' justfile project.justfile
justfile:12
project.justfile:0
```

Among them `render-media-pages`, `propose-growth-evidence`,
`fetch-pubmed-abstracts`, `apply-growth-evidence`,
`validate-evidence-references`, `enrich-genome-ids`,
`build-media-content-review-manifest`, `propose-media-variant-links` and
`validate-media-variant-links`.

The split is clean and looks accidental rather than deliberate: **every**
occurrence is in `justfile`, and **none** is in `project.justfile`, which uses
`uv run` throughout. `justfile` is not a personal or gitignored file — it is the
tracked main entry point that does `import 'project.justfile'`, so these recipes
are as public as any other.

## Consequences

1. **They run only on a machine with that exact Homebrew Python.** Anywhere else
   — CI, a Linux checkout, a collaborator's laptop, a Homebrew install that has
   moved to 3.14 — they fail with "no such file or directory".
2. **They bypass the project environment even here.** The venv is `python3.14`;
   these invoke 3.13 with none of the project dependencies importable. They work
   today only for scripts that happen to be stdlib-only, which is a property
   nobody is enforcing and any new import would break.

CI is unaffected today because the workflows call `just validate-strict`,
`just test` and `just check-chebi-grounding`, all of which live in
`project.justfile`.

## Fix

Mechanical: `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.13` → `uv run python`, 12 occurrences.
Worth doing in one pass and then checking each recipe still runs, since a few
(`gen-media-pages`, `propose-growth-evidence`) set `PYTHONPATH` to a sibling
repo and may have been deliberately kept outside `uv` for that reason — those
should be confirmed individually rather than swapped blind.

Found while reviewing #148; not fixed there to keep that PR scoped.
title: 12 more justfile recipes hardcode /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.13 (follow-up to #155)

body:
The recipe added in #148 pins an absolute, machine-specific interpreter:

```make
validate-media-recipe target *args:
    /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.13 scripts/render_media_prompt.py --target {{target}} {{args}}
```

Every other recipe in `justfile` and `project.justfile` goes through `uv run`. This one does not, with two consequences:

1. **It only runs on this laptop.** `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.13` is a Homebrew symlink. On CI (`ubuntu-latest`) or any machine without that exact Homebrew Python, the recipe fails with "no such file or directory".
2. **It runs outside the project environment even here.** The project venv is `python3.14`; this invokes 3.13 with none of the project dependencies on its path. It happens to work today only because `render_media_prompt.py` imports nothing beyond `argparse`, `sys`, `pathlib`, and a sibling script.

Verified: `uv run python scripts/render_media_prompt.py --target 1_10_r2a_medium` renders the prompt correctly, so nothing about the script needs the pinned interpreter.

## Fix

```make
validate-media-recipe target *args:
    uv run python scripts/render_media_prompt.py --target {{target}} {{args}}
```

Found while reviewing #148.
title: justfile: validate-media-recipe hardcodes /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.13

body:
## `TaxonomyClassifier.classify_functional_domain` reads a slot that is now deprecated, using values that never existed

`src/culturemech/taxonomy/classifier.py:90-103` branches on `medium_type`:

```python
medium_type = recipe.get('medium_type', '')
if medium_type == 'MINIMAL':      return 'MINIMAL'
elif medium_type == 'COMPLEX':    return 'COMPLEX'
elif medium_type == 'SELECTIVE':  return 'SELECTIVE'
elif medium_type == 'DIFFERENTIAL': return 'DIFFERENTIAL'
elif medium_type == 'ENRICHMENT': return 'ENRICHMENT'
```

Two problems, one pre-existing and one introduced by #148.

**Four of those five branches are unreachable and always were.** The corpus has
only ever held two `medium_type` values:

```
8612 COMPLEX
2480 DEFINED
   1 NEGATIVE_CONTROL
   1 BUFFER
```

`MINIMAL`, `SELECTIVE`, `DIFFERENTIAL` and `ENRICHMENT` appear on zero records,
so only the `COMPLEX` branch has ever fired. Records fall through to the
`applications` keyword heuristics below instead.

**And the slot is now deprecated.** After #148 the live signal is
`composition_type` / `nutritional_class` / `functional_role`. This function
still reads the old slot, so it will not see anything a curator sets on the new
axes.

## Severity is low

`classifier.py` sits at **7% coverage** and `classify_functional_domain` has no
call site outside the module — `taxonomy/__init__.py` exports the class but
nothing in the pipeline, scripts, or tests invokes it. So this is stale code
rather than a live wrong answer.

Worth either rewriting against the three axes or deleting, but it should be a
deliberate decision rather than a drive-by change inside #148.
title: TaxonomyClassifier branches on deprecated medium_type values that appear on zero records

body:
## Two related gaps in `scripts/migrate_medium_type_axes.py`

This script rewrote 11,088 corpus records in #148. It has **no tests**, and the
dependency that makes it safe is not declared.

### 1. No test coverage

```
$ grep -rln 'migrate_medium_type_axes' tests/
(no output)
```

For contrast, `research_media.py` — which writes nothing — has three test files.
The script that edited a third of the corpus has none.

Untested behaviors that matter: the idempotency guarantee (write an axis slot
only when absent, never touch `medium_type`), the slot insertion position, the
deliberate non-mapping of `BUFFER`/`NEGATIVE_CONTROL`, and dry-run actually not
writing.

### 2. `ruamel.yaml` is undeclared, and the fallback reflows

```python
try:
    from ruamel.yaml import YAML as RuamelYAML
except ImportError:
    RuamelYAML = None
...
ROUND_TRIP_YAML.dump(...) if ROUND_TRIP_YAML else pyyaml.safe_dump(data, sort_keys=False, ...)
```

`ruamel` is not in `pyproject.toml` — it is present only transitively (0.19.1,
via linkml). If that transitive edge ever drops, the `except ImportError` branch
silently engages and every written record goes through `pyyaml.safe_dump`.

Measured on a real record (`bacterial/r2a_medium.yaml`, 164 lines): the ruamel
path produces a **1-line** diff; the pyyaml path produces a **37-line** diff —
it reflows the record and would strip comments. Across 11,088 records that is
exactly the failure #141 describes, except silent, because the fallback is a
bare `except ImportError` with no warning.

### What actually shipped was fine

Verified, so this is a latent risk rather than damage already done:

```
$ git show --numstat 7a2ff6f362 -- data/normalized_yaml
insertions-per-file: +1 on 11,081 files
deletions-per-file:  -0 on 11,081 files
```

Exactly one added line per record, zero deletions. The ruamel path was taken and
nothing was reflowed. **This backfill is not an instance of #141.**

### Fix

- Declare `ruamel.yaml` in `pyproject.toml` rather than relying on linkml to
  keep pulling it in.
- Make the fallback loud — if round-tripping is unavailable, refuse to write
  rather than silently reflowing the corpus.
- Add tests for the four behaviors above.
title: migrate_medium_type_axes.py: no tests, and an undeclared ruamel dep whose fallback silently reflows records

body:
## What ships in #148

#148 replaces the single-valued `medium_type` with three orthogonal axes. Only
one of them actually has data.

Post-merge counts across the 15,878-record corpus:

| axis | records populated |
|---|---|
| `composition_type` | 11,092 |
| `nutritional_class` | **1** |
| `functional_role` | **1** |

The one record in each case is `data/normalized_yaml/bacterial/r2a_medium.yaml`,
set by hand in the R2A curation commits — not by the migration.

## Why

The migration can only derive axes from `medium_type`, and the corpus never used
the values that feed the other two axes:

```
8612 COMPLEX
2480 DEFINED
   1 NEGATIVE_CONTROL
   1 BUFFER
```

`MINIMAL`, `SELECTIVE`, `DIFFERENTIAL` and `ENRICHMENT` are permissible values of
`MediumTypeEnum` but appear on **zero** records. So the migration's mappings for
them — MINIMAL→`nutritional_class`, and the three functional values→
`functional_role` — never fired even once. This is not a bug in the migration;
there was simply nothing to convert.

## Why it matters

The schema now advertises three axes and a KGX consumer can filter on any of
them, but two return an empty set. `SEMI_DEFINED` is likewise a permissible
`composition_type` value that nothing emits — every undefined-component medium
is flatly `UNDEFINED`, including media that are a defined base plus a trace of
yeast extract.

The gap is worth stating explicitly because the corpus *looks* fully migrated:
11,092 of 11,094 typed records carry an axis value, so a coverage check on
`composition_type` alone reads as complete.

## What would close it

These need signal the old slot never had, so they are curation work, not another
mechanical pass:

- `nutritional_class` — inferable in bulk for well-known media (M9 and the
  defined-minimal family → MINIMAL; LB/TSB/BHI → RICH). Most of the rest are
  plausibly GENERAL_PURPOSE but that should not be assumed by default.
- `functional_role` — needs the recipe or the source catalogue (presence of
  antibiotics, dyes, bile salts, or a differential indicator).
- `SEMI_DEFINED` — separable from UNDEFINED by ingredient analysis: a
  predominantly defined ingredient list with exactly one small undefined
  component.

Filed from the review of #148. Not a blocker for that PR — the schema and the
composition backfill are correct as far as they go.
title: nutritional_class and functional_role ship populated on 1 record each; SEMI_DEFINED on none

body:
Splitting the unfinished half of #116 into its own issue.

#116 asked for per-pair reconciliation of media sharing a filename across category directories. **#134 shipped a deliberately read-only triage** and says so explicitly ("This does not close #116"). #137 then did the bacterial-half curation and commented to the same effect. #116 was closed on 2026-07-26 anyway. This issue tracks the curation that remains.

## What is already resolved

- **The 11 named `methano*` collisions** — #120 moved all 11 to `archaea/` only, pinned by a test so they cannot come back.
- **The bacterial half** — #137 moved 27 recipes from `archaea/` to `bacterial/` (*Thermus*, *Pseudomonas*, *Treponema*, *Spirochaeta*, …), taking `archaea/` from 773 to 746.

## What #134 actually found — bigger than #116 describes

**290 filenames appear in two or more category directories**, not the ~50 the issue implies. Re-counted from the committed `data/import_tracking/reports/filename_collisions.tsv` on 2026-07-30:

| classification | pairs | meaning |
|---|--:|---|
| `DIFFERENT` | 223 | compositions genuinely diverge |
| `IDENTICAL` | 56 | verbatim same labels, groundings, concentrations, units |
| `EQUIVALENT` | 11 | same medium, differing only in ingestion artefacts |

## Two things to know before picking this up

**Even the 56 IDENTICAL pairs are not safe to auto-dedupe.** Choosing which copy survives means choosing which category is correct — a domain judgment, the same one #115/#120/#137 kept getting wrong in bulk — and deduping means deleting a CultureMech id. This needs per-pair curation, not a script.

**118 of the 223 DIFFERENT pairs share no ingredient rows at all.** Those are unrelated media that merely collide on filename; they need disambiguation (rename one side), not reconciliation. Only 3 pairs overlap at 90% or more. So the 223 splits into a large trivial-rename group and a small genuinely-hard group, and separating them is cheap.

## Why the EQUIVALENT tier exists

A tuple comparison is too blunt. `1_10_sabourauds_agar.yaml` has identical concentrations throughout, yet `bacterial/` grounds Glucose to `CHEBI:42758` while `fungal/` grounds it to `CHEBI:17234`; labels differ (`MgSO4・7H2O` vs `MgSO4 x 7 H2O`); and the `bacterial/` copy carries an extra implausible `Distilled water 1 G_PER_L` row (see the #118 follow-up). Reconciling these means resolving a grounding disagreement, not just picking a file.

## Also worth carrying forward

#137's reverse audit of `archaea/` found the original 71-file import had never been domain-vetted at all — 29 genuinely archaeal, 26 genuinely bacterial, 16 ambiguous. That argues for keeping a permanent domain check rather than sweeping once, which is the same conclusion #145 reaches from a different direction.

## Remaining work

1. Split the 223 `DIFFERENT` pairs into the 118 no-overlap renames and the rest.
2. Curate the 56 `IDENTICAL` and 11 `EQUIVALENT` pairs per pair, deciding category and surviving id.
3. Disambiguate the resolver's multi-match behaviour (it hit `syntrophomonas_medium_for_syntrophospora_cellicola_19j_3`, which has a `TOGO_M520_*` sibling of the same recipe).
title: Per-pair curation of the 290 cross-category filename collisions (unfinished half of #116)

body:
Splitting the unfinished half of #118 into its own issue.

#118 asked for two things: an audit to find where stock-solution concentrations and unit slips were stored as final per-litre values, and the corpus repair. **#135 shipped the audit only** — its merge commit says so outright:

> `Does NOT close #118; the corpus repair remains.`

#118 was nonetheless closed on 2026-07-26. The corpus is still wrong; what changed is that we now know exactly where. This issue tracks the repair.

## What the audit found

Three read-only detectors, output in `data/import_tracking/reports/concentration_plausibility.tsv` and `…_by_record.tsv`. Re-counted from the committed reports on 2026-07-30:

| detector | rows | signal |
|---|--:|---|
| `INDICATOR_UNIT_SLIP` | 5,601 | indicators/vitamins ≥ 0.1 G_PER_L — a ~1000x slip |
| `TRACE_SALT_AS_STOCK` | 5,341 | trace-element salts ≥ 1 G_PER_L — stock-solution magnitude |
| `WATER_AS_VOLUME` | 598 | water ≥ 1000 G_PER_L — a prep volume flattened into the ingredient list |

**11,540 rows across 3,914 records.** All three records named in #118 are detected and pinned by a regression test.

## The actionable subset

**579 records are flagged `flattened_cocktail`** — three or more flagged vitamin/trace rows *and* no `solutions:` block. For these the repair is structural ("nest this cocktail under a solution object with an addition volume") rather than per-value, which makes them both higher-value and more mechanical than the rest. The remaining 3,335 flagged records are not cocktails and need per-value judgment.

`DSMZ_962a_THERMOVENABULUM_MEDIUM` is the worked example: the entire DSMZ vitamin solution flattened into `ingredients:` at stock strength.

## Scope limits — read before trusting the counts

- **Only `G_PER_L` rows are examined** (149,289 of 166,684). `MILLIMOLAR`, `MG_PER_L` and `VARIABLE` are untouched. A molar-basis check needs molecular weights and is separate work.
- **Detectors key on confirmed failure modes, not outlier statistics**, so bulk-nutrient errors are missed. `MARICAULIS_medium` carries `Peptone 100 G_PER_L` and `Yeast extract 50 G_PER_L`, both implausible, neither flagged.
- **Stock-solution records are excluded** via `record_kinds.is_solution_record` (from #124), where high magnitudes are correct by definition. Without that exclusion this would flag thousands of the ~4,784 solution records sitting in `bacterial/`.

So 11,540 is a floor on the real defect count, not a total.

## Remaining work

1. Nest the 579 detected cocktails under stock `solution` objects with addition volumes.
2. Work the non-cocktail flagged records per value.
3. Add a plausibility validator to the schema-gap / label-plausibility harness so new imports cannot reintroduce this — the audit is currently read-only and nothing stops a fresh import landing the same shape.

Item 3 is arguably the highest-leverage: without it the corpus repair is a one-off sweep that decays.
title: Corpus repair for the implausible-concentration audit (unfinished half of #118)

body:
## Symptom

`src/culturemech/schema/culturemech_dataclasses.py` is generated from
`culturemech.yaml` by `pythongen`, but nothing regenerates it and nothing guards
it. On #148 the schema gained three slots and three enums; the dataclasses know
about none of them.

Reproduced on the #148 branch against a real backfilled record:

```python
from culturemech.schema.culturemech_dataclasses import MediaRecipe
d = yaml.safe_load(open('data/normalized_yaml/bacterial/r2a_medium.yaml'))
MediaRecipe(**d)
# TypeError: MediaRecipe.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'composition_type'
```

That is not one record. Every one of the 11,088 backfilled records now fails to
load through the dataclass API.

## Why it went unnoticed

`linkml-validate` reads the **schema**, so `just validate-strict` passes on all
15,878 files. The dataclasses are a *separate* generated artifact that only
`tests/test_source_environment.py` and `tests/test_media_variant_links.py`
import, and neither constructs a `MediaRecipe` from a corpus record — so 520
tests pass while the API is broken.

The generation header reads `Generation date: 2026-07-20`, i.e. it tracks
whichever schema happened to be on `main` at the last manual regeneration.

## This is the #145 pattern again

Same shape as the id registry (#144/#147) and the recipe indexes (#125/#133): a
derived artifact with no regeneration recipe and no drift guard, silently
diverging from its source. #147 closed that gap for the registry. The
dataclasses are the same class of problem and are still open.

## Fix

1. Regenerate: `uv run gen-python src/culturemech/schema/culturemech.yaml`
   (verified — produces a focused 152-line diff, and the regenerated
   `MediaRecipe` accepts the record above, yielding `composition_type=UNDEFINED`).
2. Add a `just gen-dataclasses` recipe so it is reproducible rather than folklore.
3. Add a drift guard — regenerate to a temp file and assert it matches the
   tracked file modulo the `Generation date:` header — so a schema edit that
   forgets step 1 fails CI instead of shipping.
title: Generated dataclasses drift silently from the schema — every backfilled record fails to load

body:
## Summary

`validate-media-recipes` is a **local-only branch, never pushed**, last touched 2026-06-29. It carries six commits of real work that is not on `main` by any route:

```
7a2ff6f  Backfill composition_type across corpus (11,088 records)
87af185  Standardize media-type vocabulary as orthogonal axes
cdca81c  Root R2A family: parent R3 A under canonical R2A
6e5ee61  Curate Half Strength R2A: re-parent to R2A, document pyruvate exception
f7c171c  Curate R2A variant family: re-parent 1/10 R2A, fix fold-change + labels
6af6583  Add media recipe-validation deep-research flow (native + Edison)
```

Confirmed unmerged, not merged-by-another-route: `composition_type` appears **nowhere** in `main`'s schema or corpus.

Beyond the corpus it touches `src/culturemech/schema/culturemech.yaml` (+113/−9), `scripts/migrate_medium_type_axes.py`, `scripts/render_media_prompt.py`, `scripts/research_media.py`, `templates/media_recipe_validation.md` and the `deep-research-medium` skill.

## Why it can't simply be PR'd as-is

A month of `main` has landed since its merge-base (#105–#143). A direct merge reports **~1,504 conflicting paths**, almost all of them in the 11,088 backfilled records — which have since been touched by the archaeal recategorizations (#115/#120/#137/#143), the solution-record work (#124) and the id↔label passes.

## Suggested approach

Do **not** merge the 11,088 record edits. They are *derived* output — `migrate_medium_type_axes.py` produced them. Instead:

1. PR the **source** changes alone: schema, migration script, templates, skill. Small and reviewable.
2. Re-run the migration against current `main` to regenerate the backfill, so it reflects today's corpus rather than June's.
3. Land the three R2A curation commits separately — they are hand-curation, not derived, and are the part a rebase would genuinely lose.

That converts a 1,504-conflict merge into a small review plus a deterministic regeneration.

## Note

This branch has never been pushed, so it exists only on one machine and is one `git branch -D` away from being lost. Filing this so the work is at least recorded. It was not touched, pushed, or deleted while surveying branches — whether to revive it is the author's call.

Found while auditing branches for unmerged work.
title: Unpushed branch validate-media-recipes holds an unmerged schema axis + 11,088-record backfill

body:
## Problem

A category move (`git mv` + restamp `category:`) leaves a record's *old* path embedded in several tracked artifacts. There is no single step that refreshes them, and no guard on most of them.

Observed after #143 moved three records:

| artifact | tracked | guarded | refreshed by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data/normalized_yaml/*_index.json` | yes | **yes** — `tests/test_recipe_indexes.py` (#125) | `just generate-indexes` |
| `data/culturemech_id_registry.tsv` | yes | no | `scripts/assign_culturemech_ids.py` (see #144) |
| `data/import_tracking/reports/deep_research_priority*.json` | yes | no | `just prioritize-deep-research-candidates` |
| `reports/*.tsv`, `reports/*.json` | yes | no | various one-off scripts |

Only the first fails loudly. #143's index staleness was caught by its test within seconds; the registry and priority-report staleness were found only because the author went looking.

## The `reports/` case is different

Files like `reports/label_plausibility_2026-07-19.tsv` are **dated snapshots**. Their stale paths are arguably correct — they record what was true when they ran. Rewriting them would falsify history. So the fix is not "regenerate everything"; it is deciding, per artifact, whether it is a *current view* (must refresh) or a *snapshot* (must not).

That distinction is not currently expressed anywhere, which is why it is easy to get wrong in either direction.

## Suggested fix

1. Classify each tracked derived artifact as current-view or snapshot, and record it — a short table in `docs/DATA_LAYERS.md` would do.
2. For current-view artifacts, add freshness guards modelled on `tests/test_recipe_indexes.py`. That test has already proved it works.
3. Consider a `just refresh-derived` recipe that regenerates exactly the current-view set, so a bulk move has one obvious follow-up step instead of a checklist held in someone's head.

Found while reviewing #143.
title: Moving a record silently invalidates several tracked derived artifacts; only indexes are guarded

body:
## Problem

`data/culturemech_id_registry.tsv` maps every CultureMech id to its file path. It is tracked, and **5,511 of its rows point at files that do not exist**:

```
CultureMech:000243  data/normalized_yaml/archaea/thioalkalivibrio_halophilus_medium.yaml
CultureMech:000244  data/normalized_yaml/archaea/thiohalophilus_medium.yaml
CultureMech:000245  data/normalized_yaml/archaea/thiohalospira_halophila_medium.yaml
CultureMech:000248  data/normalized_yaml/archaea/halophilic_methanotrophic_bacterium_medium.yaml
...
```

Reproduce:

```python
from pathlib import Path
bad = [l for i, l in enumerate(Path("data/culturemech_id_registry.tsv").read_text().splitlines())
       if i and l.strip() and not Path(l.partition("\t")[2]).is_file()]
len(bad)  # 5511
```

## Cause

Bulk category moves. #115 moved 629 records, #120 another 73, #137 more, and #143 three — every one of those changed a file's path, and none updated the registry. The rows are not wrong about the *id*, only about where the record now lives.

## Impact

Anything resolving an id through the registry rather than by scanning the corpus gets a path that does not open. This is the same class of defect as #125 (stale indexes) but on a different artifact — and unlike the indexes, nothing guards it.

## Suggested fix

1. Refresh the registry from the corpus. `scripts/assign_culturemech_ids.py` writes it, but it also *assigns* ids, so it needs checking that a refresh mode exists which only rewrites paths and never mints or renumbers.
2. Add a guard alongside `tests/test_recipe_indexes.py` asserting every registry row resolves to an existing file. That test caught #143's index staleness immediately; the equivalent here would have caught all of the above.
3. Consider whether path belongs in the registry at all. The id is stable, the path is not — a registry keyed on id that stores a *category* rather than a full path would not rot on every move.

## Note

#143 contributed 3 of these and fixed its own 3, leaving 5,511 that predate it. Fixing the rest is a corpus-wide job rather than something to bundle into a domain-audit PR.
title: culturemech_id_registry.tsv has 5,511 stale rows — id→path lookups resolve to files that no longer exist

body:
## Problem

`organism_culture_type` is declared `recommended: true` on `MediaRecipe` and distinguishes a pure-isolate medium from one targeting a mixed community. It is unset almost everywhere it would apply:

```
media records                              : 11,094
  with target_organisms                    :     50
  ...of those missing organism_culture_type:     40  (80%)
```

Only 10 of the 50 records that name a target organism say whether the medium is for an isolate or a community.

## Impact

- `kgx_export.py` reads it to model the organism↔medium relationship; without it, community media and isolate media export identically.
- It is one of the few slots that captures *how* a medium is used rather than what is in it, so the gap is not recoverable from composition.
- Being `recommended:` rather than `required:`, nothing flags the omission — `validate-strict` passes.

## Notes

This is a pre-existing corpus gap, not a regression. It surfaced while reviewing #140, which adds an organism to `CultureMech:008911`; the sibling record `CultureMech:008908` has two organisms and also leaves the slot unset, so setting it on one record alone would only add inconsistency.

## Suggested approach

For most of these the answer is inferable with reasonable confidence — a record naming one strain from a culture collection is an isolate medium. A pass over the 40 could set `isolate` where a single strain is named and leave genuinely ambiguous cases for a curator, rather than guessing across the board.

Worth deciding at the same time whether the slot should become `required:` for records that carry `target_organisms`, so this cannot silently recur.
title: organism_culture_type is unset on 80% of records that have target_organisms

body:
## Problem

Writing a record back with `yaml.dump(..., width=120)` re-wraps **every** long string in the file, not just the fields being changed. The result is a diff dominated by formatting churn.

Concrete case — PR #140 added one organism and one curation event to `archaea/sulfolobus_medium_for_dsm_9790.yaml`:

```
47 added lines
 └─ 24  pure re-wrapping of untouched `notes:` fields
 └─ 23  the actual curation
```

Roughly half the diff is noise. Verified semantically lossless (parsed base and head compare equal once the intended additions are removed), so this is a reviewability problem, not data loss — but it makes a reviewer's job harder exactly where care matters most, and it will scale badly on a bulk apply.

## Cause

The corpus was written with a narrower wrap than the `width=120` several scripts now pass. Any script that round-trips a record therefore reflows it. `scripts/apply_edison_results.py`, `scripts/apply_ingredient_roles.py` and ad-hoc curation snippets all use the same `yaml.dump(..., default_flow_style=False, sort_keys=False, allow_unicode=True, width=120)` idiom.

## Suggested fix

Settle on one wrap width and apply it consistently — either match whatever the corpus was generated with, or normalize the corpus once in a dedicated formatting-only PR and pin the width in a shared helper that all writers call.

A shared `write_record(path, doc)` helper is probably the right shape: it also gives one place to enforce `sort_keys=False` and `allow_unicode=True`, which are currently re-specified at every call site and could drift.

Found while reviewing #140.
title: Curation scripts reflow whole records, burying the actual change in whitespace noise

body:
Residue of the #114 / #116 / #120 / #137 domain work. Everything here is a **judgment call**, which is why the audit deliberately refuses to move it.

## Background

Auditing `archaea/` in both directions showed the original 71-file import (`CultureMech:0002xx-3xx`, DSMZ/JCM) was never domain-vetted: **29 archaeal, 26 bacterial, 16 with no taxonomic evidence at all**. #120 and #137 moved everything decidable by name. This is what's left.

## 15 records in `archaea/` naming no taxon (unsubstantiated)

Their names carry only a *physiology*, and halophiles/thermophiles span both domains — so filing them under `archaea/` is a claim with nothing behind it. They may well be archaeal; nothing in the record says so.

```
DSMZ_1399_HALOPHILIC_MEDIUM.yaml            HALOPHILIC MEDIUM
JCM_J1334_NATRONOARCHAEA_MEDIUM_II.yaml     NATRONOARCHAEA MEDIUM II
JCM_J464_HP_101_HALOPHILE_MEDIUM.yaml       HP 101 HALOPHILE MEDIUM
acido_thermophile_medium.yaml               ACIDO-THERMOPHILE MEDIUM
alkalophilic_halophile_medium.yaml          ALKALOPHILIC HALOPHILE MEDIUM
artificial_seawater_for_halophiles.yaml     ARTIFICIAL SEAWATER FOR HALOPHILES
halophile_medium.yaml                       HALOPHILE MEDIUM
halophile_starch_casein_medium.yaml         HALOPHILE STARCH-CASEIN MEDIUM
halophilic_medium.yaml                      HALOPHILIC MEDIUM
halophilic_sob_medium.yaml                  HALOPHILIC SOB MEDIUM
hp_101_halophile_medium.yaml                HP 101 HALOPHILE MEDIUM
medium_for_aciduric_thermophilic_bacillus_strains.yaml
moderate_halophile_medium.yaml              MODERATE HALOPHILE MEDIUM
moderate_halophile_medium_2.yaml            MODERATE HALOPHILE MEDIUM 2
thermanaerobacter_thermophila_medium.yaml   THERMANAEROBACTER THERMOPHILA MEDIUM
```
